research_opportunities: 4-year categorical block schedule fully published. PGY-1: 4 months neurology + ICU/CCU/IM/EM. PGY-2: 4 inpatient, 4 neuro-ICU/stroke, 2 clinic, 1 neuroradiology, 1 psychiatry. PGY-3: 3 inpatient, 2 epilepsy/EMU, 2 clinic, 2 neuromuscular/EMG, 3 child neurology (at Amarillo, UT Health San Antonio or Baylor College of Medicine Houston). PGY-4: 5 inpatient, 3 clinic, 1 epilepsy/EMU, 3 electives (sleep, neuro-ophthalmology, pain, neurointervention, research, away). Hospitalist and clinician-educator tracks. Research optional

salary_benefits.summary: Program page (self-contradictory on year) PGY-1 $61,114.36 / PGY-2 $63,109.69 / PGY-3 $65,099.91 / PGY-4 $67,092.82. FREIDA 2026: $62,642 / $64,687 / $66,727 / $68,770. Vacation 15/15/20/20 days + 12 sick days PGY-2 onward. Most insurance fully paid by institution. Moonlighting allowed. 15 paid / 90 unpaid family-medical-leave days

differentiators.title: NAEC Level 4 epilepsy center, certified April 2026
differentiators.student_explanation: The National Association of Epilepsy Centers certified a Level 4 centre — its highest designation — on 3 April 2026, held jointly by Texas Tech Health El Paso and University Medical Center of El Paso. It is the first such designation in the Borderplex and the only Level 4 centre in El Paso County. Residents spend 2 months in the Epilepsy Monitoring Unit in PGY-3 and another month in PGY-4, and the epilepsy faculty (Sushma Reddy Yerram, M.D., ABPN Epilepsy and Clinical Neurophysiology, Rochester-trained) runs medically-refractory epilepsy surgical evaluation. The department also holds an epilepsy services contract with the Texas Department of State Health Services continuously since 1990.

differentiators.title: The region's only Comprehensive Stroke Center
differentiators.student_explanation: UMC of El Paso is 'home to our region's only Level 1 Stroke Center and Joint Commission-certified Comprehensive Stroke Center' and 'the only Level 1 Trauma Center in a 270-mile radius', with 293 beds, an average daily census of 269, 71,624 ED visits and 15,518 admissions a year — and it is a county safety-net hospital. The department opened, with UMC, 'the first neurocritical care unit fully staffed by neurointensivists' in the region. You get 4 months of Neuro ICU and Stroke Service in PGY-2 alone.

differentiators.title: Four neurovascular faculty and an in-house neuroendovascular service
differentiators.student_explanation: Four of nine physicians are vascular/neurointerventional, which is unusual for a four-per-year program: Cruz-Flores (ABPN Vascular Neurology, UCNS Neuro-Imaging and Neuro-critical Care), Rodriguez (vascular + endovascular surgical, Minnesota), Maud (vascular + endovascular surgical neuroradiology, Minnesota; ABPN Neurology, Vascular Neurology and Neurocritical Care) and Piriyawat (stroke/vascular, UT Houston). Neurointervention is an explicit PGY-4 elective.

differentiators.title: A UCNS-track interventional neurology fellowship
differentiators.student_explanation: The department runs a 2-year Interventional Neurology fellowship (PD Alberto Maud, M.D.; sites UMC, Las Palmas Medical Center and El Paso Children's Hospital), so you train alongside a neuroendovascular fellow — while, because the department runs NO epilepsy, neuromuscular or neurocritical care fellowship, you do not compete with fellows for cases in the department's three strongest clinical areas.

differentiators.title: The only multidisciplinary ALS clinic in the Borderplex
differentiators.student_explanation: The department describes it as 'the only one of its kind in the Borderplex Region', led by Isabel Victoria Narvaez Correa, M.D. — herself a graduate of this residency — with physical therapists, speech therapists, dieticians, social workers and respiratory therapists. Residents get 2 months of Neuromuscular Medicine and EMG in PGY-3.

differentiators.title: 85% fellowship-or-faculty placement across 20 published graduates
differentiators.student_explanation: Of 20 published graduates (2015-2024), 17 went to subspecialty fellowship or an academic post, at Baylor College of Medicine, NYU (x2), Emory, University of Miami, University of Chicago, Rush, University of Florida, UT Southwestern (x3), UTHealth Houston, VCU, University of Houston and University of South Carolina. Two graduates returned to this department as faculty (Narvaez Correa, Ghatali) — a 10% self-retention rate.

differentiators.title: Categorical four-year structure with 4 months of PGY-1 neurology
differentiators.student_explanation: The program converted from advanced to categorical (the site gives both July 2024 and July 2025), so there is no separate preliminary-year match to run. Both published PGY-1 tracks give 4 months of neurology — one month above the ACGME minimum — alongside ICU (2 months), IM wards (2), CCU (1) and either IM fellowship consults (3) or consults plus emergency medicine.

differentiators.title: December 1 deadline, October review start
differentiators.student_explanation: That is roughly a week to ten days later than the specialty norm (the OPDA guide gives 23 September 2026 as the date programs begin reviewing for 2026-2027), with an interview window running to mid-January or early February. If your Step 2 CK score arrives mid-October 2026, this calendar is materially more forgiving than most.

differentiators.title: The only academic neurology group within a 500-mile radius
differentiators.student_explanation: It is also the largest neurology practice in the city, grown from 3 full-time staff in January 2013 to 11 physicians and 6-7 advanced practice providers today. Practically, no competing academic centre siphons off complex referrals: the department is the region's referral endpoint.

differentiators.title: A named Parkinson's Clinic in the outpatient portfolio
differentiators.student_explanation: The department's published list of its outpatient clinics includes 'Parkinson's Clinic: Focused care for movement disorders' alongside General Neurology, Epilepsy, Electrodiagnosis (EMG), Geriatric Neurology and Stroke clinics; Texas Tech Physicians of El Paso separately runs a weekly community 'Dance for Parkinson's' class. Read the caveats honestly: the clinic is documented only on a medical-student clerkship page, no residency page assigns residents to it, there is no named fellowship-trained movement-disorders specialist, no movement-disorders elective, no movement-disorders research and zero of 20 graduates entered a movement disorders fellowship. Asking directly about resident access to the Parkinson's Clinic is the single highest-yield question you could put to this program.

differentiators.title: Child neurology rotation at three Texas academic centres
differentiators.student_explanation: The 3-month PGY-3 child neurology block is done at TTUHSC Amarillo, UT Health San Antonio, or Baylor College of Medicine in Houston — a published, funded rotation that can put you in Houston for a quarter of a year.

differentiators.title: Bilingual clinical faculty documented provider-by-provider
differentiators.student_explanation: Four of the nine neurology physicians list Spanish in the institution's own provider directory (Cruz-Flores, Rodriguez, Maud, Acosta-Corrales) and five of nine trained in Spanish-speaking countries. Institution-wide, 64 of 236 Texas Tech Physicians providers (27.1%) list Spanish, and the neurology service's advanced practice providers are almost entirely El Paso natives or from Chihuahua with long UMC ICU backgrounds. Note what this is not: the program states 'Spanish Proficiency: Not required; bilingual staff and certified medical translators are available', and no residency-level medical Spanish course, syllabus, contact hours or proficiency assessment is published. The institution's famous required Medical Spanish curriculum is an UNDERGRADUATE MD-student course (code PSPA, preclerkship), not residency training.

spanish_latino.summary: Genuine border/safety-net clinical context with published provider-level bilingualism (4 of 9 neurology physicians and 27.1% of 236 institutional providers list Spanish) at a county hospital-district safety-net teaching hospital; program states Spanish is NOT required and provides bilingual staff plus certified medical interpreters. The 'Medical Spanish Curriculum = Yes' flag is this program's own FREIDA checkbox but is uncorroborated by any program page; the famous required Medical Spanish curriculum is an UNDERGRADUATE MD-student course, not residency training
spanish_latino.registry_field_warning: The registry's `Medical Spanish Curriculum` field is unreliable — wrong at 3 of 16 Texas programs, twice by cross-program contamination. Do not project the registry field; project this structure.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: Zero UCC, Puerto Rico or U.S.-territory ties in 20 published graduate records (2015-2024), 9 faculty medical-school and training records, current resident material, or any institutional affiliation page

program_name: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley Program

fellowships.absence_message: Research complete · There are zero in-house neurology fellowships here, and UTRGV sponsors no ACGME fellowship programs in any specialty. The UTRGV GME Program Directory lists the complete set of UTRGV-sponsored GME programs - seven entries, every one typed 'Residency': Family Medicine (Knapp), General Surgery (Valley Baptist), three Internal Medicine programs, Neurology and Psychiatry. The program's own Program Description says only that the curriculum 'allows for continuation of sub-specialization within neurology in the form of fellowships, if so desired' - i.e. an external, post-residency option. Any subspecialty training would require leaving the institution.

board_pass.summary: No board pass rate exists or is published. The program has no graduates, so no ABPN certification cohort exists. Independently, FREIDA (8/20/2026) reports under 'Program Evaluations' that 'Graduates board certification pass rates: No' - i.e. the program does not even use graduate board pass rates as an evaluation method, consistent with having none. This is a change against the registry, which recorded 'Board Certification Pass Rate Evaluation: Yes'. The program's Program Description states its curriculum 'satisfies the requirements of the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN) and ensures successful board certification' - an aspirational statement, not a rate.
board_pass.student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · No graduates yet, therefore no ABPN board certification pass rate exists for any year or range. Any source publishing a specific board pass rate for this program is fabricating it.

career_outcomes: Institutional context only, and explicitly NOT a neurology-program outcome: UTRGV GME overall reports having trained 400+ residents since 2016, with more than half remaining in Texas and a significant portion staying in the Valley.
outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: Neither. There is no placement data of any kind, complete or selected, because the program has produced no graduates. First expected graduating class: 2029.

movement_disorders.summary: No documented movement disorders faculty, dedicated clinic, fellowship, elective or active research at this program as of September 2026. Prior Parkinson's research capability (Dr. Nawaz Hack, 2024) appears to have left the institution.
movement_disorders.raw_finding: NO movement disorders faculty, clinic, fellowship, elective or research program could be documented at the program level. Specific checks performed. (1) UT Health RGV Neurology (Harlingen) -- the residency's home clinic -- publishes a full 'Conditions and Treatments' list: Bell's palsy, concussions, dizziness, general neurological disorders, headaches, infectious diseases of the brain, infectious diseases of the spinal cord, Lyme disease, memory loss, muscle diseases, neuromuscular disorders, seizures, sleep disorders, sports-related head injuries, vertigo. Parkinson's disease, movement disorders, tremor, dystonia, botulinum toxin and DBS are ALL ABSENT from that list. (2) The sole listed neurologist, Martinez-Menendez, is fellowship-trained in Behavioral Neurology & Neuropsychiatry, not movement disorders. (3) The UTRGV SOM directory contains no faculty with a movement disorders title. (4) UTRGV has NO ACGME fellowships at all (domain 18), so no movement disorders fellowship exists. (5) The only movement-disorders-adjacent signal found is historical: Dr. Nawaz Hack, formerly associated with the UTRGV Institute of Neuroscience Department of Neurology, presented Parkinson's disease research at the 2024 UTRGV SOM Research Symposium ('Influence of Neurotoxin Load on Parkinson's Disease Pathophysiology' and a TMS neuroplasticity study). Dr. Hack is ABSENT from the current 307-entry UTRGV SOM faculty directory and external listings place him in Bethesda, MD and San Diego, CA. (6) UTRGV Institute of Neuroscience marketing and local news coverage mention treating 'movement disorders' and 'Parkinson's disease' in general institutional terms, but name no movement disorders specialist and describe no dedicated clinic.
movement_disorders.student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · No evidence of a dedicated Movement Disorders fellowship or center was found.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: See raw_finding; the Texas contract required capability and resident exposure to be distinguished in prose.

ms_neuroimmunology.summary: No documented current MS/neuroimmunology faculty, dedicated clinic, fellowship or elective. The Valley MS specialist publicised by UTRGV in 2022 (Dr. Francisco Pascual Gomez) no longer appears in the UTRGV SOM faculty directory. Infusion capability exists at the Institute of Neuroscience but is not tied to a documented MS service or MS physician.
ms_neuroimmunology.raw_finding: NO current MS/neuroimmunology faculty, clinic, fellowship or elective could be documented at the program level. Specific checks. (1) Multiple sclerosis is ABSENT from the UT Health RGV Neurology (Harlingen) 'Conditions and Treatments' list (full list reproduced in domain 16). (2) The sole listed neurologist is fellowship-trained in Behavioral Neurology & Neuropsychiatry. (3) HISTORICAL ONLY: a 2022 UTRGV Newsroom article identifies 'Dr. Francisco Pascual Gomez', a multiple sclerosis specialist and assistant professor of Neurology at UTRGV SOM, described as one of just two MS-focused specialists in the Valley. He is ABSENT from the current 307-entry UTRGV SOM faculty directory -- a targeted DOM scan of the complete directory returned 'Pascual' ABSENT and 'Francisco' ABSENT, against working positive controls. (4) The UTRGV Institute of Neuroscience location page lists infusion therapy among its capabilities and names multiple sclerosis among conditions in general institutional marketing, but names no MS specialist and describes no MS clinic; its listed providers are a psychiatrist, a behavioral health consultant, a second psychiatrist and the Institute director. (5) UTRGV sponsors no fellowships (domain 18), so no neuroimmunology fellowship exists.

research_opportunities: 4-year categorical program, July 1 start, ~60 hrs/week PGY-1, 12-hour maximum consecutive duty, no night float, no moonlighting, 4 hours/week PGY-1 didactics, 50% hospital outpatient. Clinical emphases: stroke (via HCA neuroendovascular-capable sites in McAllen and Brownsville), epilepsy/seizures, and cognitive/Alzheimer's disease through a neurobehavioral-medicine orientation. Research rotation OPTIONAL. Academic/clinician-educator track offered; health systems leadership curriculum offered; off-campus electives offered; training beyond accredited length available. NO published month-by-month

salary_benefits.summary: CURRENT (2026-27, effective 2026-07-01): PGY1 $65,600 / PGY2 $68,000 / PGY3 $70,400 / PGY4 $73,000. 15 vacation days, 12 sick days, no carryover. Resident medical fully paid by institution; dental, vision and disability optional and resident-paid; $50,000 group life and $50,000 AD&D at no cost; malpractice covered by UT System; FSAs available; $20/month longevity after 2 years.

differentiators.title: Founding cohort of a 2025 program
differentiators.student_explanation: The residency enrolled its first-ever class in 2025, so a 2027 entrant is still among the founding cohorts. Inaugural resident Dr Fidel Moreno puts it directly: 'We are not only training to become neurologists, but we are also helping to build something new from the ground up... This is a rare privilege that few trainees across the country experience, and it's an opportunity to shape a positive and enduring culture of learning for those who follow.'

differentiators.title: Two residents per year, very high attention
differentiators.student_explanation: The program takes 2 residents per year and the actual current census is 2 residents in total, with a FREIDA-reported faculty/resident ratio of 0.6:1. Individual teaching is a stated program goal - 'Individualized teaching that focuses on a balance of clinical knowledge and anatomical localization'.

differentiators.title: Neurobehavioral medicine as stated strength
differentiators.student_explanation: The residency sits inside a single combined Department of Neuro & Behavioral Health spanning Neurology, Neuroscience and Psychiatry, alongside a Psychiatry residency. The founding PD: 'Our strength is in neurobehavioral medicine. We're bringing together neurology, psychiatry and neuroscience. Physician residents will be immersed in multidisciplinary care.'

differentiators.title: Dementia and minority-aging research next door
differentiators.student_explanation: Organizationally adjacent to the residency are the Alzheimer's Disease Resource Center for Minority Aging Research (directed by Gladys E. Maestre, MD, PhD), a Memory and Aging Center, the UTRGV Institute of Neuroscience and a South Texas Alzheimer's Research Center. The program's neurologist is documented as joining Dr Maestre's team.

differentiators.title: Current anti-amyloid therapy experience
differentiators.student_explanation: The program's core neurologist Dr Carlos Martinez-Menendez helped oversee an infusion suite administering LEQEMBI (lecanemab) on its 2023 FDA approval and monitored patients in the TRAILBLAZER trials that led to donanemab's 2024 approval. That is unusually current disease-modifying-therapy experience to learn from at a small program.

differentiators.title: HCA stroke volume across two cities
differentiators.student_explanation: The residency is a collaboration with HCA Healthcare Gulf Coast Division placing residents at Rio Grande Regional Hospital (McAllen) and Valley Regional Medical Center (Brownsville), whose 'neurologists bring expertise in neuroendovascular services and high-quality stroke care'.

differentiators.title: Curriculum tailored to a high-disparity population
differentiators.student_explanation: The program writes in its own FREIDA profile: 'The population is close to 90% of Hispanic descent. Income per capita shows significant income disparity in this region. Medical resources are limited. The curriculum is tailored to serve the community.'

differentiators.title: Late-friendly Step 2 CK timing and 220 minimum
differentiators.student_explanation: The program states: 'Applications will be considered, and interviews offered prior to receiving Step 2 scores. However, successful completion of Step 2 (USMLE or COMLEX) is required before ranking.' With a published minimum of 220 - well below the national neurology mean - that is materially more accessible than most programs.

differentiators.title: All-virtual interviews, no travel cost
differentiators.student_explanation: 'We will conduct all residency interviews virtually for the 2026 application season', corroborated by FREIDA's 'Applicant Interview Format: Virtual'. FREIDA also notes the program does not offer an open house or second look, so there is no hidden in-person expectation.

differentiators.title: Clinician-educator track and curricular flexibility
differentiators.student_explanation: FREIDA reports an academic or clinician-educator track, a curriculum to develop health systems leadership skills (QI project leadership, community/organizational advocacy), off-campus electives, and additional training beyond the accredited length. Teaching is also a written program objective - 'Experience in the teaching of neurology to colleagues and students... by means of formal presentation and publication'.

differentiators.title: Strong regional retention for South Texas practice
differentiators.student_explanation: 'Since 2016, UTRGV has trained more than 400 resident physicians, with more than half choosing to remain in Texas and a significant portion staying in the Valley.' Entry is categorical at PGY-1, so there is no separate preliminary-year match to manage. Note this is a UTRGV GME-wide figure, not a neurology-program outcome.

spanish_latino.summary: MIXED, and the distinction matters. The program DOES meet the program-specific bar for a documented Latino/Hispanic patient-population mission: it states in its own FREIDA profile that it serves a ~90% Hispanic, income-disparate, resource-limited population and that 'the curriculum is tailored to serve the community', and its founding rationale as published by UTRGV is explicitly built on Hispanic dementia disparity, backed by a real minority-aging research center in the same department. planned_or_aspirational.status: IN DEVELOPMENT, NOT OPERATING — do NOT report this as an available fellowship. A director is already appointed: Dhanya Vijayakumar, MD, PhD is titled 'Director, Movement Disorders Fellowship Program' on both her faculty page and the Our Team page. But the department's Education navigation lists exactly THREE fellowship programs — Clinical Neurophysiology, Neurocritical Care, Vascular Neurology — with no movement disorders entry and no movement disorders fellowship page; there is no named fellow; and no SFMatch listing or accreditation evidence was found. fellowships.absence_message: Research complete · There is NO MS/neuroimmunology, epilepsy, neuromuscular, neuro-oncology, headache, sleep or behavioural neurology fellowship at UTMB. The department lists exactly three operating fellowships (Clinical Neurophysiology, Neurocritical Care, Vascular Neurology) and the movement disorders fellowship — although it has a named director — is still in development and must not be counted as available. So neither of the two subspecialties of interest here has a fellowship you could continue into at UTMB: MS has no fellowship at all, and movement disorders has one that has not launched.

board_pass.summary: No program-specific ABPN board pass rate is published by UTMB. Checked: the Residency Overview, Our Program, Our Team, Didactics, Resident Life and Applicant Information pages (none carries a pass-rate figure); the UTMB GME site; and the UTMB Office of Institutional Effectiveness 'Student Achievement' reporting page, which covers degree-program student achievement rather than GME board outcomes. ABPN does not publish per-program first-time pass rates — its public resource is a five-year 'Pass Rates for First-time Takers' PDF aggregated by specialty and subspecialty. Doximity's Residency Navigator entry reports no board pass rate (only an 'Alumni publication percentile' of 54th and an 'Alumni clinical trial percentile' of 52nd, from 215 ratings and 45 reviews). ONE INDIRECT, PROGRAM-SPECIFIC SIGNAL EXISTS: the department's own alumni page records 'Board Certification: ABPN' individually for every named graduate in the 1993-2007 cohort — evidence of historical certification success, but not a rate, and decades old.
board_pass.student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · UTMB does not publish a board pass rate for this program, and the search covered all six residency pages, the UTMB GME site, Doximity's Residency Navigator entry and ABPN's public reporting. It is genuinely unpublished, not unsearched, and the absence is not evidence of a poor rate. Field-wide figures exist as context ONLY and must never be attributed to this program: a Neurology/Child Neurology training-program study reported a mean first-time ABPN pass rate of 0.86 across 145 neurology programs with 77.9% of programs at or above 80%, and ABPN reported a 73% pass rate on the 2025 Neurology initial certification examination.

movement_disorders.summary: STRONG CLINICAL. 2 Baylor-trained MDS faculty (Wu = Division Chief; Vijayakumar = named fellowship director); dedicated Movement Disorders Clinic with DBS clinic + Botox/spasticity clinic + established Huntington's Disease Clinic; REQUIRED resident rotation; Parkinson's endowed research chair (Kayed) in a $55M+ Mitchell Center; fellowship IN DEVELOPMENT, not verified operating; NO active movement-disorder clinical trials
movement_disorders.raw_finding: TESTED HARD ON ALL FIVE SUB-QUESTIONS. (1) NAMED FACULTY — TWO fellowship-trained movement disorders neurologists, both trained at Baylor College of Medicine's movement disorders program. Laura Wu, MD, PhD, Associate Professor, 'Chief, Movement Disorders Division' and Associate Director of the Neurology Clerkship; MD China Medical University (Taiwan), PhD Chang-Gung University, internship Montefiore, neurology residency Stony Brook, movement disorder fellowship Baylor College of Medicine; clinical focus 'General neurology' and 'Movement disorders' with specific expertise in deep brain stimulation, botulinum toxin injection and headache; research interests 'Movement disorders' and 'Neurodegenerative disorders' with publications on Parkinson's disease medication administration, dystonia, and genetic analysis of familial parkinsonism; member of the Movement Disorder Society, AAN and Texas Neurological Society. Dhanya Vijayakumar, MD, PhD, FANA, Associate Professor and 'Director of the Movement Disorders Fellowship Program'; MD Weill Cornell Medicine-Qatar 2011, neurology residency Virginia Commonwealth University 2015, movement disorders fellowship Baylor College of Medicine 2017; subspecialty focus Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, dystonia, tardive dyskinesia, restless legs syndrome; performs botulinum toxin injections and DBS programming; Dystonia Medical Research Foundation grant 2016-2017; joined UTMB in June 2024 after seven years in practice in South Carolina (Prisma Health Upstate), where she was also establishing a fellowship. (2) DEDICATED CLINIC — YES. The residency curriculum page lists among required subspecialty clinics a 'Movement Disorders Clinic, including Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) Clinic' and separately a 'Botox/Spasticity Clinic'. A UTMB institutional article dated 2025-04-11 describes the movement disorders program treating 'Parkinson's disease, dystonia, essential tremor, and Huntington's disease through medication management, botulinum toxin injections, and deep brain stimulation procedures', operating at the Clear Lake and Galveston campuses, and quotes Dr. Vijayakumar on the DBS workflow: 'We work closely with Dr. Karas to provide DBS surgery. After the procedure, I continue managing the patient's care by fine-tuning the device's settings based on how their symptoms evolve.' DBS surgery is performed by neurosurgeon Patrick Karas, MD. There is additionally a dedicated HUNTINGTON'S DISEASE CLINIC: the department's HD page states 'The HD Clinic at UTMB is established to answer the complex needs by HD patients, caregivers, and family members' and that 'As a member of the HSG [Huntington Study Group], the Department of Neurology at UTMB is preparing for participation in such studies.' (3) FELLOWSHIP — A MOVEMENT DISORDERS FELLOWSHIP DIRECTOR IS NAMED BUT THE FELLOWSHIP IS NOT YET DEMONSTRABLY OPERATING. Dr. Vijayakumar's faculty page and the Our Team page both title her 'Director, Movement Disorders Fellowship Program'. However, the department's Education navigation lists exactly THREE fellowship programs — Clinical Neurophysiology, Neurocritical Care, Vascular Neurology — with no movement disorders entry and no movement disorders fellowship page; and the April 2025 institutional article says she 'is working toward launching a movement disorders fellowship to train the next generation of specialists'. The honest reading is a fellowship in development with a director already appointed, not an accredited or matriculating program. I found no SFMatch listing, no ACGME/UCNS accreditation evidence and no named fellow. (4) RESIDENT ELECTIVES — the movement disorders clinic is a REQUIRED subspecialty rotation in PGY-2, not merely an elective; residents additionally learn and perform 'Botox Injections for Chronic Migraine', 'EMG-Guided Botox for Muscle Spasticity related to conditions such as stroke or multiple sclerosis', trigger point injections and occipital neuralgia blocks. PGY-3 has 'increased elective time' and PGY-4 has approximately five months of elective, which can be directed at movement disorders. (5) RESEARCH — Rakez Kayed, PhD holds the JOHN SEALY CHAIR FOR PARKINSON'S RESEARCH in the Mitchell Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases, whose stated scope explicitly includes 'Parkinson's Disease and related synucleopathies (such as DLB)' and Huntington disease alongside tauopathies; the Center reports over $55 million in active NIH and foundation grants, a $1.6M T32 training grant, $616,000 in foundation funding, 160+ peer-reviewed publications, 25+ graduate students and 11 postdoctoral fellows, and it hosts the Neurobiology of Disease (NOD) PhD track available to residents. COUNTERWEIGHT, STATED PLAINLY: the department's own Clinical Trials page says 'At this juncture, the Department of Neurology is not conducting any clinical studies', listing Huntington's Disease and Friedreich's Ataxia only among PREVIOUS studies; and a ClinicalTrials.gov API query for Parkinson Disease, Movement Disorders and Alzheimer Disease studies at Galveston, Texas in any active status returned ZERO UTMB neurology trials (the single 'movement' hit was an obstetric fetal-movement app study). So movement disorders here is clinically strong and research-strong on the bench side, but has no active patient-facing therapeutic trial portfolio.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: See raw_finding; the Texas contract required capability and resident exposure to be distinguished in prose.

ms_neuroimmunology.summary: MODERATE-TO-GOOD CLINICAL, WEAK RESEARCH. Michlene Passeri MD (Colorado MS/neuroimmunology fellowship, Barrow residency, Chief of Neuroimmunology Division since Sept 2024); required Neuroimmunology/MS clinic rotation; DMT + infusion program (ocrelizumab, natalizumab, IVIG, PLEX) across Galveston/League City/Angleton/Clear Lake/Friendswood; inpatient MS exacerbation and autoimmune encephalitis management; NO MS fellowship; NO MS center designation; NO active MS trials
ms_neuroimmunology.raw_finding: TESTED HARD ON ALL FIVE SUB-QUESTIONS. (1) NAMED FACULTY — YES, a dedicated division chief. Michlene Passeri, MD, Assistant Professor and 'Chief, Neuroimmunology Division'. Training: MD Texas A&M University System 2017; internal medicine internship Creighton University/St. Joseph's Hospital, Phoenix 2018; neurology residency at Barrow Neurological Institute, Phoenix, completed 2021, serving as CHIEF RESIDENT in her fourth year; FELLOWSHIP IN MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS AND NEUROIMMUNOLOGY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO, completed 2022. Board certified by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology. She is originally from Houston, Texas, and practised as a neurologist in LAREDO, TEXAS — a medically underserved, overwhelmingly Spanish-speaking border community — for two years before joining the UTMB faculty in SEPTEMBER 2024. A second faculty member, Xiang Fang, MD, PhD, FAAN, FANA (Professor; Chief, Memory Disorders Division; Medical Director of the UHC and TDC Neurology Clinics), is listed on the UTMB Health neuroimmunology service page as a provider covering 'General Neurology, Memory and Cognitive Disorders, and Neuroimmunology'. So the MS/neuroimmunology service has one fellowship-trained subspecialist plus one senior generalist-covering professor — thinner than the two-deep movement disorders bench. (2) DEDICATED CLINIC — YES. The residency curriculum lists 'Neuroimmunology/MS Clinic' among the required PGY-2 subspecialty clinics, and the earlier short-form description of the same rotation names 'neuro-immunology/MS clinic' explicitly. The UTMB Health neuroimmunology service page lists conditions treated as multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica, autoimmune encephalitis, chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) and myasthenia gravis, and treatments as disease-modifying therapies (DMTs), biologic infusions, IVIG, plasma exchange and steroid treatment for relapses, with symptom management through PT and OT. Clinic locations span the full UTMB footprint: Neurology Angleton-Danbury, Clear Lake Campus, Friendswood, League City Campus, and PCP Galveston. Infusion centres operate in Galveston, League City and Angleton, with named biologic agents including ocrelizumab and natalizumab. NO formal 'MS Center' designation is claimed anywhere, and there is no NMSS Partners-in-Care or Center-for-Comprehensive-Care badge on any page I opened. (3) FELLOWSHIP — NO. There is no MS or neuroimmunology fellowship at UTMB. The department lists exactly three fellowships (Clinical Neurophysiology, Neurocritical Care, Vascular Neurology) and neuroimmunology is not among them, nor is any MS fellowship director named. (4) RESIDENT ELECTIVES AND INPATIENT EXPOSURE — the neuroimmunology/MS clinic is a REQUIRED rotation, not an elective. Inpatient exposure is explicit and substantial: the Non-Vascular Ward Service description states residents 'gain extensive experience in managing complex conditions such as epilepsy, neuro-infectious diseases, neuro-immunological disorders, Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS), neuro-ophthalmological conditions, and various neuromuscular pathologies, including Myasthenia Gravis', and that 'The pathologies managed on this service range from acute crises, such as status epilepticus and myasthenic crises, to chronic and relapsing conditions like MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS EXACERBATIONS AND AUTOIMMUNE ENCEPHALITIS.' Residents also perform 'EMG-Guided Botox for Muscle Spasticity related to conditions such as stroke or multiple sclerosis', a procedural skill directly in the MS care pathway. (5) RESEARCH — WEAK, AND THIS IS THE DOMAIN'S CLEAR DEFICIT. The department's Clinical Trials page states 'At this juncture, the Department of Neurology is not conducting any clinical studies' and lists Multiple Sclerosis only among PREVIOUS studies. A ClinicalTrials.gov API query for Multiple Sclerosis studies at Galveston, Texas across RECRUITING, NOT_YET_RECRUITING, ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION and ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING returned ZERO results. The Mitchell Center's stated scope (tauopathies, synucleinopathies, Huntington, ALS, autism, epilepsy) does not include demyelinating or autoimmune neurology. An attempt to read Dr. Passeri's publication list on researchexperts.utmb.edu returned HTTP 403, so her individual scholarly output could not be enumerated. NET: MS/neuroimmunology at UTMB is a real, named, fellowship-trained clinical service with infusion infrastructure across five clinic sites and genuine inpatient acuity, but it has no fellowship, no center designation, no active trials and a one-deep subspecialist bench that is only two years old.

differentiators.title: Houston Texas Medical Center rotations built into the curriculum
differentiators.student_explanation: Residents spend two months at MD Anderson Cancer Center in the Texas Medical Center during PGY-2 and PGY-3 (acute neurology consult service, inpatient neuro-oncology service, neuro-oncology outpatient clinic; gliomas, meningiomas, vestibular schwannomas, CNS lymphoma, metastatic disease, chemotherapy and radiation neurotoxicity, experimental therapies), and rotate at Texas Children's Hospital in the Texas Medical Center during PGY-3/PGY-4 (the program states two months on one page and one month on another — the conflict is preserved). If your family is in Houston, that is roughly three to four months of residency spent physically in Houston, not a marketing claim.

differentiators.title: Named division chiefs for both interests
differentiators.student_explanation: Laura Wu, MD, PhD is Chief of the Movement Disorders Division (Baylor College of Medicine movement disorders fellowship; DBS and botulinum toxin expertise), and Michlene Passeri, MD is Chief of the Neuroimmunology Division (University of Colorado MS and Neuroimmunology fellowship; Barrow Neurological Institute residency and chief resident). The 'Movement Disorders Clinic, including Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) Clinic' and the 'Neuroimmunology/MS Clinic' are both listed among the REQUIRED PGY-2 subspecialty clinics, not as optional electives.

differentiators.title: A second Baylor-trained movement disorders neurologist
differentiators.student_explanation: Dhanya Vijayakumar, MD, PhD, FANA (Weill Cornell Medicine-Qatar 2011, VCU neurology residency 2015, Baylor College of Medicine movement disorders fellowship 2017, Dystonia Medical Research Foundation grantee) joined in June 2024 and is titled Director of the Movement Disorders Fellowship Program, which UTMB describes as being launched. Two Baylor-trained movement disorders specialists in a 19-physician department is a deep bench for that subspecialty at this scale. Read the caveat with it: the fellowship itself is not yet operating.

differentiators.title: Continuity neurology clinic from PGY-1
differentiators.student_explanation: The program states 'A distinctive feature of our program is the continuity neurology clinic, which begins in the PGY-1 year', and the weekly half-day continuity clinic continues through PGY-2 with you managing your own patient panel. That is earlier than the common PGY-2 start.

differentiators.title: In-house PGY-1 with neurology boot camp
differentiators.student_explanation: The PGY-1 is a categorical internal-medicine-based year run inside this program, spent entirely on the Galveston campus, ending with a boot camp of introductory neurology lectures and hands-on neurologic procedural training before PGY-2 begins.

differentiators.title: 14-bed neuro-ICU, Comprehensive Stroke Center
differentiators.student_explanation: The NCCU was established in 2013 and moved into Jennie Sealy Hospital (opened April 2016, $438 million, 310+ rooms) in 2016; the program states UTMB 'is among the few in the nation with a dedicated neuro-critical care unit'. You work alongside a neurocritical care fellow, a stroke fellow and a neurophysiology fellow on three different services.

differentiators.title: A statewide correctional tertiary hospital on campus
differentiators.student_explanation: TDCJ Hospital Galveston, 178 beds, 'serves as the tertiary care hospital of the prison inmates for the entire State of Texas', and residents run a weekly neurology clinic AND a weekly neurology telemedicine clinic there — a specific, unusual, named clinical asset that also gives you structured teleneurology experience.

differentiators.title: Roughly 44 of 45 graduates placed
differentiators.student_explanation: Named destinations include Mayo Clinic (x2), Yale (x2), Stanford, Beth Israel Deaconess/Harvard, Johns Hopkins, Weill Cornell, NYU (x2), Mount Sinai (x2), Emory (x4), Memorial Sloan Kettering, MD Anderson, Michigan, Pittsburgh, Georgetown, UVA, NIH, Baylor College of Medicine (x2) and UT Southwestern. Six graduates stayed at UTMB for fellowship and at least two are now UTMB neurology faculty (Ruiqing 'Linda' Sun, class of 2020; Vijaya Valaparla, class of 2024).

differentiators.title: Funded PhD pathway and TARCC fellowships
differentiators.student_explanation: Residents may take the Neurobiology of Disease (NOD) Track and 'get a PhD in neuroscience at the Mitchell Center on the Galveston Campus, during their 4 years of residency'; two PGY-4 residents each year are awarded the Texas Alzheimer's Research Care Consortium (TARCC) fellowship in dementia research. The Mitchell Center reports over $55 million in active NIH and foundation grants, a $1.6M T32, 160+ publications, 25+ graduate students and 11 postdoctoral fellows, and hosts the John Sealy Chair for Parkinson's Research (Rakez Kayed, PhD).

differentiators.title: Monthly mentorship plus annual chairman meeting
differentiators.student_explanation: Each resident has an assigned faculty mentor who meets with them monthly; each junior resident additionally has an assigned senior-resident mentor; and the chairman meets one-on-one with every resident yearly. The chairman also personally leads the daily Morning Report attended by all residents and faculty.

differentiators.title: Procedural training that maps onto both subspecialty interests
differentiators.student_explanation: Residents 'learn and perform' Botox injections for chronic migraine, EMG-guided Botox for muscle spasticity related to stroke or multiple sclerosis, trigger point injections and occipital neuralgia blocks in the subspecialty clinics — procedures that sit inside both the movement-disorders and MS care pathways rather than adjacent to them.

Positive evidence it exists: both program directors assert it in the signed Directors' Welcome — 'The Department of Neurology currently offers fellowships in neurophysiology, NEUROIMMUNOLOGY and vascular neurology' — and Ethan Meltzer's faculty bio independently records that he 'completed a fellowship in multiple sclerosis and neuroimmunology at the Dell Medical School'. No dedicated page, application route, complement or accreditation record could be found, only two official assertions that it exists. PRACTICAL POINT: an MS interest has a local fellowship continuation here, but its current status should be confirmed directly, since a non-ACGME fellowship's existence can depend on a single faculty member's availability in a given year.

planned_or_aspirational.fellowship_name: Comprehensive movement disorders program (a PROGRAM being built, not a fellowship)
planned_or_aspirational.sponsor_institution: Dell Medical School at The University of Texas at Austin, Department of Neurology
planned_or_aspirational.status: BEING RECRUITED FOR, NOT BUILT. There is no movement disorders fellowship and no named movement disorders faculty member. As of a posting dated 18 February 2026 the department was actively advertising for a full-time academic neurologist to develop a comprehensive movement disorders program. Whether the search has been filled cannot be determined from public sources. The forward-looking read is genuinely two-sided: a resident arriving July 2027 could enter just as a newly recruited movement disorders lead is building a programme — unusual early access to a founding faculty member and to programme-building scholarship — or could arrive to find the recruitment unfilled and the rotation staffed thinly.
planned_or_aspirational.dossier_wording: The department advertised for 'a full-time academic neurologist to DEVELOP a comprehensive program in movement disorders', with the stated ambition that it become 'a local and regional referral center with a national impact'.

fellowships.absence_message: Research complete · NOT offered at this institution: movement disorders, adult epilepsy, neuromuscular, neurocritical care, behavioural neurology and adult headache. Note carefully that the epilepsy and headache fellowships on the departmental list are PAEDIATRIC — the Pediatric Epilepsy Fellowship, the Pediatric Headache Fellowship and the Child Neurology Residency are paediatric training programs, are named here only to explain what the departmental list contains, and no content from them was imported into this adult record. A Postdoctoral Fellowship in Clinical Neuropsychology also appears on the departmental list. The two published official lists do not match — the Department of Neurology page enumerates Neurology Residency, PM&R Residency, Child Neurology Residency, Neuroendovascular Fellowship, Pediatric Epilepsy Fellowship, Clinical Neurophysiology Fellowship, Pediatric Headache Fellowship, Vascular Neurology Fellowship and Postdoctoral Fellowship in Clinical Neuropsychology, while the Directors' Welcome names neurophysiology, neuroimmunology and vascular neurology — and the discrepancy (the neuroimmunology fellowship) is preserved rather than silently resolved.

board_pass.summary: No ABPN board pass rate is published for this program. The program site, the Department of Neurology page, the Dell Med GME pages and the full 177-field FREIDA node--survey_2025 payload all lack any pass-rate figure. What the FREIDA survey DOES confirm is that the metric is tracked but not disclosed: field_program_evaluation_2019 includes 'Graduates' board certification pass rates' among the methods by which the program evaluates itself. Board preparation is deliberate and funded — the Curriculum page notes 'As they prepare for the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology's certification examination, PGY-4 residents further refine their competence...' and the GME Salary & Benefits page states 'The cost of in-training exams and Step 3 of the USMLE will be paid by the program. Additionally, once during the duration the training program, the cost of board exam registration or preparation will be provided up to $1,000.'
board_pass.student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · This program does not publish a board pass rate. ABPN publishes pass rates by programme only in aggregate multi-year form and no entry surfacing this program's figure was found. SEMANTIC TRAP FLAGGED: the registry field 'Board Certification Pass Rate Evaluation: Yes' is an evaluation-methods checkbox meaning the program USES board pass rates as a program-evaluation method — it does NOT encode a pass rate, and any consumer that renders it as 'board pass rate: yes' or infers a high pass rate from it would be wrong.

career_outcomes: The closest published statement is qualitative, not quantitative: the PGY-4 curriculum states residents 'complete plans for their future careers in general neurology or in additional fellowship training', confirming both pathways are normal without quantifying either.

FREIDA field_program_evaluation_2019 records that the program evaluates itself using 'Aggregate resident Milestone achievements', 'Graduates' board certification pass rates' and 'Performance-based assessment scores (e.g. OSCE, patient or computer simulations)' — so it tracks graduate board performance internally and simply does not publish the result.
outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: NEITHER — there is no placement data at all, not a complete cohort and not selected marketing examples. The program publishes no alumni page, no fellowship placement list, no practice-destination data and no graduating-class roster anywhere on the program site, department site, GME site or in FREIDA.

movement_disorders.summary: DEVELOPING, not established. Named PGY-4 outpatient movement disorders rotation YES; Parkinson's/movement disorders in PGY-3 core curriculum YES; dedicated movement disorders centre NO; movement disorders fellowship NO; named movement disorders faculty NOT PUBLISHED; department actively recruiting (Feb 2026) to BUILD a comprehensive movement disorders programme; pre-DBS evaluation pathway exists via Mulva/Neurosurgery; 5 of 24 residents list movement disorders as an interest
movement_disorders.raw_finding: HONEST ANSWER: movement disorders at Dell Med is a REAL BUT DEVELOPING capability, not an established centre of excellence. It is materially weaker than this program's MS/neuroimmunology offering, and I am reporting that difference rather than flattening it. WHAT EXISTS - CURRICULUM (verified, named, specific): the Curriculum page lists, among PGY-4 additions, 'New rotations for senior residents include supervisory roles in the neurocritical care unit, a "teaching senior" position where residents coordinate various educational conferences, and additional outpatient offerings such as epilepsy and MOVEMENT DISORDER ROTATIONS.' That is a named, dedicated outpatient movement disorders rotation available to senior residents. Separately, the PGY-3 description states residents 'broaden the scope and complexity of the health care problems they address to include multiple sclerosis, neuromuscular disease, dementia, central nervous system infections, tumors of the nervous system, PARKINSON'S DISEASE AND OTHER MOVEMENT DISORDERS.' So movement disorders is an explicit, written part of both the PGY-3 core and the PGY-4 elective menu. WHAT DOES NOT EXIST - and this is the load-bearing finding. (1) NO dedicated movement disorders centre. The Mulva Clinic page enumerates its specialised clinics exhaustively - 'Comprehensive Memory Center', 'Neurosciences' Multiple Sclerosis and Neuroimmunology Center', 'Bipolar Disorder Center', 'Women's Reproductive Mental Health of Texas' - and a movement disorders centre is NOT among them. (2) NO movement disorders fellowship. The Department of Neurology's own GME list is Neurology Residency, Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Residency, Child Neurology Residency, Neuroendovascular Fellowship, Pediatric Epilepsy Fellowship, Clinical Neurophysiology Fellowship, Pediatric Headache Fellowship, Vascular Neurology Fellowship, and Postdoctoral Fellowship in Clinical Neuropsychology - no movement disorders fellowship, and the Directors' Welcome's own fellowship list ('neurophysiology, neuroimmunology and vascular neurology') omits it too. (3) NO named movement disorders faculty member appears in departmental leadership, on the residency Team page, or on the Mulva Clinic care-team listing I extracted. (4) MOST TELLING: as of a posting dated FEBRUARY 18, 2026, the Department of Neurology was actively advertising for 'a full-time academic neurologist to DEVELOP a comprehensive program in movement disorders', with the stated ambition that it become 'a local and regional referral center with a national impact'. The posting names no existing movement disorders faculty, clinic, or DBS programme - it references only the Mulva Clinic as existing infrastructure. A department does not recruit someone to build a comprehensive movement disorders programme if it already has one. RESIDENT-LEVEL INTEREST (real, and a genuine positive): among the 24 Dell Seton residents, five publish movement disorders as a professional interest - Lidya Teshome PGY-4 ('movement disorders and headache management'), Lily Qian PGY-3 ('epilepsy and movement disorders'), Maren Anderson PGY-1 ('movement disorders, stroke and neurocritical care'), Sruti Gorantla PGY-1 ('epilepsy, movement, neurophysiology and cognitive'), Saini Kethireddy PGY-1 ('movement disorders, neuroimmunology and neuromuscular disorders'). A peer cohort with this interest exists even though the faculty infrastructure is still being assembled. ADJACENT INFRASTRUCTURE: the Mulva Clinic care team includes 'pre-DBS (deep brain stimulation) and other neurosurgical cognitive evaluations', implying a functioning DBS pathway run jointly with Neurosurgery, though it is described as a neuropsychological evaluation service rather than a movement disorders neurology clinic.

It treats ADULT patients (18+) for multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica, optic neuritis, transverse myelitis and autoimmune encephalitis, based at the Health Transformation Building, 1601 Trinity Street Bldg. A, 7th Floor, Austin TX 78712. Its published service set is unusually deep: comprehensive evaluations with cognitive rehabilitation, neuropsychological testing, lab work, imaging, lumbar puncture, small fibre biopsy, neurourology and urogynecology assessment, speech and language rehabilitation, nutritional counselling, and social work/case management. EXTERNAL DESIGNATION: *** RETRACTED BY ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION - THIS CLAIM WAS NOT SUPPORTED BY ITS OWN CITED SOURCES. *** This dossier originally asserted that the Center 'has been recognized by the National Multiple Sclerosis Society as a Center for Comprehensive Care' (a Partners in MS Care designation). The sibling agent researching ACGME 1804800001 challenged it, and the orchestrator then fetched both cited pages directly on 2026-09-12: uthealthaustin.org/clinics/mulva-clinic-for-the-neurosciences/multiple-sclerosis (HTTP 200, server-rendered, 43 occurrences of 'Sclerosis') and dellmed.utexas.edu/units/mulva-clinic-for-the-neurosciences (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of 'National Multiple Sclerosis Society', 'National MS Society', 'Partners in MS Care', 'Center for Comprehensive Care', or 'recognized by' appear on either page. NO NMSS DESIGNATION IS CLAIMED FOR THIS CENTER. The probable origin is a brand-string collision: UT Health Austin now brands as 'UT Medicine', and 'UT Medicine' was historically UT Health SAN ANTONIO's brand - and UT Health San Antonio (ACGME 1804821112) DOES hold a genuine NMSS Comprehensive MS Center designation, independently verified in that program's dossier. Treat the designation as belonging to San Antonio, NOT Austin. NAMED FACULTY (adult): Esther Melamed, M.D., Ph.D. - board-certified neurologist in the MS and Neuroimmunology Center; MD/PhD through the UCLA Medical Scientist Training Program; internal medicine internship at Cedars-Sinai; neurology residency AND neuroimmunology fellowship at Stanford, where she was Chief Resident of Education; Research Director of UT Medicine's Post-COVID-19 Program; principal investigator of the Melamed Lab at UT Austin. Ethan Meltzer, M.D. - board-certified neurologist in the same Center, specialising in MS, neuromyelitis optica, transverse myelitis and autoimmune encephalitis; UT Southwestern MD; neurology residency through Harvard Medical School at Massachusetts General and Brigham and Women's; MS/neuroimmunology fellowship completed at Dell Medical School itself; research uses the visual system to characterise neuroimmunologic disease; author of an internationally published book on teaching the clinical method in neurology. (Duriel Hardy, M.D. also appears on this Center's care team and holds a Dell Med Neurology assistant professorship; his MS practice is paediatric and I deliberately exclude his paediatric clinic from this adult dossier.) ACTIVE RESEARCH: the Melamed Lab is affiliated with the Dell Med Neurology Department, the UT Health Austin NeuroImmunology Center and the Mulva Clinic. Its programme investigates genetic, environmental and sex differences in MS toward patient-specific treatment, and how alcohol and other dietary factors modulate the gut microbiome and CNS inflammation and regeneration in MS. This is a funded, lab-based, translational MS research operation a resident can actually join - the Curriculum page states 'All residents are encouraged to develop research and quality improvement projects early in their training' and FREIDA field_research_rotation = 'Optional'. FELLOWSHIP: a Dell Med MS/neuroimmunology fellowship demonstrably exists - the Directors' Welcome states 'The Department of Neurology currently offers fellowships in neurophysiology, NEUROIMMUNOLOGY and vascular neurology', and it is independently corroborated by Ethan Meltzer's bio recording that he 'completed a fellowship in multiple sclerosis and neuroimmunology at the Dell Medical School'. See domain 18 for the caveat about its absence from the departmental GME list. CURRICULUM: multiple sclerosis is named explicitly in the PGY-3 core scope. RESIDENT-LEVEL INTEREST: six of the 24 Dell Seton residents publish MS/neuroimmunology interests - Bhargavi Akkineni PGY-4 ('stroke realm along with neuro-immunology'), Mahboobeh Fereidan Esfahani PGY-4 ('multiple sclerosis and autoimmune neurology... translational research bench to bedside with focus on remyelination and neuroregeneration'), Kara Reitz PGY-4 ('headache, neuroimmunology and neuro-oncology'), Isabel Miller PGY-3 ('neuroimmunology, stroke, and palliative care'), Neha Patel PGY-3 ('neurocritical care, neurohospitalist and neuroimmunology'), Saini Kethireddy PGY-1 ('movement disorders, neuroimmunology and neuromuscular disorders').

differentiators.title: Two shots at one department
differentiators.student_explanation: The program explicitly instructs applicants that 'Applicants interested in matching to one of the neurology residencies at Dell Medical School are strongly encouraged to apply to both programs.' A single ERAS effort reaches two separately-matched programs (NRMP 1793180C0 for Dell Seton and 1793180C1 for Ascension Seton) totalling 10 categorical first-year positions, with 'equivalent training and faculty expertise' and shared rotations across both sites.

differentiators.title: A published Step 2 expectation of 200
differentiators.student_explanation: The FAQ states 'A score of 200 or higher on the first attempt on Step II is preferred' — a soft preference, and one of the lowest published Step 2 expectations a competitive university program will state. FREIDA carries no numeric cutoff (field_usmle_step_2_minimum_score = None).

differentiators.title: Step 2 is not an interview gate
differentiators.student_explanation: Confirmed in the program's own survey answer: FREIDA field_usmle_step2_req_int = False, matched by the program page's 'All documentation must be submitted prior to rank list submission' and 'The application does not need to be complete before submitting to ERAS.'

differentiators.title: Quantified outpatient emphasis, unusual for neurology
differentiators.student_explanation: 'We schedule residents for outpatient rotations a minimum of 50% of PGY2-4 blocks' (FREIDA field_special_features), with the Curriculum page adding that the residencies 'differ from many neurology training programs in that the curriculum emphasizes outpatient neurology as much as hospital-based rotations' and that two-week blocks are deliberately scheduled back-to-back for continuity. This is where longitudinal chronic-disease neurology — movement disorders, MS — is actually learned.

differentiators.title: No 24-hour call
differentiators.student_explanation: Stated flatly on the Curriculum page, with night float instead and home call confined to PGY-3/PGY-4 (FREIDA field_beeper_home_call = [0,0,10,10]).

differentiators.title: A named adult MS and Neuroimmunology Center
differentiators.student_explanation: The Multiple Sclerosis and Neuroimmunology Center is a named adult subspecialty centre within the Mulva Clinic for the Neurosciences, listed as such on Dell Med's own Mulva Clinic page. It treats adults (18+) for multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica, optic neuritis, transverse myelitis and autoimmune encephalitis, based at the Health Transformation Building, 1601 Trinity Street Bldg. A, 7th Floor, Austin. Its published service set is unusually deep: comprehensive evaluations with cognitive rehabilitation, neuropsychological testing, lab work, imaging, lumbar puncture, small fibre biopsy, neurourology and urogynecology assessment, speech and language rehabilitation, nutritional counselling, and social work/case management. It is staffed by Esther Melamed, M.D., Ph.D. (UCLA MSTP; Stanford neurology residency and neuroimmunology fellowship; PI of the Melamed Lab; Research Director of UT Medicine's Post-COVID-19 Program) and Ethan Meltzer, M.D. (Harvard/MGH-BWH-trained; Dell Med MS/neuroimmunology fellowship).
differentiators.retraction_note: RETRACTED CLAIM REMOVED FROM THIS ITEM. The dossier's original wording described this as a 'National MS Society-designated MS and Neuroimmunology Center... recognised by the National Multiple Sclerosis Society as a Center for Comprehensive Care'. That designation claim was RETRACTED after direct verification of both cited pages on 2026-09-12 found zero occurrences of 'National Multiple Sclerosis Society', 'National MS Society', 'Partners in MS Care', 'Center for Comprehensive Care' or 'recognized by' on either page. NO NMSS DESIGNATION IS CLAIMED FOR THIS CENTER and none is asserted here. The probable origin is a brand-string collision: UT Health Austin now brands as 'UT Medicine', which was historically UT Health SAN ANTONIO's brand — and UT Health San Antonio (ACGME 1804821112) does hold a genuine NMSS Comprehensive MS Center designation. The designation belongs to San Antonio, not Austin. Everything else in this item — the named Center, Melamed, Meltzer, the service set, the Melamed Lab — survives verification.

differentiators.title: A local MS/neuroimmunology fellowship to continue into
differentiators.student_explanation: Asserted by both program directors in the signed Directors' Welcome and corroborated by Ethan Meltzer having completed it at Dell Med — so an MS-interested resident can subspecialise without leaving Austin. Caveat, stated plainly: there is no program page for it, it is absent from the department's enumerated GME list, and its URL returns HTTP 404 while the accredited fellowships' URLs resolve. Confirm its current status directly.

differentiators.title: Two structurally different teaching hospitals
differentiators.student_explanation: Deliberately contrasted by the program: 'Ascension Seton Medical Center gives residents exposure to pure consultative neurology whereas the Dell Seton Medical Center services are a hybrid of both primary neurology patients and consults', with complex cardiac and obstetric neurology at one site and complex rheumatologic and infectious disease at the other.

differentiators.title: Safety-net Level I trauma centre primary
differentiators.student_explanation: Dell Seton Medical Center at UT is Travis County's safety-net hospital, operated in partnership with Central Health (the county public hospital district), a 210-bed academic hospital and the only Level I Trauma Center for an eleven-county Central Texas region. Residents also rotate through the Central Texas Veterans Health Care System during PGY-1 clinic weeks.

differentiators.title: Graduated supervision with a named mechanism
differentiators.student_explanation: Not a slogan: 'There is an in-house night senior for the first four months of the year, during which every PGY-2 resident has the opportunity for direct observation and feedback', and 'There is dedicated staff for the neurocritical care unit 24/7, so junior residents are not expected to manage these patients overnight.' Didactics are protected by attendings holding the pagers and outpatient residents being excused from clinical duty.

differentiators.title: Concrete funded benefits
differentiators.student_explanation: $1,500 for one mandatory national conference (registration, three hotel nights, travel, meal per diem); 50% retirement match on up to 6% of gross; daily meal cards for three meals; free hospital-garage parking; transportation home for post-call residents who do not feel safe driving; USMLE Step 3 and in-training exam fees paid; and up to $1,000 once for board exam registration or preparation.

movement_disorders.summary: Strong, fully built-out Movement Disorders program: 5 faculty including 2 endowed/nationally recognized leaders, a dedicated clinic plus a functional/surgical DBS program, a 1-position SF Match fellowship with a documented fellow-in-post and a named graduate, a required PGY-2 outpatient block, and an active clinical-trials portfolio.
movement_disorders.raw_finding: FACULTY: five movement-disorders faculty on the residency teaching directory - William G. Ondo, MD (Professor of Neurology; Program Director, Movement Disorders Fellowship; nationally recognized in Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, botulinum toxin, and restless legs syndrome), Eugene C. Lai, MD, PhD (Robert W. Hervey Chair for Parkinson's Research and Treatment; Principal Investigator), Andrew Billnitzer, MD, Olga Waln, MD, and Joseph F. Imbs, DO. CLINIC: a dedicated Movement Disorders Clinic is one of the department's 11 specialized centers and programs, alongside a separate Functional and Movement Disorder Surgical Program. FELLOWSHIP: one-year Movement Disorder Fellowship, one position annually, applications via San Francisco Match (SF Match), reviewed on a rolling basis by invitation; requires a completed accredited adult neurology residency; fellows train via inpatient consultation and the outpatient Movement Disorders Clinic in Parkinson's disease, dystonia, tremor, restless legs syndrome, Huntington's disease and ataxias, and develop proficiency in botulinum toxin administration, deep brain stimulation management, and baclofen pump adjustment. RESIDENT CURRICULUM: a dedicated Movement Disorders outpatient block in the PGY-2 year (one of three required PGY-2 outpatient subspecialty blocks alongside Dementia and Epilepsy); movement disorders is a named topic in the daily Resident Lecture Series; residents may build further movement-disorders exposure through the 10 months of elective time. EVIDENCE OF A LIVE PIPELINE: a current Movement Disorders fellow (Beatriz Helena Thames, MD, UTMB) appears on the program's directory feed, and a Movement Disorders Fellowship graduate (Vindhya Tulasi Koneru, MBBS, 2022) appears in the alumni feed. RESEARCH: a dedicated Movement Disorders research and clinical-trials portal exists within the Academic Institute.

ms_neuroimmunology.raw_finding: FACULTY: exactly one MS/neuroimmunology faculty member on the residency teaching directory - Abdul Alchaki, MD, Assistant Professor of Clinical Neurology, section labelled 'Neuroimmunology / Multiple Sclerosis', who completed a Neuroimmunology & Multiple Sclerosis fellowship at the University of Rochester (2018-2019) and has delivered Houston Methodist Medicine Grand Rounds on 'Multiple Sclerosis, Trends & Updates'. CLINICAL SERVICE: the residency page confirms residents rotate on the neuroimmunology service - verbatim, 'Residents will rotate on all adult inpatient/consult and outpatient services at Houston Methodist, including the vascular neurology, neuromuscular, headache/speech disorders, epilepsy, movement disorders, neuroimmunology and general neurology services.' DIDACTICS: neuroimmunology is a named topic in the required daily Resident Lecture Series. FELLOWSHIP: NO MS or neuroimmunology fellowship exists - it is absent from the Houston Methodist GME program list, absent from the departmental training-opportunities page, and no MS/neuroimmunology fellow or alumnus appears in either directory feed. CENTER: no MS or neuroimmunology center appears among the department's 11 named specialized centers and programs. RESEARCH: a 'Director of MS & Neuroimmunology Research' position has been advertised for Houston Methodist, indicating the program is being built out rather than established.

differentiators.title: Stanley Appel himself on the teaching faculty
differentiators.student_explanation: You would train inside the Stanley H. Appel Department of Neurology with Dr Appel on the active residency teaching faculty (Peggy and Gary Edwards Distinguished Chair in ALS Research). The department runs an MDA/ALSA ALS Clinic, and residents staff their own MDA clinic twice monthly on the 2nd and 4th Fridays under neuromuscular faculty, seeing motor neuron disease, Duchenne/Becker dystrophy, Charcot-Marie-Tooth, myasthenic syndromes and ataxias.

differentiators.title: Required neuro-oncology rotation at MD Anderson
differentiators.student_explanation: PGY-3 includes a required 2-block neuro-oncology rotation at MD Anderson Cancer Center, split two weeks inpatient consult/admission and two weeks in the outpatient Primary Brain Tumor clinic. Very few neurology residencies embed required training at a top-two cancer center.

differentiators.title: Ten months of elective time, optional research block
differentiators.student_explanation: Electives run across PGY-3 and PGY-4 - four blocks PGY-3, five blocks PGY-4, plus outpatient neurology - with an optional six-month research block in PGY-4 subject to PD approval. There is also a formal mechanism to design your own combined-clinic elective with a written Goals and Objectives statement.

differentiators.title: Nine in-house fellowships to progress into
differentiators.student_explanation: Vascular Neurology (ACGME, 2 positions), Clinical Neurophysiology (ACGME), Neuromuscular Medicine (ACGME), Behavioral Neurology & Neuropsychiatry (UCNS), Neuroimaging, Movement Disorders, Neurocritical Care, Neuro-Ophthalmology and Neuropathology are all run in-house, so you need not leave the institution to subspecialise. Six of the nine are independently confirmed by named graduates in the program's own alumni directory.

differentiators.title: Deep movement disorders bench and surgical program
differentiators.student_explanation: William G. Ondo, MD (fellowship PD, nationally known in Parkinson's, essential tremor, botulinum toxin and RLS), Eugene C. Lai, MD PhD (Robert W. Hervey Chair for Parkinson's Research and Treatment), plus Billnitzer, Waln and Imbs staff both a dedicated Movement Disorders Clinic and a separate Functional and Movement Disorder Surgical Program. There is a guaranteed PGY-2 movement disorders outpatient block, with on-site procedural training in botulinum toxin, DBS management and baclofen pumps.

differentiators.title: A year per subspecialty continuity clinic
differentiators.student_explanation: Residents spend a full year in ONE subspecialty continuity clinic and then rotate to another, at a 1:1 faculty-to-resident ratio with no more than two residents per half-day session. You build longitudinal ambulatory experience across several different subspecialties rather than one generic clinic for four years.

differentiators.title: Required research with real scaffolding
differentiators.student_explanation: Residents receive certified training in research methods and ethics, FREIDA records the research rotation as Required, and the environment supplies 81 active clinical trials and 67 peer-reviewed publications in 2024.

differentiators.title: Weekly safety-net clinic at San Jose Clinic
differentiators.student_explanation: PGY-3s and PGY-4s hold a weekly longitudinal clinic at San Jose Clinic, Houston's original safety-net clinic, whose 2023 patient population was 80% Hispanic/Latino and entirely uninsured/underserved. The program frames it explicitly as 'an opportunity for autonomy in a clinical setting with limited resources', treating epilepsy, headache, Parkinson's, myasthenia, dementia, neuropathy and back pain; Houston Methodist is a six-figure institutional donor to the clinic and holds a board seat.

differentiators.title: Favorable teaching density, 37 faculty to 28 residents
differentiators.student_explanation: The teaching faculty directory returns 37 named faculty for 28 residents (about 1.3:1), with at least nine endowed chairs among them, in a program the PD describes as having 'a high faculty-to-resident ratio'. Ignore the registry's 0.00:1 ratio - that is a FREIDA null-sentinel artifact, not a real value.

differentiators.title: Structured leadership and educator pathway
differentiators.student_explanation: One PGY-4 is elected administrative chief resident each year and works as liaison between staff and residents while assisting in program development; every PGY-4 delivers a Houston Methodist Grand Rounds presentation on a topic of their choice; PGY-3s present basic-science lectures to the department under a research mentor. FREIDA also records a Clinician Educator track plus Health Systems Leadership and Healthcare Economics curricula.

differentiators.title: Named procedural training, clinic and neuro-ICU
differentiators.student_explanation: In the PGY-4 general continuity clinic you are trained in Botox injection, occipital nerve block and lumbar puncture; across two Neuro-ICU blocks (PGY-2 and PGY-3) in intubation and ventilator management, arterial and central line placement, and emergent cardioversion during CPR. Many neurology programs leave this vague.

differentiators.title: Weill Cornell affiliation and Rice neural-systems center
differentiators.student_explanation: Academic infrastructure beyond the hospital includes a Weill Cornell Medical College affiliation, a new Weill Cornell neuroscience PhD program on campus, and the joint Houston Methodist-Rice University Center for Neural Systems Restoration - alongside U.S. News rankings of Best in Texas and No. 13 nationally for Neurology & Neurosurgery, and No. 1 hospital in Texas for 15 consecutive years.

program_name: Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center at Lubbock Program

fellowships.absence_message: Research complete · TTUHSC Lubbock offers NO neurology fellowship of any kind, and this was established from the institution's own complete GME programme index rather than inferred. That index enumerates the full portfolio: 15 residencies (Anesthesiology, Dermatology, Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, General Surgery, Internal Medicine, NEUROLOGY, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Ophthalmology, Orthopedics, Otolaryngology, Pediatrics, Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation, Psychiatry, Urology) and 17 FELLOWSHIPS (Breast Oncology, Burn & Wound, Cardiovascular Diseases, Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, Gastroenterology, Geriatric Medicine, Hematology & Medical Oncology, Hospice & Palliative Medicine, Infectious Disease, Interventional Cardiology, Mohs, Nephrology, Pain Management, Pediatric Hospitalist, Pulmonary & Critical Care Medicine, Sports Medicine, Surgical Critical Care) — and not one of the 17 is a neurology subspecialty. Specifically absent: clinical neurophysiology, epilepsy, vascular neurology, neurocritical care, neuromuscular, MS/neuroimmunology, movement disorders, headache, sleep medicine under neurology, and neuro-oncology. This is an in-house count of ZERO, established by exhaustive search, not a gap in the research. The department's own site tree likewise has no fellowship section. Note one FREIDA trap: field_match_nrmp_adv_fellow = true reflects participation in the NRMP's specialties matching service for the ADVANCED (PGY-2 entry) neurology RESIDENCY positions, not the existence of a fellowship here. CONSEQUENCE: residents who want subspecialty training must leave Lubbock — the department's published alumni record shows they do so successfully, but there is no internal fellowship pathway, no 'stay on as a fellow' option in either movement disorders or MS, and no in-house fellow layer above the residents on service. SECONDARY BENEFIT, stated plainly: with no fellows, residents are the senior learners on every neurology service, so procedural and consult volume is not siphoned off, which is consistent with the chair letter's emphasis on 'unrestricted access' to EEG, EMG/NCV, evoked potentials, TCD, autonomic and tilt-table testing.

board_pass.summary: No ABPN board pass rate is published for this program anywhere reachable. Where the search went: the residency Overview, Application Process, Didactics, Monthly Rotations, Benefits and Where Are They Now pages; the department home page and chair letter; the department's downloadable welcome PDF; the TTUHSC GME programme index, admission-requirements page and ACGME-accreditation page; the full 30-page House Staff Policies and Procedures; the complete FREIDA 2026 survey record (210 fields — it contains no board-pass-rate field at all); and targeted web search. The closest published performance signals are indirect: the Didactics page shows a structured 'AAN RITE (Residency In-service Training Exam): February each year - Preparation Sessions two (2) months before exam; Neurology Faculty & Residents', i.e. a dedicated in-service-exam preparation block, and FREIDA records 'Academic support for USMLE Step 3 preparation' among the program's resident offerings. Neither is a board pass rate.
board_pass.student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · This program does not publish a board pass rate. An access boundary is recorded honestly: ACGME's public case-log and board-pass data sit behind the CAPTCHA-gated ADS public search, which was not defeated, and a direct probe of the ADS detail endpoint returned 404 because ADS keys on an internal surrogate id rather than the ACGME 10-digit number. This is a truthful 'searched and not published', NOT an inference that the rate is poor. It should be a direct question at interview, together with the 2021-2026 graduate placements.

career_outcomes: Read across 2014-2018: 15 named graduates, of whom at least 12 went to named fellowships or academic appointments at UT Southwestern, Vanderbilt, Cleveland Clinic (x2), University of Chicago, Mount Sinai, Mayo Clinic Rochester, Baylor College of Medicine (Houston), SUNY Upstate, University of Florida and MGH/Harvard. That is a strong placement record for a small West Texas program with a nearly all-IMG resident body.

Two graduates became this program's own leadership: Mirla Avila (Class of 2016) is now Interim Chair and residency Associate Program Director, and Mst Jannatul Ferdous (Class of 2017) is now Program Director. The program grows and retains its own — a real and verifiable finding.

One graduate's published destination is a Puerto Rico private practice: Angel O. Claudio, Class of 2016 — 'After Dr. Claudio graduates from our program, he plans to return to Puerto Rico and be in Private Practice.' His medical school is not published and was not inferred.
One graduate went to the VA: Roberto B. Quintos Jr (Class of 2017), Department of Veterans Affairs, El Paso VA Healthcare System.
One graduate received an AAN 2014 Annual Meeting Resident Scholarship (Kasra Maasumi, Class of 2014).
outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: COMPLETE BY CLASS AS PUBLISHED, BUT SIX YEARS STALE — and partially hollow at the end. The 'Where Are They Now?' page is organised by graduating class and appears to name every graduate of the classes it covers (2014 through 2020), so it is not a curated set of marketing examples for those years. But destinations are published only through the Class of 2018; the 2019 and 2020 classes are name-only; and the classes of 2021 through 2026 are absent altogether. All 21 published entries are captured above, including the six with no destination published, so nothing looks unsearched.
