Velez, MD, the residency's Inpatient Director, holds his medical degree from Universidad Central del Caribe - Alejandra's own school - and interned at Damas Hospital-Ponce School of Medicine. Separately, Orlando Health operates hospitals in Puerto Rico, though with no published educational link to this residency. No resident, current or past, attended a Puerto Rico medical school.

program_name: Broward Health Program (Adult Neurology); the program styles itself the 'Broward Health North Program' and the 'Broward Health Neurology Residency Program'

affiliated.fellowship_name: No neurology subspecialty fellowship identified at any Broward Health academic affiliate that this program's residents have institutional access to
affiliated.sponsor_institution: Florida Atlantic University Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine (academic affiliate; two of the program's neurology education leaders hold FAU faculty appointments and Broward Health's Neurology page cites 'close ties to Florida Atlantic University' and clinical-trial participation)
affiliated.status: NONE IDENTIFIED

fellowships.absence_message: Research complete - Broward Health sponsors eight ACGME fellowships, none of them in neurology, so there is no in-house neurology subspecialty fellowship for graduates of this program; FREIDA records that the program offers placement assistance into practice, fellowship or academia.

board_pass.note: No graduates exist. The inaugural class began July 2024 and is PGY-3 in AY2026-27; the first residents become eligible to sit the ABPN certification examination after June 2028. The registry's 'Board Certification Pass Rate Evaluation: Yes' is a FREIDA methodology checkbox, not a pass rate.

outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: Neither selected examples nor a complete cohort exists. The program has graduated nobody, and Broward Health's GME Alumni page - which carries alumni collections for twenty other Broward Health programs - has no Neurology entry. Any claimed placement or board figure for this program would be fabricated.

movement_disorders.resident_elective: No movement-disorders rotation is named at any level. Four generic elective blocks exist (one PGY-2, one PGY-3, two PGY-4) that a resident could in principle direct toward movement disorders, but nothing movement-specific is published.
movement_disorders.research: None found. FREIDA 2026 lists research as an optional rotation with field_research_rotation_duration = 0 and no movement-disorders research is published.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: Institutional capability is general-neurology level: Broward Health's conditions-treated list includes Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, dystonia, Huntington's disease, ataxia, Tourette syndrome and tremors, and a 'Movement Disorders' service heading exists with generic prose only. Actual resident exposure is incidental - through the PGY-2 continuity clinic, PGY-1 outpatient neurology and inpatient/consult work - because there is no movement clinic to rotate through, no movement-disorders attending to learn from, and no DBS programme. The Program Director's autonomic-disorders fellowship is adjacent to atypical parkinsonism but is not a movement-disorders credential and no clinic or fellowship is inferred from it.
movement_disorders.summary: Movement disorders are treated as part of general neurology at Broward Health. No dedicated clinic, no named movement-disorders faculty, no rotation, no DBS programme, no fellowship and no Parkinson's Foundation, HDSA or CurePSP designation could be established. For a student whose stated interest is movement disorders, this is the program's weakest dimension.

ms_neuroimmunology.resident_elective: No MS or neuroimmunology rotation, clinic or elective is named anywhere in the published four-year curriculum.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: Institutional capability itself could not be established: multiple sclerosis does not appear on any of Broward Health's published neurology conditions-treated lists, and the Neurosciences page's areas of expertise are limited to Neurology, Neurosurgery and Interventional Neurology. With no MS service, there is nothing for a resident to be exposed to beyond incidental inpatient or consult encounters. No infusion service for disease-modifying therapy is published.
ms_neuroimmunology.summary: No multiple sclerosis or neuroimmunology service, clinic, faculty member, rotation or fellowship could be established, and the program holds no National MS Society Comprehensive Care Center or Partners in MS Care designation. A search-engine summary claiming a 'Broward Health Multiple Sclerosis Center' in Fort Lauderdale was traced to a non-Society website that does not contain the claim, and was rejected.

research_opportunities: A four-year categorical curriculum delivered almost entirely at Broward Health North: heavy inpatient, consult and stroke time, an epilepsy/EEG and epilepsy-monitoring-unit thread, a PGY-2 continuity clinic and four elective blocks across PGY-2 to PGY-4. Research is optional; no movement-disorders or MS rotation is named.

salary_benefits.summary: Two official figures disagree: Broward Health's own GME page still publishes an AY2025-26 salary table (PGY-1 $59,847.40 rising to PGY-4 $66,158.00), which is exactly what the registry holds, while FREIDA's newer 2026 survey reports higher figures (PGY-1 $61,295 to PGY-4 $68,660). Vacation is 15 days in PGY-1 and 20 days thereafter.

differentiators.title: You train inside a DNV-certified Comprehensive Stroke Center, not adjacent to one
differentiators.student_explanation: Broward Health North - the hospital where essentially all of your rotations happen - holds Comprehensive Stroke Certification from DNV Healthcare (announced 12 July 2021) and Broward Health's own site describes it as 'a certified Comprehensive Stroke Center'. In PGY-3 you spend eight blocks on the consultation and stroke services there, so the certification translates into your own case volume rather than being a marketing line.

differentiators.title: Six stroke-and-neurointervention attendings on a 17-person faculty
differentiators.student_explanation: Three vascular neurologists (Danisette Torres, Menachem Nagar, Swaroop Pawar) and three interventional neurologists (Celso Agner - who is also a site director and subspecialised in neurocritical care - Ridwan Lin, and Mehdi Bouslama) are named on the program's faculty page. For a program taking three residents a year, that is unusually deep supervision in one area.

differentiators.title: An epilepsy and EEG thread that runs through three of your four years
differentiators.student_explanation: PGY-2 includes neurology-service patients 'undergoing long-term EEG monitoring' plus two-week epilepsy and EEG rotations; PGY-3 adds dedicated epilepsy and EMG time; PGY-4 puts you in charge of 'patients in the epilepsy monitoring unit at Broward Health North'. Sonia Kalirao is the epilepsy site director and Damon Salzman covers clinical neurophysiology and sleep. Note: Broward Health does not hold an NAEC epilepsy-center accreditation, so this is about the rotations and the unit, not a designation.

differentiators.title: A state-designated Memory Disorder Center at your own training site
differentiators.student_explanation: Broward Health's Memory Disorder Center is at 201 E. Sample Rd., Deerfield Beach - the residency's base hospital - and appears as entry 12 on the Florida Department of Elder Affairs' own 2025 Memory Disorder Clinic Location Map. Broward Health's Neurology page adds that it is 'designated and funded by the State of Florida Department of Elder Affairs' and part of 'the Florida Brain State initiative', and Broward Health North's page says the hospital is 'home to the nation's first certified Alzheimer's Disease Care program'. This is a real behavioural-neurology and dementia asset, and it pairs with the PGY-2 two-week behavioral neurology rotation.

differentiators.title: Your own continuity clinic panel from PGY-2 onward
differentiators.student_explanation: The curriculum states that in PGY-2 'you'll also begin your continuity clinic, following a panel of patients under faculty supervision and building long-term therapeutic relationships'. If longitudinal neurology is what you want to practise, this starts two years before graduation rather than as a senior add-on.

differentiators.title: Four elective blocks you control, weighted to the senior years
differentiators.student_explanation: One elective block in PGY-2, one in PGY-3 and two in PGY-4, described as being for 'preparing for fellowship, refining a subspecialty skill, or exploring a new area of interest'. Because the program has no movement-disorders or MS service of its own, these blocks - and the system's off-campus elective policy recorded in FREIDA - are the concrete mechanism by which you would build that exposure, most likely externally.

differentiators.title: A public safety-net remit, stated as a service area rather than as a slogan
differentiators.student_explanation: The program page lists as an institutional fact that Broward Health is the 'Safety net provider for the northern 2/3 of Broward County, covering 275 square miles', across a five-hospital system with 1,529 licensed beds, one Level I and one Level II trauma center, and 1,900 credentialed physicians. Broward Health is the North Broward Hospital District, a public district, and FREIDA records the salary as paid by a non-profit institution.

differentiators.title: Academic scaffolding through Florida Atlantic University without the size of a university program
differentiators.student_explanation: Broward Health's Neurology page states 'With close ties to Florida Atlantic University, we stay on the cutting edge of neurology care and participate in clinical trials that give our patients access to the newest therapies', and two of the program's neurology education leaders have held FAU Schmidt College of Medicine appointments (the current Associate Program Director is an Assistant Professor of Vascular Neurology there). FREIDA classifies the program as 'Community-based university affiliated'. An October 2025 version of the program page also named Nova Southeastern, FIU, FAU and the University of Miami as system affiliates.

differentiators.title: Three residents a year, with published placement support
differentiators.student_explanation: FREIDA's 2026 survey records field_program_size [3,3,3,3], 12 total positions, 5 hours a week of structured didactics in PGY-1, a 60-hour average week, and among the program's offerings 'Placement assistance upon completion of program into practice, fellowship or academia', plus a health-systems-leadership curriculum, a formal interprofessional-teamwork program, debt-management counselling, off-campus electives and hospice/home-care experience.

spanish_latino.summary: The Spanish-relevant evidence here is structural, not curricular: the residency is based in a public safety-net hospital district that serves the northern two-thirds of Broward County, and the system publishes a language line. There is no Medical Spanish curriculum, no Spanish-language clinic, no bilingual track and no published clinician language list.
spanish_latino.explicitly_rejected_evidence: REFUSED as evidence: (a) Broward County and South Florida Hispanic/Latino demographics of any kind - the fact that South Florida has a large Spanish-speaking population says nothing about this program's training, and Florida is precisely where that temptation is strongest; (b) the program page's 'an opportunity to care for a diverse patient population' and 'cultural diversity' lines, and the GME page's 'our mission is to deliver quality healthcare to the diverse communities we serve' and 'Broward County's vibrant population is reflected in the patients who come to our hospitals and clinics' - generic diversity language with no named mechanism, and explicitly banned; (c) every surname on the resident and faculty rosters (for example Torres, Reategui, Casas-Reyes, Corrales-Reyes, Trinidad, Deras) - a name is not evidence of language, nationality or ethnicity and no such inference was drawn; (d) the International Patient Program's 'multicultural staff' framing, which describes a fee-paying medical-travel concierge service and not the residency's training environment; (e) an unopened search-summary claim that Broward Health offers 'interpreters who can assist in more than 240 languages' - the page that was actually opened says only 'Language line', so the 240-language figure was not adopted; (f) an unopened search-summary claim that Broward Health's financial-assistance documents exist in Spanish, Portuguese and Creole - plausible and probably true, but not verified on a page opened here and in any case a billing document rather than clinical training; (g) Memorial Healthcare System's Spanish-language and MS assets (ACGME 1801100159, Hollywood - the south Broward district and a different employer entirely) and any University of Miami, Baptist Health or Cleveland Clinic Florida material.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: No Universidad Central del Caribe or other Puerto Rico medical school connection was found - not among the nine named residents, not in the published leadership training histories, and not on the 17-name faculty roster.

program_name: HCA Florida Healthcare/Kendall Hospital Program - Neurology Residency Program, HCA Florida Kendall Hospital

fellowships.not_in_house_note: No fellowship was inferred from any faculty member's specialty, which was a live temptation: the published core faculty hold completed fellowships in neurocritical care, interventional neuroradiology, epilepsy, clinical neurophysiology and vascular neurology. None of those implies a sponsored fellowship here. Consortium membership was also not treated as institutional access: Kendall's own GME page describes 'HCA East Florida's GME consortium, with 10 teaching hospitals, and over 45 residency and fellowship programs', but I did not go looking for neurology fellowships at other consortium hospitals and label them affiliated.
fellowships.absence_message: Research complete - HCA Florida Kendall Hospital sponsors no neurology subspecialty fellowship, and the program publishes no affiliated fellowship pathway. The hospital's complete program list is Anesthesiology, Emergency Medicine, Internal Medicine, Neurology, Podiatry, Surgery, Surgical Critical Care Fellowship and Transitional Year - one fellowship, and it is surgical.

board_pass.note: No ABPN pass rate can exist yet because the program has graduated no one. The hospital's GME page advertises 'near 100% initial attempt specialty board pass rates' across Kendall's GME programs collectively - seven programs, most long-established - and that figure is NOT a neurology result and is not reported as one.

outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: Neither exists. There is no cohort of graduates to sample from and no selected examples are published, because the program's first recruiting season with positions was the 2024 cycle and its first class therefore graduates no earlier than June 2028. An alternative reading in which the first class entered July 2023 (first graduation June 2027) could not be fully excluded, because the registry's three-PGY-level resident figure could not be sourced and the ACGME public search that would settle the accreditation date is CAPTCHA-gated. Under either reading, zero graduates exist as of September 2026, so there is no placement record at all - a material gap for any applicant who intends to pursue a subspecialty fellowship, since the program has never yet had to place anyone into one.

movement_disorders.resident_elective: Six elective months exist across the four years (1 in PGY-1, 2 in PGY-3, 3 in PGY-4) but their content is not published, so no movement disorders elective can be confirmed to exist.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY: real but shallow and mostly surgical - both training hospitals treat Parkinson's disease as one condition among many, and Aventura offers deep brain stimulation for Parkinsonian and essential tremor. RESIDENT EXPOSURE: not published. There is no movement disorders rotation, no named movement disorders faculty member, no movement disorders clinic and no fellowship, so the only route to movement-disorders exposure a resident could count on from published material is incidental contact on the nine months of Inpatient Neurology Consults and nine months of Ambulatory Neurology, plus whatever a resident could arrange inside the six unallocated elective months (1 in PGY-1, 2 in PGY-3, 3 in PGY-4). The elective content is not published, so that route is a possibility rather than a documented offering. A department that treats Parkinson's disease is not a resident who rotates in a movement clinic, and at this program the second thing is not published to exist.
movement_disorders.summary: No movement disorders clinic, faculty member, fellowship or rotation is published for this program. Parkinson's disease appears in both training hospitals' general lists of conditions treated and deep brain stimulation is offered at the Aventura site, but nothing published connects a resident to a movement disorders experience.

ms_neuroimmunology.resident_elective: Six unallocated elective months exist; no MS or neuroimmunology elective is published.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY: minimal. Multiple sclerosis appears once on Kendall's conditions-treated list and once inside Aventura's deep-brain-stimulation paragraph as a cause of tremor. There is no MS clinic, no infusion service described as an MS service, and no MS-trained physician named on any page I opened. RESIDENT EXPOSURE: not published at all. No MS or neuroimmunology rotation exists in the four-year grid, no MS faculty member is named, and there is no fellowship. Whatever MS a resident sees would arrive through general inpatient consults and the nine months of Ambulatory Neurology at Design Neuroscience Center, whose own neurology page mentions demyelinating disease only in a generic textbook list. For an applicant whose stated interest is MS, this program publishes no mechanism at all - and the gap here is wider than for movement disorders, because movement disorders at least has a named surgical service at a training site.
ms_neuroimmunology.summary: No MS or neuroimmunology clinic, faculty member, fellowship or rotation is published, and no National MS Society Comprehensive Care Center or Partners in MS Care designation was found for any training site. Multiple sclerosis appears only in Kendall's conditions-treated list and inside Aventura's deep-brain-stimulation paragraph.

research_opportunities: A four-year categorical curriculum built around 9 months of inpatient neurology consults, 9 months of ambulatory neurology, 5 months of neurocritical care, 3 months of epilepsy/EMU, 3 months of child neurology and 6 unallocated elective months, with inpatient work at Kendall and Aventura and outpatient work at the WeMind Institute and Design Neuroscience Center. Movement disorders and MS do not appear anywhere in the grid.

salary_benefits.summary: The program publishes an AY2026-27 scale of $65,042 (PGY-1) to $73,133 (PGY-4) plus a $950 annual on-call meal stipend, with 4 weeks of vacation and 6 weeks of paid medical, parental and caregiver leave. The registry's salary figures are one cycle behind, and the registry's statement that the salary is paid by a non-profit institution is wrong.

differentiators.title: One categorical NRMP code, no prior-GME gate, and no advanced or reserved track to complicate the application
differentiators.student_explanation: The program has a single NRMP code, 2232180C1, and it is categorical. You apply once, match once, and enter as a PGY-1 with the internship year built in - there is no separate preliminary year to arrange. FREIDA records prior graduate medical education as not required, and the reserved ('R') and advanced position types that can shut out a senior medical student are both explicitly false for this program.

differentiators.title: Your primary hospital is a verified Level I Trauma Center and a DNV-accredited Comprehensive Stroke Center
differentiators.student_explanation: HCA Florida Kendall Hospital's own awards page lists, verbatim, 'Comprehensive Stroke Center Accreditation by DNV', 'Level I Trauma Center designation from the Florida Department of Health and verification from the American College of Surgeons', and 'Thrombectomy-Capable Center accreditation from The Joint Commission'. Its GME page adds that it is 'one of only two American College of Surgeons certified Level I Trauma Centers in Miami-Dade County'. That is the acuity your inpatient months are built on.

differentiators.title: Five months of neurocritical care across three years, which is unusually heavy for a community program
differentiators.student_explanation: The published rotation grid gives you Neurology Neurocritical Care for 2 months in PGY-2, 2 months in PGY-3 and 1 month in PGY-4 - five dedicated months - on top of a separate Critical Care month in PGY-1. If neuro-ICU comfort matters to you, this schedule builds it deliberately rather than incidentally.

differentiators.title: Nine months of inpatient neurology consults, so consult reasoning is the spine of the curriculum
differentiators.student_explanation: Inpatient Neurology Consults appears in every single year: 1 month in PGY-1, 4 in PGY-2, 2 in PGY-3 and 2 in PGY-4. Nine months of consult work across two hospitals, Kendall and Aventura, is where you learn to be the neurologist other services call.

differentiators.title: Three months of epilepsy including a dedicated epilepsy monitoring unit block, taught by an epilepsy-fellowship-trained site director
differentiators.student_explanation: You get Epilepsy/EMU for 1 month in PGY-2 and Epilepsy for 1 month plus EMG for 1 month in PGY-3. Carlos Oliu, MD - core faculty and Site Director for the Design Neuroscience Center - completed both his neurology residency and an epilepsy fellowship at University of Miami/Jackson Memorial Hospital, and a second core faculty member, Elza Vasconcellos, MD, holds a fellowship in epilepsy and clinical neurophysiology from the Cleveland Clinic Foundation.

differentiators.title: Neurointerventional exposure through a Cornell-trained interventionalist and a biplane angiography suite at the second site
differentiators.student_explanation: Core faculty member Michael Crimmins, MD is a neurointerventional surgeon who completed both a Neurocritical Care Fellowship and an Interventional Neuroradiology Fellowship at Cornell University Medical Center. HCA Florida Aventura Hospital, where you rotate inpatient, publishes a neurointervention service including biplane angiography, carotid stenting, aneurysm coiling, embolization and intracranial stenting. Your PGY-3 Neuroimaging month sits alongside that.

differentiators.title: Nine months of ambulatory neurology in community specialty practices, not a hospital clinic
differentiators.student_explanation: Ambulatory Neurology totals nine months - 1 in PGY-1, 3 in PGY-2, 2 in PGY-3 and 3 in PGY-4 - and the program states it takes place at the WeMind Institute and the Design Neuroscience Center, both private specialty practices. FREIDA's newest survey puts 10 percent of training in non-hospital ambulatory settings and 0 percent in hospital outpatient clinics, so your continuity experience is genuinely office-based.

differentiators.title: Six unallocated elective months you would need to use deliberately
differentiators.student_explanation: The grid gives you Elective for 1 month in PGY-1, 2 months in PGY-3 and 3 months in PGY-4. The program does not publish what those electives contain. For someone whose interests are movement disorders and multiple sclerosis - neither of which appears anywhere in this curriculum - those six months are the only published mechanism by which you could build that exposure, and you would need to ask in writing whether off-site movement or MS electives have actually been approved before you count on them. FREIDA does record 'Off-campus electives' among what the program offers.

differentiators.title: Scholarly activity is a graduation requirement with named research infrastructure and a protected research month
differentiators.student_explanation: The program states that 'Some form of scholarly activity; research, QI or a case report is required for graduation' and that 'We have a dedicated faculty member who serves as our Division Research Director and a Research Coordinator', whose job is to align projects with each resident's interests. A QI project is also required, and PGY-2 includes a dedicated one-month Research block. For an applicant who wants a publication record, the requirement plus the protected month plus a named coordinator is a concrete mechanism.

differentiators.title: A new program that explicitly invites residents to build it, and publishes a second look
differentiators.student_explanation: The program's own FAQ says: 'Since our program is brand new, your involvement will not only provide you with a top-notch training experience but will allow you the opportunity to shape the future of the program. Our academics and administrative staff are very approachable, receptive to feedback and adaptable to make the necessary adjustments.' Its FREIDA special-features answer reads 'The growth culture and the impact residents make on the program development.' Its newest survey also turns on a second look, so you can visit again before ranking. Take this as a genuine trade: real influence over curriculum, against no track record.

differentiators.title: A published, current salary scale plus concrete benefits including full conference and technology support
differentiators.student_explanation: The program publishes an AY2026-27 table: PGY-1 $65,042, PGY-2 $67,309, PGY-3 $69,659, PGY-4 $73,133, each with a $950 annual on-call meal stipend on top. Benefits listed on the same page include an HCA Healthcare 401(k), an Employee Stock Purchase Plan, conference and travel expenses, a cell phone, a laptop, board prep, professional memberships and USMLE Step 3 reimbursement if taken after your start date. Four weeks of vacation and six weeks of paid medical, parental and caregiver leave are published in writing.

differentiators.title: Three residents per year, so your cohort is small and the faculty-to-resident ratio is above one to one
differentiators.student_explanation: The program takes 3 residents a year for 12 total, and FREIDA's newest survey reports 20 physician faculty against a 1.70-to-1 faculty-to-resident ratio. A cohort of three per class at a program whose core faculty you can count on one hand means you will be known individually - and it also means there are only three seats, which is worth weighing against the 60 interviews the program conducted for those three seats in 2025.

spanish_latino.summary: The only program-specific Spanish evidence is a single FREIDA survey checkbox - 'Instruction in medical Spanish or other non-English language' - which this program selected in the survey received 2025-07-16 and again in the survey received 2026-06-16. No description of that instruction exists on any page the program publishes, and the checkbox's own wording does not even establish that the language is Spanish. Miami's demographics and the hospital's Hispanic patient share were both refused as evidence.
spanish_latino.explicitly_rejected_evidence: FOUR THINGS REFUSED. (1) MIAMI DEMOGRAPHICS. That Miami-Dade County is heavily Hispanic and Spanish-speaking is not evidence about this residency program, and law 5 of the contract forbids using it. I did not count it in any form. (2) THE '80-90% HISPANIC' PATIENT FIGURE, which is the single most tempting item in this dossier and which I refuse on two independent grounds. It appears in the FAQ of the INTERNAL MEDICINE residency page at HCA Florida Kendall Hospital (program director Jose A. Gascon, MD), not on the neurology program's pages, and it reads in full: 'What is the patient population like at HCA Florida Kendall Hospital? / Miami has a large Hispanic population-80-90% of the patients seen at HCA Florida Kendall Hospital identify themselves as Hispanic. There is a great deal of social diversity amongst the patients so residents are exposed to a wide array of pathology.' Ground one: it is another residency's page at the same institution, which contamination guard 1 forbids me from attributing to this program without exact identity verification, and there is no neurology-program equivalent of the sentence. Ground two: its own reasoning opens with 'Miami has a large Hispanic population', which is precisely the geographic-stereotype inference law 5 bars - so even at the institutional level the sentence derives its force from city demographics. I record it as context I read and declined to score. (3) THE CURRICULUM PAGE'S 'DIVERSE POPULATION'. The program's own curriculum page says it offers 'extensive clinical exposure to all neurological illnesses in a diverse population', and the GME location page says 'Living in Miami Dade County offers exposure to a wide variety of communities and cultures'. Both are generic and both are banned language; neither names a language, a clinic or a mechanism, so neither was counted. (4) FACULTY NATIONAL ORIGIN AND MEDICAL SCHOOL LANGUAGE. Two published core faculty trained at Latin American institutions - Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia in Lima and the University of Brasilia - and the program director grew up in Lebanon. I did not convert any of that into documented Spanish clinical capability. Language capability is a documented attribute or it is nothing, and no page I opened documents any faculty member's languages.
spanish_latino.adversarial_note: Reviewer B finding, severity MEDIUM, affects student advice. FORMAL_MEDICAL_SPANISH was removed. The underlying FREIDA checkbox is real, but its own wording bundles 'instruction in medical Spanish OR OTHER NON-ENGLISH LANGUAGE'. This dossier's own prose said exactly that, so the tag contradicted the text it sat beside. A renderer keying on evidence_type would have told the student this program offers a formal Medical Spanish curriculum, which no program page corroborates. This is the same registry/FREIDA field that has now been wrong or unsupportable at five Florida programs.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: No Universidad Central del Caribe or Puerto Rico tie was found among leadership, published core faculty, or the program's aggregate resident self-report. No resident is named publicly, so the resident finding rests on the program's own aggregate figure rather than on a roster.

program_name: AdventHealth Orlando Neurology Residency Program (registry: 'AdventHealth Florida Program')

in_house.sponsor_institution: AdventHealth Orlando (AdventHealth Florida GME)
in_house.acgme_or_non_acgme: Non-ACGME - UCNS-accredited
in_house.status: Active
in_house.detail: 12-24 months (12 for applicants with a prior critical care fellowship). Program Director Okorie Okorie, MD; Associate Program Director Murad Talahma, MD, who is also a named residency core faculty member; faculty include Amay Parikh MD, Michael Bellew MD (Neurosurgery), Indrani Acosta MD (Neurology and Vascular Neurology), Bassel Raad MD (also residency core faculty), Carlos Pacheco MD, Khaled Fernainy MD and Huan (John) Wang MD. Current fellow: Mehrdad Pahlevani, MD (PGY-4). Training occurs in a 40-bed dedicated neuroscience ICU with integrated stepdown unit in the Ginsburg Tower. Applications via SF Match or ERAS depending on cycle; coordinator Kathryn Clarke.

fellowships.absence_message: Research complete - AdventHealth Orlando sponsors no movement disorders, MS/neuroimmunology, epilepsy, clinical neurophysiology, vascular neurology, neuromuscular, headache or sleep fellowship. The single neurology subspecialty fellowship is the UCNS-accredited Neurocritical Care fellowship.

board_pass.note: No graduates yet, so no ABPN neurology certification pass rate can exist. FREIDA records that the program intends to use graduates' board certification pass rates as a self-evaluation metric.
board_pass.student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - the program has not yet graduated a class, so no board certification pass rate exists for it.

outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: Neither applies: there is no cohort. The program's first class entered no earlier than July 2025, so the earliest possible first graduating class is June 2029. No selective 'highlights' list and no complete cohort list exists, and none should be expected yet. The program does advertise 'Placement assistance upon completion of program into practice, fellowship or academia', which is an intention rather than an outcome.

named_faculty: Anwar Ahmed, MD, FAAN (Program Director; Medical Director of Neurology; movement disorders and tremor analysis in Parkinson's disease, dystonia; former Director of the Movement Disorder Fellowship Program at Cleveland Clinic and Section Head of its Movement Disorder Program)

Mitesh Lotia, MD (Medical Director, Movement Disorders; two-year Movement Disorders fellowship at Baylor College of Medicine under Joseph Jankovic, chief fellow; former neurology residency Program Director at UAMS; founding member of the Functional Neurological Disorder Society)
Zarmina Mufti, MD (institute movement disorders team; headache, epilepsy, movement disorders, neuroimaging)
Chandan Reddy, MD, MS, FAANS (neurosurgeon; head of the Deep Brain Stimulation Program at AdventHealth Celebration)
Mays Al-Ani, MD (institute team, AdventHealth Apopka; movement disorders fellowship at Yale)
movement_disorders.dedicated_clinic: Movement Disorders program of the AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute at AdventHealth Medical Group Neurology at Innovation Tower, 265 East Rollins Street, 6th Floor, Orlando, FL 32804 (407-303-6729), about one block from the residency's primary clinical site at 601 East Rollins Street. Named multidisciplinary clinics include Parkinson's Disease, Essential Tremor and Huntington's Disease.
movement_disorders.resident_elective: Movement Disorder is one of eight named topics in the daily 12-1PM Resident Core Competency Conference. The block grid provides two elective blocks in each of PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4 plus two, two and four continuity clinic blocks in PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4 respectively. No movement disorders rotation is named as required.
movement_disorders.research: PD Ahmed's published work covers unusual movement disorders, treatment of tremor caused by multiple sclerosis, brain stimulation for movement disorders and Parkinson's disease. The AdventHealth Research Institute and Neuroscience Institute run Phase I-III trials across all neurology subspecialties, with methodological support from the Center for Academic Research Excellence (CARE).
movement_disorders.formal_designation: HDSA Center of Excellence PARTNER SITE at Central Florida Center for Huntington Disease - quoted verbatim from the Huntington's Disease Society of America's own page heading, and listed in HDSA's directory under Partner Sites as 'University of Central Florida and Advent Health Mov Dis Clinic'. Director: Anwar Ahmed, MD; Co-Director: Amber Southwell, PhD. AdventHealth clinic site: AdventHealth Medical Group Neurology at Innovation Tower, 265 E. Rollins St., 6th Floor, Orlando, FL 32804, meeting the 2nd Wednesday of every month, 8AM-1PM. This is NOT a full HDSA Center of Excellence; Florida's full HDSA Centers of Excellence are the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, the University of Florida and the University of South Florida. No Parkinson's Foundation Center of Excellence exists here and none is claimed (Florida's three are UF, UM and USF).
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: Institutional capability is strong and specific: two fellowship-trained movement disorders neurologists among the named residency core faculty (one of them the program director, who previously ran Cleveland Clinic's movement disorders fellowship, the other Baylor/Jankovic-trained and himself a former neurology residency program director), a third and fourth movement-disorders-trained physician elsewhere in the institute, a functional neurosurgeon running DBS, MR-guided focused ultrasound, botulinum toxin for dystonia, and named Parkinson's, essential tremor and Huntington's multidisciplinary clinics including a verified HDSA partner site. Published resident exposure is narrower than that capability: movement disorders appears as a named daily didactic topic and is reachable through six elective blocks and eight senior continuity-clinic blocks, but no movement disorders rotation is named as required anywhere in the published block grid, and the Huntington's clinic itself is a single half-day per month. An applicant should read this as excellent mentorship access with an unpublished formal rotation structure, and should ask the program directly how residents are scheduled into the movement disorders and HD clinics.
movement_disorders.summary: Movement disorders is the program's strongest subspecialty: the program director and a second core faculty member are both fellowship-trained movement disorders neurologists, the institute runs DBS, MR-guided focused ultrasound and botulinum toxin services, and the Huntington's clinic holds a verified HDSA Center of Excellence Partner Site designation directed by the program director.

named_faculty: Anita Fletcher, MD (Medical Director Neuroscience Research; the ONLY physician listed on the institute's Neuroimmunology and MS team; specialty training in neuroimmunology and neuroinfectious diseases; Neuroimmunology and Neuroinfectious Disease fellowship at the NIH in Bethesda, where she served as Director of the Neuroimmunology Clinic for NINDS; NOT on the residency's published nine-name core-faculty list)
ms_neuroimmunology.dedicated_clinic: Named 'Neuroimmunology and Multiple Sclerosis' program of the AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute, with two distinct named multidisciplinary clinics: 'Multiple Sclerosis - Advanced/Progressive' and 'Multiple Sclerosis - Newly Diagnosed'. Conditions diagnosed and treated include multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica (NMO) and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody disease (MOGAD).
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_elective: Neuroimmunology is one of eight named topics in the daily 12-1PM Resident Core Competency Conference, and the curriculum overview names neuroimmunology among the subspecialties in which the program provides extensive training. No MS or neuroimmunology rotation appears in the published PGY-1 to PGY-4 block grid.
ms_neuroimmunology.research: Anita Fletcher, MD is Medical Director of Neuroscience Research; the AdventHealth Research Institute and Neuroscience Institute run Phase I-III trials across all neurology subspecialties; PD Ahmed has published on treatment of tremor caused by multiple sclerosis.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: Institutional capability is real but single-threaded: one fellowship-trained neuroimmunologist with an unusually strong pedigree (NIH/NINDS, and former director of the NINDS Neuroimmunology Clinic) leads a named programme with two differentiated MS clinics covering newly diagnosed and advanced/progressive disease plus NMO and MOGAD. Published resident exposure is thinner still: neuroimmunology is a named daily didactic topic, but Fletcher is not on the residency's published core-faculty list, no MS rotation or elective is named in the block grid, and no MS-specific resident experience is described anywhere. Tested independently of movement disorders, and it comes out lower - which is the honest answer rather than the symmetrical one. An applicant with a stated MS interest should ask specifically whether residents rotate in the MS clinics and with whom.
ms_neuroimmunology.summary: MS and neuroimmunology are present and led by an NIH-trained neuroimmunologist running two named MS clinics, but this is a single-physician service with no National MS Society designation, no fellowship, no representation on the residency's published core-faculty list and no published resident MS rotation.

research_opportunities: The program publishes a complete PGY-1 to PGY-4 block grid of 13 blocks per year, with unusually heavy internal medicine ward time (11 ward blocks across the four years, including 5 in PGY-1), 3 EEG blocks, 4 EMG blocks plus an EMU block, 2 stroke blocks, 3 neurocritical care/neuro-ICU blocks, 3 child-neurology blocks, 8 clinic blocks in the senior years, 2 research blocks and 6 elective blocks. Daily noon didactics explicitly cover movement disorders and neuroimmunology.

salary_benefits.summary: For AY2026-2027 the official benefits page lists PGY-1 $69,394, PGY-2 $72,188, PGY-3 $74,879 and PGY-4 $78,536 - each about $2,700-$3,000 higher than the registry's figures, which are one cycle stale. Time off is 20 paid days inclusive of sick, vacation, holidays and personal days. Moonlighting is not permitted, night float is used including in PGY-1, and residents must live within 25 miles of an AdventHealth facility.

differentiators.title: The program director is a movement-disorders subspecialist who previously ran Cleveland Clinic's movement disorders fellowship
differentiators.student_explanation: Anwar Ahmed, MD, FAAN is both your program director and the Chief of Neurology for the AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute, and his subspecialty is movement disorders - tremor analysis in Parkinson's disease and related neurodegenerative disorders, and dystonia. Before Orlando he was Director of the Movement Disorder Fellowship Program at Cleveland Clinic and Section Head of its Movement Disorder Program. For a Parkinson's and movement-disorders interest, having that be the program director rather than a distant faculty member is unusual.

differentiators.title: A second fellowship-trained movement disorders neurologist who is also a former neurology residency program director
differentiators.student_explanation: Mitesh Lotia, MD is AdventHealth's Medical Director for Movement Disorders. He completed a two-year Movement Disorders fellowship at Baylor College of Medicine under Dr. Joseph Jankovic, where he was chief fellow, then joined the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences where he served as the neurology residency Program Director. You would have two movement-disorders-fellowship-trained mentors, one of whom has run a residency himself. Baylor College of Medicine is the principal academic partner of Baylor St. Luke's in Houston, where you are doing your away rotation.

differentiators.title: A verified HDSA Center of Excellence Partner Site for Huntington's disease, directed by the program director
differentiators.student_explanation: The Huntington's Disease Society of America lists an 'HDSA Center of Excellence Partner Site at Central Florida Center for Huntington Disease', a joint AdventHealth and University of Central Florida clinic directed by Dr. Ahmed with co-director Amber Southwell, PhD. The AdventHealth half-day clinic runs the 2nd Wednesday of every month, 8AM-1PM, at AdventHealth Medical Group Neurology at Innovation Tower, 265 E. Rollins St., 6th Floor. Note this is a Partner Site, not a full Center of Excellence - Florida's full HDSA Centers of Excellence are UM, UF and USF - and ask whether residents are scheduled into it.

differentiators.title: An NAEC Level 4 adult epilepsy center plus an ABRET-accredited EEG lab, matched by three EEG blocks and an EMU block
differentiators.student_explanation: The National Association of Epilepsy Centers' own directory lists 'AHMG Epilepsy at Orlando' at 615 E Princeton St Suite 540 as a Level 4 Adult Epilepsy Center - the highest designation - and separately lists AdventHealth's pediatric epilepsy center at Level 4 as well. The EEG laboratory is ABRET-accredited. Your curriculum gives you one EEG block in PGY-2, two in PGY-3, one epilepsy monitoring unit block in PGY-4, plus a Comprehensive Epilepsy Conference, so the clinical volume and your training time actually line up.

differentiators.title: A DNV-certified Comprehensive Stroke Center, verified in Florida's state registry
differentiators.student_explanation: The Florida Agency for Health Care Administration's Hospital Stroke Programs Report of 8 April 2026 lists ADVENTHEALTH ORLANDO, 601 E ROLLINS ST, as a DNVGL-certified Comprehensive Stroke Center effective 4/19/2010 - the same address as your primary clinical site. Your curriculum includes one stroke block in PGY-2, one in PGY-3, a neurocritical care block in PGY-1 and a neuro-ICU block in each of PGY-3 and PGY-4.

differentiators.title: A 40-bed dedicated neuroscience ICU and an in-house UCNS-accredited neurocritical care fellowship
differentiators.student_explanation: AdventHealth Orlando runs a 40-bed dedicated neuroscience ICU with an integrated stepdown unit in the Ginsburg Tower, and sponsors a UCNS-accredited Neurocritical Care fellowship there (currently one fellow, Mehrdad Pahlevani, MD). Two of your nine named core faculty - Murad Talahma, MD and Bassel Raad, MD - are on that fellowship's faculty, so the neurocritical care teaching you get as a resident comes from the same people who train fellows.

differentiators.title: A named MS and neuroimmunology program led by an NIH- and NINDS-trained neuroimmunologist
differentiators.student_explanation: Anita Fletcher, MD completed a Neuroimmunology and Neuroinfectious Disease fellowship at the NIH in Bethesda and served as Director of the Neuroimmunology Clinic for the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke. She leads AdventHealth's Neuroimmunology and MS program, which runs two separate multidisciplinary clinics - one for newly diagnosed MS and one for advanced/progressive MS - and treats NMO and MOGAD. Be aware she is not on the residency's published core-faculty list and no MS rotation is published, so ask directly how residents get into those clinics.

differentiators.title: Daily noon didactics that explicitly include movement disorders and neuroimmunology
differentiators.student_explanation: The Resident Core Competency Conference runs every day from 12-1PM and the program lists its eight core topics as stroke, neurocritical care, neuromuscular, movement disorder, neuroimmunology, neuro-infectious, headache and cognitive neurology. Both of your stated interests are named topics in a daily conference, not occasional add-ons. FREIDA separately records five structured didactic hours per week in PGY-1.

differentiators.title: A staffed research support unit (CARE) plus two protected research blocks
differentiators.student_explanation: AdventHealth's Center for Academic Research Excellence gives residents an Academic Research Mentor, a Project Coordinator and a Regulatory Coordinator, plus biostatisticians, a health economist and a medical editor, and supports case studies, QI projects and full research studies from protocol through manuscript. The block grid includes one research block in PGY-3 and one in PGY-4, and the Neuroscience and Research Institutes run Phase I-III trials across neurology subspecialties with residents able to serve as sub-investigators.

differentiators.title: A documented Universidad Central del Caribe graduate on the faculty of the institute where you would train
differentiators.student_explanation: Angel O. Claudio, MD is an epileptologist with the AdventHealth Medical Group whose official bio states he 'obtained his medical degree from UCC School of Medicine in Bayamon, Puerto Rico' before a neurology residency at Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center and an epilepsy fellowship at the University of Miami. He is fluent in English and Spanish. He is not on the residency's own faculty list, but your medical school is already known to this institution - which is worth knowing given that AdventHealth's eligibility policy is written as 'LCME-accredited schools in the United States and Canada' without naming Puerto Rico.

differentiators.title: A documented bilingual neuroscience service line, including Spanish-language neuropsychological testing
differentiators.student_explanation: Ten clinicians on the AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute team - including epileptologist Angel O. Claudio, MD, system stroke medical director Indrani Acosta, MD, and neurologist Lixandra Gonzalez, MD - state Spanish fluency in their own official AdventHealth bios, and neuropsychologist Alexandra Bengoa de la Mota, PhD 'offers neuropsychological evaluations in both English and Spanish', which is a language-concordant cognitive testing capability few programs document. AdventHealth also provides 24/7 no-cost medical interpreters in person and by phone. There is no formal Medical Spanish curriculum, so your Spanish would be an asset you bring rather than a skill the program teaches.

differentiators.title: A small single-track categorical program with a high faculty-to-position ratio
differentiators.student_explanation: There is one NRMP code, 1102180C0, categorical, with four PGY-1 positions a year and sixteen approved positions in total - no advanced track and no reserved 'R' track to complicate your application. FREIDA reports twelve full-time physician faculty against those sixteen positions, a 0.80:1 faculty-to-position ratio, and 88 interviews for four positions last cycle. Interviews are in person only, with an open house and a second look offered.

spanish_latino.summary: There is a genuinely bilingual clinical environment in the neuroscience service line where these residents train - ten clinicians' own official AdventHealth bios document Spanish fluency, including an epileptologist, the system stroke medical director and a neuropsychologist who performs evaluations in Spanish - plus 24/7 no-cost interpreting. But there is no formal Medical Spanish curriculum, and none of the nine named residency core faculty could be confirmed as Spanish-speaking because AdventHealth's provider directory blocks access.
spanish_latino.explicitly_rejected_evidence: Orange County and Osceola County Hispanic/Latino demographics and the Orlando metro's large mainland Puerto Rican population - refused outright as the single most tempting substitution at this program and not evidence of residency training content. Any inference from a surname - refused; every language claim recorded is a verbatim quotation from that clinician's own official AdventHealth bio. Aggregator language claims - Healthgrades, WebMD, Sharecare and Vitals state that named core faculty member Murad Talahma, MD speaks Spanish; refused because these sites are quarantined under the source hierarchy and AdventHealth's own /doctors/ provider profiles, which carry the authoritative Languages field, return HTTP 403 Forbidden. AdventHealth's corporate Spanish-language initiatives - Spanish-language social-media pages, a Spanish-language morning-briefing broadcast, Lake County Spanish breast-cancer resources - refused as marketing and community relations outside the residency training environment. Generic 'diverse patient population' language from the program director's welcome letter and the program's own FREIDA special-features text - refused as non-evidence. Orlando Health's Multiple Sclerosis Comprehensive Care Center and its National MS Society 'Partner in MS Care' designation - refused as a different institution and a different residency program (ACGME 1801100003). The program's Adventist 'whole-person care' mission - refused as not constituting a documented Latino community mission.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: This is the strongest documented UCC tie found anywhere in the Florida wave: Angel O. Claudio, MD, an epileptologist on the AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute team where these residents train, earned his medical degree from UCC School of Medicine in Bayamon, Puerto Rico - Alejandra's own school. Two other institute clinicians have documented Puerto Rico training. No UCC or Puerto Rico resident could be identified, because the program publishes no roster, and there is no documented institutional relationship with any Puerto Rico institution.

program_name: University of Central Florida/HCA Florida Healthcare (Greater Orlando/Osceola) Program - Adult Neurology

fellowships.not_in_house_note: The hospital does sponsor fellowships, but none in neurology: Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility and Vascular Surgery appear on the HCA GME location page, and UCF's GME programs page adds Cardiovascular Disease, Emergency Medical Services, Endocrinology, Gastroenterology, and Hospice and Palliative Care at the same Osceola site. No vascular neurology, neurocritical care, epilepsy, clinical neurophysiology, neuromuscular, movement disorders or neuroimmunology fellowship exists there. I did not infer any fellowship from faculty subspecialty labels, which would have been easy given a dual-fellowship-trained vascular/neurocritical care program director, an interventional neurologist, two epileptologists and two movement-disorders physicians on the faculty page. I also refused to count Dr Bhatti's non-accredited online 'mini-fellowship' in movement disorders as a fellowship at this institution.
fellowships.absence_message: Research complete - no evidence was found of any neurology subspecialty fellowship sponsored at HCA Florida Osceola Hospital or anywhere in the UCF/HCA Florida Healthcare GME Consortium, so residents here have no in-house fellowship to progress into.

board_pass.note: No program-specific ABPN neurology certification pass rate is published by the program, by UCF, by HCA, by FREIDA or by the ABPN. FREIDA does record that this program uses 'Graduates' board certification pass rates' as one of its self-evaluation methods, which confirms it measures the figure without publishing it. The ACGME's public program search, which can carry accreditation-level data, is CAPTCHA and JavaScript gated and was not bypassed.
board_pass.student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - neither the program nor the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology publishes a board certification pass rate specific to this residency.

graduate_fellowship_placements.cohort: Class of 2021 (the program's first graduating class, graduated June 18, 2021)
graduate_fellowship_placements.non_fellowship_outcomes: One graduate accepted a hospital position in Georgia

career_outcomes.outcome: Three of the four first-class graduates entered fellowship training; one entered hospital practice in Georgia.

outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: This is a COMPLETE account of ONE cohort at destination-category level - all four graduates of the class of 2021 are accounted for - and NOTHING for the five cohorts that should have graduated since (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, approximately 20 further graduates at 4 per year). No individual graduate is named anywhere, no fellowship institution is named, and the program's Scholarly Commons collection stops at 2023 and cannot be used to trace graduates. The program does report offering 'Placement assistance upon completion of program into practice, fellowship or academia'. Readers should treat the 2021 movement-disorders and epilepsy fellowship placements as a documented precedent for one year, not as a placement rate.

named_faculty: Danish Bhatti, MD - listed by the program as 'Movement Disorders and Education'
Mark Klafter, DO - listed by the program as 'Movement Disorders and Vascular Neurology'
movement_disorders.resident_elective: 'Movement Disorder' appears as a named elective rotation on the program's curriculum page, alongside Neuro-Ophthalmology, Neuroradiology, Neuromuscular Medicine, Pain Medicine, Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Clinical Neurophysiology, Epilepsy, Neuroimmunology, Interventional Neurology and Neuro-Critical Care.
movement_disorders.research: Dr Bhatti's UCF College of Medicine profile describes him as a member of the national Parkinson Study Group who participates in multi-centre clinical trials, with 26 peer-reviewed papers and 35 abstracts. The program's own Scholarly Commons collection contains a 2022 retrospective study, 'Association between Parkinson's disease and Acute or Subacute Subdural Hemorrhage', with authors including program faculty member Afra Janarious.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY IS THIN; RESIDENT EXPOSURE IS ELECTIVE AND FACULTY-DEPENDENT. HCA Florida Osceola Hospital's own neurological care page - which lists its service highlights in detail (biplane imaging, dedicated neuro-telemetry unit, dedicated neurotrauma ICU, dedicated inpatient rehabilitation unit, Certified Comprehensive Stroke Center, neuroscience clinical research) - does not mention a movement disorders clinic, a Parkinson's programme, deep brain stimulation, or botulinum toxin services anywhere. So there is no movement disorders centre at the primary teaching site. What genuinely exists for a resident is: a named 'Movement Disorder' elective block; two faculty who carry movement-disorders labels on the program's own faculty page; and a documented precedent that a graduate of this program entered a movement disorders fellowship. Both movement-disorders faculty practise primarily outside the hospital - Dr Bhatti is a consultant at the Orlando VA Medical Center (which IS one of this program's three participating institutions, so VA clinic exposure is structurally available) and UCF College of Medicine's neurology clerkship director; Dr Klafter is a founding member of the private practice Neurological Services of Orlando, PA, whose own bio describes 'a large practice in movement disorders such as Parkinson's disease' and national speaking work on botulinum toxin for spasticity and dystonia, and whose hospital affiliations are listed elsewhere as AdventHealth Orlando and Orlando Health. Rated MODERATE rather than STRONG because the exposure is an elective plus named mentors rather than a dedicated clinic, and MODERATE rather than LIMITED because of the elective block, two labelled faculty, a movement-disorders fellowship placement from the one documented graduating cohort, and structural access to the VA where a movement-disorders neurologist consults.
movement_disorders.summary: Two faculty carry movement-disorders labels, a dedicated 'Movement Disorder' elective rotation exists, and one graduate from the program's first class entered a movement disorders fellowship - but there is no movement disorders clinic, centre or formal designation at the training site, and no fellowship.
movement_disorders.formal_designation_verification: NO MOVEMENT-DISORDERS DESIGNATION IS CLAIMED BY THIS PROGRAM AND NONE WAS FOUND, AND I CHECKED THE AWARDING BODY. The Parkinson's Foundation's Florida chapter names exactly three Parkinson's Foundation Centers of Excellence in Florida - the University of Florida's centre for movement disorders and neurorestoration, the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, and the University of South Florida's Parkinson's disease and movement disorders programme. HCA Florida Osceola Hospital, the UCF/HCA consortium and this residency appear on none of them. No HDSA Center of Excellence, CurePSP Center of Care or comparable designation was found for this site either. Any Parkinson's Center of Excellence claim attached to this program would be false.

named_faculty: Daniel Jacobs, MD - listed by the program as 'Neuroimmunology, Vascular Neurology'
ms_neuroimmunology.dedicated_clinic: Not at this program's training sites. Dr Jacobs directs the 'Multiple Sclerosis Care Center of NSO', which belongs to Neurological Services of Orlando, PA - a private practice at 3849 Oakwater Circle, Orlando - and not to HCA Florida Osceola Hospital, the Orlando VA or this residency.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_elective: 'Neuroimmunology' appears as a named elective rotation on the program's curriculum page.
ms_neuroimmunology.research: Dr Jacobs' practice bio states he 'participates in clinical research associated with multiple sclerosis'. No MS research by this residency was found; the program's Scholarly Commons collection contains neuroimmunology-adjacent case work (a 2020 case report of Zic4-antibody-positive autoimmune encephalitis responding to rituximab, co-authored with program faculty Fabian Rossi and Umesh Sharma; a 2020 report of cavernous malformation mimicking transverse myelitis; a 2019 report of Hashimoto's encephalopathy with faculty member Yassar Chakfe) but no multiple sclerosis studies.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: THE CAPABILITY IS A COMMUNITY PHYSICIAN'S, NOT THE INSTITUTION'S. HCA Florida Osceola Hospital's neurological care page lists no MS clinic, no infusion programme for disease-modifying therapy, and no neuroimmunology service; the hospital's neurological identity is overwhelmingly cerebrovascular and neurotrauma (Certified Comprehensive Stroke Center, 24/7 stroke team, stroke unit, interventional neuroradiology suite, neurovascular ICU, biplane imaging). What a resident here can actually get in MS is a 'Neuroimmunology' elective block with one labelled faculty member whose MS centre sits in a private Orlando practice outside the program's named training sites. That is genuine mentorship access but it is not an institutional MS programme, and a resident could not count on a longitudinal MS panel of their own beyond whatever their weekly half-day continuity clinic happens to contain. Rated LIMITED. For a candidate whose stated interests are movement disorders AND multiple sclerosis, the MS half of that pair is the weaker half at this program.
ms_neuroimmunology.summary: One faculty member carries a neuroimmunology label and a 'Neuroimmunology' elective rotation exists, but the multiple sclerosis centre he directs belongs to a private Orlando practice rather than to this residency's training sites, and the hospital publishes no MS programme or designation.
ms_neuroimmunology.formal_designation_verification: NO MS DESIGNATION IS CLAIMED BY THIS PROGRAM, AND ONE NEAR-MISS WAS REFUSED. An aggregator profile of Dr Jacobs was reported in search results as describing the Multiple Sclerosis Care Center of NSO as an 'MSFC (Consortium) certified multiple sclerosis center'. I opened his own practice bio at Neurological Services of Orlando and it makes NO such claim - it says only that he 'does direct the Multiple Sclerosis Care Center of NSO, and participates in clinical research associated with multiple sclerosis'. The aggregator phrasing also garbles the acronym (MSFC is the Multiple Sclerosis Functional Composite, a disability measure, not a certifying body). I therefore record NO designation. Critically, even if such a certification existed it would belong to a private practice in Orlando, not to this residency or to HCA Florida Osceola Hospital, so it could not be reported as a designation of this program. No National Multiple Sclerosis Society Comprehensive Care Center or Partners in MS Care designation was found for HCA Florida Osceola Hospital or the UCF/HCA consortium.

research_opportunities: A four-year categorical curriculum: an in-program internal medicine intern year with four months of neurology and emergency medicine, inpatient stroke and consult neurology in PGY-2, then graduated responsibility with child neurology, psychiatry, night float and twelve named electives in PGY-3 and PGY-4, alongside a weekly half-day continuity clinic from PGY-2 onward. The rotation-by-rotation block schedule is not published.

salary_benefits.summary: For academic year 2026-2027 the UCF/HCA consortium's published salary schedule pays $64,744 at PGY-1 and $72,689 at PGY-4 at the Osceola/Kissimmee site, with 15 vacation days in PGY-1 rising to 20 thereafter, 10 sick days and cost-shared medical, dental, life and disability coverage. Moonlighting is not permitted.

differentiators.title: Comprehensive stroke centre volume from the first neurology year onward
differentiators.student_explanation: The main teaching site, HCA Florida Osceola Hospital, is a 404-bed Certified Comprehensive Stroke Center and Joint Commission-certified Level II trauma centre with a 24/7 multidisciplinary acute stroke team, a stroke unit, an interventional neuroradiology suite, a neurovascular intensive care unit, a dedicated neuro-telemetry unit and biplane imaging. PGY-2 is spent primarily on the inpatient stroke and neurology consultation services, so you are inside that volume from your first neurology year rather than waiting for it.

differentiators.title: A named Movement Disorder elective with two movement-disorders faculty
differentiators.student_explanation: 'Movement Disorder' is one of twelve named elective rotations, and the program's faculty page labels two physicians for movement disorders - Danish Bhatti, MD (Movement Disorders and Education), who is a UCF College of Medicine associate professor, the college's neurology clerkship director and a member of the national Parkinson Study Group, and Mark Klafter, DO (Movement Disorders and Vascular Neurology), whose practice bio describes a large Parkinson's disease practice and national speaking work on botulinum toxin for spasticity and dystonia. If movement disorders is your direction, there are named people attached to a named block.

differentiators.title: A graduate of the first class went into a movement disorders fellowship
differentiators.student_explanation: UCF College of Medicine reported that of the four residents in the program's first graduating class in June 2021, three went on to fellowships 'in areas that include movement disorders and epilepsy'. That is a documented precedent that this program's training can lead into a movement disorders fellowship, rather than a general assurance about fellowship prospects.

differentiators.title: Three genuinely different training environments, including a VA and a children's hospital
differentiators.student_explanation: The program's three participating institutions are HCA Florida Osceola Hospital in Kissimmee, the Orlando VA Medical Center and Nemours Children's Hospital in Lake Nona. You rotate on veterans' neurological care at the VA and on paediatric neurological care at Nemours, alongside community and tertiary adult neurology at Osceola - three payer mixes and three patient populations inside one four-year programme.

differentiators.title: Your own continuity clinic for three straight years
differentiators.student_explanation: Every resident has their own longitudinal continuity clinic throughout PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4, running a half-day per week. For someone with a longitudinal-neurology interest, that is a three-year panel of your own patients rather than a rotating block of clinic weeks.

differentiators.title: The intern year is inside the programme, not separately matched
differentiators.student_explanation: This is a four-year categorical programme entered at PGY-1, and the FAQ states plainly: 'Yes, it is a four-year categorical program. The preliminary year (PGY1) in internal medicine is supervised by the internal medicine and neurology program directors.' You match once, for all four years. NRMP lists a single track for this programme, 1587180C0, with no advanced or reserved variant - so there is no separate preliminary year to arrange and no upper-level-only entry route.

differentiators.title: Twelve named electives across most of neurology's subspecialties
differentiators.student_explanation: The published elective list covers Ophthalmology, Neuro-Ophthalmology, Movement Disorder, Neuroradiology, Neuromuscular Medicine, Pain Medicine, Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Clinical Neurophysiology, Epilepsy, Neuroimmunology, Interventional Neurology and Neuro-Critical Care, and the programme also reports off-campus electives are permitted. That breadth matters at a programme with no in-house neurology fellowship, because electives are the main route to subspecialty exposure here.

differentiators.title: A thirteen-item weekly didactic programme including a neuropathology course and biostatistics
differentiators.student_explanation: The published conference schedule includes morning report, grand rounds, a neurological emergency course, neurology board review, neurovascular conference, neuroimaging conference, neurology subspecialty conferences, a neuromuscular disease conference, a neuropathology course, a research course including biostatistics for the clinician, journal club, a stroke quality improvement conference and morbidity and mortality conference. The programme reports six hours per week of structured didactics in the intern year.

differentiators.title: Small, four-per-year classes with a published interview-to-position ratio
differentiators.student_explanation: The programme takes four residents a year against a total approved complement of sixteen, and reports conducting 60 interviews for those four positions in its most recent cycle - about fifteen interviews per position - while stating that roughly 10% of applicants are offered an interview. It reports an average 56-hour duty week in the intern year and does not permit moonlighting.

spanish_latino.summary: No Spanish-language clinical service, formal Medical Spanish curriculum, bilingual track, residency-specific interpreter policy or documented Latino community partnership was found for this residency. The registry's 'Medical Spanish Curriculum: No' was re-verified against a newer survey cycle and holds.
spanish_latino.explicitly_rejected_evidence: I refused, in order of how tempting each was. (1) OSCEOLA COUNTY DEMOGRAPHICS - the single most tempting substitution available anywhere in Florida. Osceola County has one of the highest Puerto Rican population shares of any county in the United States, and Kissimmee sits at the centre of the largest mainland Puerto Rican community. A Spanish-speaking applicant would obviously encounter Spanish-speaking patients here. That is a fact about a county, not a fact about a residency curriculum, and governance law 5 forbids treating it as evidence. Not counted, in any strength rating, in any domain. (2) THE HOSPITAL WEBSITE'S SPANISH INFRASTRUCTURE - hcafloridahealthcare.com and hcafloridaphysicians.com both ship an English/Espanol language toggle and a 'physicianReferralPhoneNumberSpanish' of (855) 790-3627, and the pages carry a Spanish-language version of HCA's physician-referral disclaimer. This is HCA corporate template applied identically across dozens of hospitals in multiple states; it is marketing localisation, not a clinical service and not a residency curriculum. Refused under contamination guard 4. (3) HCA'S NONDISCRIMINATION NOTICE - present in the footer of every HCA page and containing the boilerplate language-assistance provisions federal law requires. Institution-wide compliance text is not an interpreter policy tied to this residency. Refused. (4) FACULTY AND CO-AUTHOR SURNAMES - the program's faculty page includes Fernando Gonzalez-Portillo, MD, and its Scholarly Commons collection includes co-authors such as Giovanni F. Ramirez and Paola Colon Fugueroa. Governance law 4 forbids inferring language, nationality or ethnicity from a name, so none of these was counted as evidence of Spanish capability, and 'spanish_documented' is null rather than true for every faculty member. (5) THE MIAMI HCA PROGRAM'S MEDICAL SPANISH CLAIM - see the raw finding; a different program, via an aggregator. Refused. (6) GENERIC DIVERSITY LANGUAGE - the program's mission statement says its faculty are committed to 'expanding residents' perspectives to be inclusive of cultures, values and ideals'. That is a values statement with no named clinical mechanism and is not Spanish-language or Latino-community evidence. Refused. WHAT WOULD HAVE COUNTED AND WAS ABSENT: a named Spanish-language clinic or service line, a formal Medical Spanish curriculum or elective, a bilingual track or bilingual-resident designation, an interpreter policy written into this residency's own materials, or a documented partnership with a named Latino community organisation or federally qualified health centre.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: No documented tie to Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce, the University of Puerto Rico, San Juan Bautista or any Puerto Rico institution was found for this residency - no residents, alumni, fellows, faculty or leadership, and no partnership or recruitment relationship. Osceola County's large Puerto Rican population is not evidence and was not counted.

outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: These are COMPLETE COHORTS, not selected examples, and the distinction was tested rather than assumed. Three lines of evidence: the published class sizes (4, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, 2) track the program's own uneven cohort pattern rather than a curated highlight reel; the list includes outcomes no marketing page would choose, with 'General Neurology at Miami, FL' appearing three times and 'Neurology Specialist in Fort Myers, FL' once; and decisively, the four names in the 2026 class are exactly the four residents shown as PGY-4s in the independently retrieved 2026-06-09 Wayback snapshot of the resident roster, with matching fellowship destinations. The one caveat is the class of 2020, listed with only two graduates, which may be incomplete for an early year. Graduates' medical schools are NOT published, so alumni-level UCC or Puerto Rico representation cannot be assessed.
