Aizik L. Wolf, MD - neurosurgeon; Gamma Knife stereotactic radiosurgery including for movement disorders; founder, Miami Neuroscience Center
Carrie Landess, MD - clinically manages Parkinson's disease among other conditions (UCC graduate)
movement_disorders.dedicated_clinic: Yes, but EXTERNAL to Larkin: the Parkinson's Disease and Movement Disorders Center of Boca Raton (Dr Isaacson) and South Miami Neurology (Dr Starosta-Rubinstein). Larkin itself operates a 'Neuroscience Center' and a 'Center for Advanced Neurology' but publishes no in-house movement disorders clinic.
movement_disorders.resident_elective: Not an elective - REQUIRED. Six movement-disorders-inclusive months are built into the required curriculum: '1 Month - Movement Disorders' plus '1 Month - Cognitive and Movement Disorders' in each of PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4.
movement_disorders.research: The Boca Raton centre is described by the program as 'a nationally recognized, non-university-based academic center and leading clinical research institution that provides community access to Phase II and Phase III FDA-regulated clinical trials focused on improving symptoms and slowing disease progression in Parkinson's disease.' Dr Isaacson 'has led extensive clinical research and drug development programs, authored hundreds of publications' and promotes education 'through the Parkinson's Research & Education Foundation'.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: These diverge sharply and the distinction is the whole story of this domain. RESIDENT EXPOSURE IS STRONG and, unusually, mandatory: six named movement-disorders months across PGY-2 to PGY-4 in a 48-month curriculum, at a nationally active Parkinson's trial centre, plus hands-on procedural exposure in a separate continuity clinic that includes 'monthly deep brain stimulation (DBS) programming' and 'botulinum toxin injections'. Required DBS programming exposure is rare at community programs and is the single most concrete movement-disorders asset here. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY IS LIMITED: Larkin Community Hospital itself runs no movement disorders clinic, no movement disorders fellowship and no movement disorders research program. Every one of those months is delivered at an external private practice, and the Isaacson centre is in BOCA RATON - roughly 45 to 50 miles north of the South Miami primary site, which is a real commuting burden a student should price in. OUTCOME COUNTERWEIGHT, and it matters: across 25 published graduates from 2020 to 2026, ZERO entered a movement disorders fellowship. Placements went overwhelmingly to vascular neurology and neurocritical care. So the program reliably delivers movement disorders EXPOSURE but has no track record of converting it into movement disorders CAREERS. Strength is rated MODERATE rather than STRONG for that reason: the required-rotation structure is strong, the owning institution's own capability and the outcome record are not.
movement_disorders.summary: Movement disorders is this program's most distinctive required-curriculum feature: six mandatory movement-disorders months across PGY-2 to PGY-4, taught by a nationally recognised Parkinson's specialist at his Boca Raton trial centre, plus monthly DBS programming and botulinum toxin exposure in a Coral Gables continuity clinic. All of it is delivered at external private practices rather than at Larkin, there is no in-house fellowship, and no graduate in seven years has entered a movement disorders fellowship.

named_faculty: Brian Steingo, MD - Medical Director, Boca Raton Multiple Sclerosis Center; MS biologic-therapy trialist; Chairman of the Professional Advisory Committee for the South Florida Chapter of the National Multiple Sclerosis Society
Carrie Landess, MD - clinically manages multiple sclerosis among other conditions (UCC graduate)
ms_neuroimmunology.dedicated_clinic: Yes, but EXTERNAL to Larkin: the Boca Raton Multiple Sclerosis Center, led by Dr Brian Steingo. Larkin publishes no in-house MS or neuroimmunology clinic.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_elective: Not an elective - REQUIRED, but only once: '1 Month - Multiple Sclerosis' in PGY-2. There is no further required MS month in PGY-3 or PGY-4, though three PGY-4 elective months and one PGY-3 elective month exist and could in principle be used for more.
ms_neuroimmunology.research: Dr Steingo 'has been extensively involved in clinical research, including numerous clinical trials evaluating biologic therapies for multiple sclerosis.' No MS research role for residents is published.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: RESIDENT EXPOSURE IS REAL BUT THIN IN DURATION: exactly one required month, in PGY-2, at a named MS-specialist centre. The program describes it as a 'clinical neuroimmunology rotation' with a substantive competency list - 'diagnosis and classification of CNS demyelinating diseases', 'initiating and monitoring immunomodulatory therapies, recognizing treatment-related complications', and long-term symptom management. So the month is well specified, it is simply one month. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY IS LIMITED: no in-house MS centre, no neuroimmunology fellowship, no MS infusion service published at Larkin, and the rotation sits in Boca Raton some 45 to 50 miles from the primary site. OUTCOME EVIDENCE IS POSITIVE BUT SINGULAR: one graduate of 25 published (Robert Coppola, DO, class of 2021) entered a 'Neuroimmunology Fellowship at Jackson Memorial Hospital, University of Miami'. That is genuine proof the pathway from this program into academic neuroimmunology is open, and it is exactly one data point in seven years. Strength MODERATE: a named specialist centre, a well-defined required month and one real fellowship outcome exceed 'LIMITED', while a single month and no institutional infrastructure fall short of 'STRONG'.
ms_neuroimmunology.summary: One required PGY-2 month at the Boca Raton Multiple Sclerosis Center under Dr Brian Steingo, an MS trialist who chairs the National MS Society's South Florida chapter professional advisory committee. The rotation is explicitly framed as clinical neuroimmunology and one graduate went on to a neuroimmunology fellowship at University of Miami/Jackson - but it is a single month, delivered off-site, with no in-house MS centre or fellowship. No NMSS institutional care-centre designation could be verified.

research_opportunities: A four-year categorical curriculum with unusually specific subspecialty months - six movement-disorders months, one MS month, four EEG/epilepsy months, four EMG/NCS months, and required sleep, pain and neuro-ophthalmology blocks - delivered across five teaching hospitals and nine named private practices. There is no research rotation and no research track.

salary_benefits.summary: PGY-1 salary is $47,500 rising to $53,500 in PGY-4, with 20 vacation days, a housing stipend, free parking and cost-shared medical, dental and disability coverage. Group life and mental health benefits are reported as not available. The salary figures are one cycle newer than the registry's.

differentiators.title: Six required movement-disorders months - not electives
differentiators.student_explanation: The curriculum builds in '1 Month - Movement Disorders' plus '1 Month - Cognitive and Movement Disorders' in each of PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4. That is six mandatory movement-disorders months out of 48, repeated annually so the exposure is longitudinal rather than a single block. For someone targeting movement disorders this is a structural commitment most programs of this size do not make.

differentiators.title: Monthly deep brain stimulation programming and botulinum toxin injections as a resident
differentiators.student_explanation: In the Coral Gables continuity clinic the program states residents 'participate in therapeutic procedures such as botulinum toxin injections and monthly deep brain stimulation (DBS) programming.' Hands-on DBS programming during residency is rare, and it is the most concrete procedural movement-disorders skill on offer here.

differentiators.title: A Universidad Central del Caribe graduate on the faculty who precepts a required rotation
differentiators.student_explanation: Dr Carrie Landess earned her medical degree from Universidad Central del Caribe - your own school - and she is not a peripheral name: she precepts a required continuity-clinic rotation in North Miami, and her clinic is listed in FREIDA as a participating training institution. She is a natural mentor and a concrete point of connection in your application.

differentiators.title: Movement disorders taught at a Phase II/III Parkinson's trial centre
differentiators.student_explanation: The Movement Disorders month is spent at the Parkinson's Disease and Movement Disorders Center of Boca Raton, which the program describes as providing 'community access to Phase II and Phase III FDA-regulated clinical trials' in Parkinson's disease, under Dr Stuart Isaacson. You would see trial-stage therapeutics, not just clinic management. Note the site is in Boca Raton, roughly 45-50 miles north of South Miami.

differentiators.title: A dedicated MS and clinical neuroimmunology month at a specialist centre
differentiators.student_explanation: PGY-2 includes '1 Month - Multiple Sclerosis' at the Boca Raton Multiple Sclerosis Center under Dr Brian Steingo, an MS trialist who chairs the National MS Society South Florida chapter's professional advisory committee. The program frames it as a 'clinical neuroimmunology rotation' covering immunomodulatory therapy initiation and monitoring. It is one month, so plan to extend it with elective time if MS is a serious goal.

differentiators.title: Two Spanish-fluent neurologists precept required rotations
differentiators.student_explanation: The program's own faculty page documents that 'Dr. Lalama is bilingual and fluent in both English and Spanish' and that 'Dr. Starosta Rubinstein is fluent in Spanish.' Both precept required continuity rotations, so your Spanish would be used in supervised clinical care with attendings who share the language - not just with patients.

differentiators.title: A genuinely strong fellowship placement record for a community program
differentiators.student_explanation: Nineteen of 25 graduates from 2020-2026 entered fellowships, at Emory, University of Chicago, Rutgers, Tulane, UC Davis, UT Southwestern, UT Health San Antonio, UTMB, Virginia, Washington, Oklahoma, South Florida and University of Miami. The program publishes every graduate by name and destination, including the unglamorous ones, which is a credible disclosure.

differentiators.title: Categorical PGY-1 entry with no preliminary year to arrange
differentiators.student_explanation: NRMP code 1481180C0 carries the 'C' categorical suffix and the program reports offering no preliminary or advanced positions. You would enter at PGY-1 and stay four years, with no need to separately match a preliminary year - a materially simpler application than an Advanced-only program.

differentiators.title: Your delayed Step 2 CK result does not block the application
differentiators.student_explanation: The application page asks for a 'USMLE Step 2 or COMLEX Level 2 score (if available)' - explicitly optional at submission - and interviews run on Fridays in November, December and January. A mid-October 2026 score arrives before any interview date.

differentiators.title: High-volume stroke training across three certified stroke centres
differentiators.student_explanation: Stroke and Neurologic Critical Care is required in PGY-2 (3 months), PGY-3 (2 months) and PGY-4 (1 month), delivered at Larkin Palm Springs - 'an ACHC-accredited Comprehensive Stroke Center and Primary Stroke Center' offering thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy - and at HCA Florida Kendall, 'a DNV-accredited Comprehensive Stroke Receiving Facility and Joint Commission certified Stroke Center' and Level I Trauma Center. The program director is himself an interventional neuroradiologist from the Emory/Grady neurovascular team.

differentiators.title: A required rotation explicitly built around underserved-population care
differentiators.student_explanation: The North Miami continuity clinic is described as serving 'an underserved area' where residents address 'challenges unique to underserved populations, such as limited resources, language and cultural barriers, and social determinants of health.' The primary hospital is also 'designated an "Area of Critical Need" by both the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) and the Florida Department of Health.' This is named, curricular safety-net training rather than a slogan.

differentiators.title: Behavioural neurology at an NIH-funded Alzheimer's centre
differentiators.student_explanation: Residents rotate at the Wien Center for Alzheimer's Disease & Memory Disorders at Mount Sinai, 'a leading participant in NIH-funded research initiatives, including Florida's Alzheimer's Disease Research Center', and the Cognitive and Movement Disorders months include 'assessment and monitoring of patients for new anti-amyloid therapies in Alzheimer's disease.' Cognitive neurology sits directly alongside your movement-disorders interest.

spanish_latino.summary: Two neurologists who precept required rotations have documented Spanish fluency on the program's own faculty page, and a required North Miami continuity clinic is explicitly built around underserved care including 'language and cultural barriers'. But the program publishes NO formal Medical Spanish curriculum - it answers 'no' to that question in its own 2026 AMA survey - no named Spanish-language clinical service, and no interpreter policy.
spanish_latino.explicitly_rejected_evidence: Five categories of tempting evidence were searched, found, and REFUSED. (1) MIAMI-DADE AND SOUTH MIAMI DEMOGRAPHICS. The single largest temptation in this ticket. That South Miami sits in a county with a very large Hispanic population is NOT evidence about this residency's training, and the contract forbids it absolutely. No demographic statistic appears anywhere in this dossier's Spanish assessment. (2) RESIDENT AND FACULTY SURNAMES. Many people on both rosters have Spanish surnames. No language, nationality, ethnicity or immigration inference was drawn from any name, for anyone. (3) RESIDENT SCHOOL COUNTRIES AS A SPANISH PROXY. Nine of 16 current residents trained in Ecuador and others in Venezuela and Cuba, so the peer group is very likely Spanish-speaking. I declined to count this: it is a fact about where residents were educated, not about Spanish-language training the PROGRAM provides, and counting it would let a recruitment pattern masquerade as a curriculum. It is reported in Domain 12 as composition, and deliberately not used here. (4) GENERIC DIVERSITY LANGUAGE. Phrases such as 'serving the diverse communities of Miami-Dade County' (HCA Kendall description), 'a diverse outpatient population' (Doral clinic) and 'diverse and vulnerable patient populations' were not counted as Spanish or Latino evidence; they are unfalsifiable boilerplate. (5) INSTITUTIONAL LANGUAGE PROGRAMS OUTSIDE THE RESIDENCY. No hospital-wide interpreter service or language-access statement was located, and had one been found it would not have counted as residency training content.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: No current resident trained at a Puerto Rico medical school, but one core faculty member - Dr Carrie Landess - is a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate, and she precepts a required continuity-clinic rotation. Graduate medical schools are not published, so alumni-level Puerto Rico representation could not be assessed.

program_name: Florida Atlantic University Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine Program — Neurology

fellowships.not_in_house_note: FAU sponsors six fellowships — Cardiovascular Disease, Emergency Medical Services, Geriatric Medicine, Hospice and Palliative Medicine, Pulmonary Critical Care Medicine and Vascular Surgery — and NONE is in neurology. There is therefore no in-house neurology subspecialty fellowship: no movement disorders, no MS/neuroimmunology, no epilepsy, no vascular neurology, no clinical neurophysiology and no neuromuscular fellowship at this institution. This is a positive enumeration from the institution's own complete fellowship list, corroborated by NRMP's program listing for FAU-Schmidt COM-FL (which carries no neurology subspecialty code) and by FREIDA's field_match_nrmp_adv_fellow = false.

board_pass.note: No ABPN pass rate is published by the program or FAU GME. FREIDA records that the program uses graduates' board certification pass rates as an internal program-evaluation measure, which the registry rendered as 'Board Certification Pass Rate Evaluation: Yes' — that is a method flag, not a rate.
board_pass.student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · The program does not publish a board certification pass rate.

graduate_fellowship_placements.name: Octavio Carranza-Renteria, M.D.
graduate_fellowship_placements.institution: University of Florida, Department of Neurology
graduate_fellowship_placements.note: The UF profile does not itself name FAU; the link to this program rests on FAU's own scholarly-activity page, which lists him as a resident author on AAN and ANA presentations and as the 2022 Gold Foundation Humanism & Excellence in Teaching Award recipient.

career_outcomes.name: Roxana Maria Dragomir, M.D.
career_outcomes.current_position: Board-certified neurologist at Marcus Neuroscience Institute, part of Baptist Health (Boynton Beach and Boca Raton), practising as a neurohospitalist with interests in stroke, neuromuscular emergencies and headache; also Clinical Affiliate Assistant Professor of Neurology at FAU Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine
career_outcomes.pathway: Retained at the primary teaching site as attending faculty without an intervening fellowship

outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: These are SELECTED EXAMPLES recovered from employers' own pages, not a cohort. The program publishes no alumni or placement page. Four cohorts have graduated (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025), roughly twelve people, and I established the current position of two of them. No fellowship-match rate, retention rate, or placement percentage can be computed from this and none should be inferred. A third graduate (Denis Babici, M.D.) appeared in search results as practising neurology and vascular neurology at Wellstar Health System, but the official employer page returned HTTP 404 when opened, so no placement is recorded for him.

named_faculty: Sameea Husain Wilson, D.O. — Director of Movement Disorder Neurology, Marcus Neuroscience Institute; Assistant Professor of Neurology, FAU; fellowship trained in Movement Disorders
movement_disorders.dedicated_clinic: A dedicated outpatient Movement Disorders clinic rotation is a REQUIRED part of the PGY-2 year, listed alongside Epilepsy/EEG and EMG/Neuromuscular on both the program index and the rotations page.
movement_disorders.resident_elective: 'Movement Disorders' is one of twelve named PGY-2 through PGY-4 electives.
movement_disorders.research: No movement-disorders-specific resident research track is published. Departmental neurodegeneration research sits in the David and Lynn Nicholson Center for Neurodegenerative Disease Research and the FAU Brain Institute.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: Exposure is required, not merely available: every resident rotates through a dedicated outpatient movement disorders clinic in PGY-2, and can add a movement disorders elective in PGY-2 through PGY-4. The teaching faculty member is the movement disorders service director at the primary teaching site with an FAU academic appointment, so the mentorship line is direct rather than nominal. Institutional capability is deeper than resident-facing structure in one respect — DBS, DUOPA pump, botulinum toxin and high-frequency ultrasound are all in the service's published armamentarium — but there is no movement disorders fellowship, no separately branded movement disorders centre, and no awarding-body designation.
movement_disorders.summary: Movement disorders is structurally embedded: a required PGY-2 outpatient movement disorders clinic, a PGY-2-4 elective, and a single fellowship-trained faculty member who directs the service at the primary teaching site. No fellowship and no formal designation.

named_faculty: Amy Wei-Hsin Laitinen, M.D. — Associate Program Director AND Director of Multiple Sclerosis and Neuroimmunology, Marcus Neuroscience Institute; Columbia neuroimmunology fellowship 2023; NMSS-supported Clinical MS Fellow; fluent in Spanish
Thomas Hammond, M.D., FAAN — FAU core faculty and FAU associate professor, clinically active in the Institute's MS program
Constance Katsafanas, D.O. — Program Director, published clinical focus includes multiple sclerosis
ms_neuroimmunology.dedicated_clinic: Dr. Laitinen's MS clinic at the Marcus Neuroscience Institute, with a co-located ground-floor outpatient neuro-infusion lab that administers IV therapies for multiple sclerosis, an in-house specialty pharmacy with an on-site clinical pharmacist, infusion and triage nurses, a nurse practitioner and a patient navigator.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_elective: 'Neuroimmunology/Multiple Sclerosis' is a named PGY-2 through PGY-4 elective, and was already on the elective list in FAU's 2018 accreditation announcement.
ms_neuroimmunology.research: As of April 2024 the MS research programme was described by its own director as still being assembled — a research officer, research coordinators and a dedicated research nurse in place, with clinical trials an expressed near-future intention. I am not recording an operating MS trials portfolio.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: The decisive structural fact is role overlap: the residency's Associate Program Director is the MS and neuroimmunology service director at the primary teaching site, which removes the usual distance between a capable service and a resident's access to it. But resident exposure is ELECTIVE rather than required — MS sits on the PGY-2-4 elective menu, unlike movement disorders which is a required PGY-2 rotation. So a resident must choose MS, and the mentor available to support that choice is unusually senior and directly involved in resident education. No MS fellowship exists here and no MS centre designation could be verified.
ms_neuroimmunology.summary: MS and neuroimmunology is strong because the residency's own Associate Program Director directs the MS and neuroimmunology service at the primary teaching site, with an MS clinic and co-located infusion centre. Resident exposure comes through a named elective rather than a required rotation, and there is no MS fellowship or verified centre designation.

research_opportunities: A four-year categorical curriculum with the internal medicine intern year built in, four months of inpatient neurology in PGY-1, required dedicated outpatient epilepsy, neuromuscular and movement disorders clinics in PGY-2, and a twelve-item neurology elective list in PGY-2 through PGY-4 that includes both movement disorders and neuroimmunology/MS. All PGY-4s serve as chief residents and overnight call is mostly home call.

salary_benefits.summary: FY26 stipends run $66,433 at PGY-1 to $74,791 at PGY-4, with up to four weeks paid time off, university-paid malpractice and long-term disability, cost-shared health and dental, free parking and an on-call meal allowance. The registry's salary figures are a full cycle stale and understate every year.

differentiators.title: A required movement disorders clinic in PGY-2, not just an elective
differentiators.student_explanation: Every resident here rotates through a dedicated outpatient Movement Disorders clinic during the PGY-2 year, listed on the program's own rotations page alongside Epilepsy/EEG and EMG/Neuromuscular. Most neurology programs make movement disorders an optional elective. If movement disorders is one of your two declared interests, this program builds it into the required curriculum rather than leaving it to chance.

differentiators.title: You would learn movement disorders from the person who runs the service
differentiators.student_explanation: Sameea Husain Wilson, D.O., is on the residency faculty roster as fellowship trained in Movement Disorders, and Baptist Health lists her as Director of Movement Disorder Neurology at the Marcus Neuroscience Institute and an assistant professor of neurology at FAU. Her published practice includes deep brain stimulation, botulinum toxin injection, the DUOPA pump and high-frequency ultrasound — the full modern movement-disorders toolkit, at the hospital where you would spend most of your time.

differentiators.title: The Associate Program Director is an MS and neuroimmunology subspecialist
differentiators.student_explanation: Amy Wei-Hsin Laitinen, M.D., is the residency's Associate Program Director and simultaneously the Director of Multiple Sclerosis and Neuroimmunology at the Marcus Neuroscience Institute. She did a Columbia neuroimmunology fellowship as a National MS Society-supported Clinical MS Fellow. For a student naming MS as an interest, the person who would shape your training is also the person who runs the MS service.

differentiators.title: A Spanish-speaking subspecialty mentor, documented by her institution
differentiators.student_explanation: Baptist Health's official profile for Dr. Laitinen states she is fluent in English, Spanish and Mandarin. That is a documented clinical language for the residency's Associate Program Director and MS service director — Spanish-language mentorship inside your exact subspecialty interest, attested by her employer rather than assumed from geography.

differentiators.title: A named Neuroimmunology/Multiple Sclerosis elective in PGY-2 through PGY-4
differentiators.student_explanation: The rotations page lists 'Neuroimmunology/Multiple Sclerosis' among twelve upper-year electives, and it has been on that list since the program was accredited in 2018. Combined with the MS clinic and the ground-floor infusion lab in the same building, an MS-interested resident can build real depth here in the upper years.

differentiators.title: One categorical code, filled three of three for six straight Match years
differentiators.student_explanation: NRMP's own Program Results list a single neurology code for this program, 1586180C0, with a quota of 3 and 3 filled in each of 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026. Because the only code carries the 'C' suffix, there is no Advanced code requiring you to separately match a preliminary year, and no Reserved or Physician code carrying NRMP's 'not available to senior medical students' footnote. One application, one code, PGY-1 entry.

differentiators.title: Step 2 is needed before ranking, not before applying or interviewing
differentiators.student_explanation: The program states 'Passing USMLE Step 2 or COMLEX Level 2 score posted before ranking' and 'A passing Step 2 or COMLEX 2 score is required to be ranked.' Nothing conditions application or an interview invitation on Step 2. A mid-October score arrives months before rank lists are certified in late February, so a late-September Step 2 sitting does not close this door.

differentiators.title: A current PGY-3 is a University of Puerto Rico School of Medicine graduate
differentiators.student_explanation: The program's own roster names a PGY-3 who graduated from the University of Puerto Rico School of Medicine, and FREIDA's arithmetic counts him among the program's U.S. MD graduates. This is a demonstrated pathway rather than an assumption: this program has already matched and is training a graduate of an LCME-accredited Puerto Rico medical school.

differentiators.title: Every PGY-4 serves as a chief resident
differentiators.student_explanation: The program states 'PGY-4 residents all serve as chief neurology residents', with the explicit aim of developing supervision and leadership skills. In a program taking three residents a year, that means a guaranteed chief-resident year rather than a competition for one or two slots — directly relevant if you have led a student interest group and want to keep building that.

differentiators.title: Mostly home call, with two weeks of in-house call per year
differentiators.student_explanation: The program describes overnight call as 'a hybrid model consisting mostly of home-call with 2 weeks of in-house call per year per PGY2-4 resident', and says a tele-stroke service covers stroke after 5 PM and on weekends. FREIDA reports no night float and 60 average duty hours per week in PGY-1. This is a concrete, published call structure rather than a vague wellness claim.

differentiators.title: The home base is a DNV-certified Comprehensive Stroke Center with a 20-bed neuro ICU
differentiators.student_explanation: Boca Raton Regional Hospital received Comprehensive Stroke Center certification from DNV GL Healthcare on July 27, 2020, the first in Palm Beach County, and had already been certified as a Thrombectomy-Capable Stroke Center by The Joint Commission in July 2019. The Marcus Neuroscience Institute houses a 20-bed neuro ICU and step-down unit, four ORs with intraoperative MRI and CT and a biplane angiography suite, and a four-room epilepsy monitoring unit that Baptist Health describes as the only EMU from West Palm Beach to Fort Lauderdale. Residents take daytime stroke call as part of that program.

spanish_latino.summary: The Associate Program Director — who is also the MS and neuroimmunology service director at the primary teaching site — is documented by her institution as fluent in Spanish, and the program publishes two of its twelve current residents as fluent in Spanish. There is no formal Medical Spanish curriculum.
spanish_latino.explicitly_rejected_evidence: I refused, and name each refusal because each was available: (a) Boca Raton and Palm Beach County Hispanic population demographics — I did not look them up and would not count them; contract law 5 and my tasking forbid it by name, and county demographics say nothing about a residency. (b) Surnames. Three people in this dossier carry Spanish surnames (residents Rodriguez and Canosa, graduate Carranza-Renteria). For Rodriguez and Canosa I counted the program's PUBLISHED fluency statement, not the name; for Carranza-Renteria, where no language is published, I counted nothing despite the surname and despite a Mexican medical school. (c) Baptist Health's Spanish-language corporate communications — the program director's press release is offered in English and Spanish versions and Baptist publishes extensive Spanish patient material system-wide across twelve hospitals from Miami-Dade to Palm Beach. That is marketing for a health system, not a feature of this residency's training environment, and an institutional language programme outside the residency is expressly excluded. (d) System-wide interpreter services — certainly present, but I found no residency-level documentation of interpreter training or language-concordant clinic assignment, so INTERPRETER_SERVICE is recorded nowhere. (e) 'We see an extensive case pathology with a diverse patient population' — the program's own FREIDA special-features text. A banned generic claim with no named mechanism; neither counted here nor used in why_this_program. (f) The Puerto Rico roster finding — recorded as a school-pathway precedent under domain 25, not double-counted as institutional Spanish capability.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: No Universidad Central del Caribe tie was found anywhere — no resident, faculty member, or program leader. The program does, however, currently train a graduate of the University of Puerto Rico School of Medicine, which is the first Puerto Rico medical school graduate identified in the Florida universe so far.
