board_pass.note: No board certification pass rate is published by the program, by Larkin or by FREIDA, and FREIDA's rendered Evaluations block records 'Graduates board certification pass rates | No' as a program-evaluation measure. The ABPN does not publish pass rates by individual residency program. Context: the first graduating cohort was a single resident in 2022-23, with 11 graduates in total across three years, so any rate would be statistically fragile. This must not be reported as a poor result or as any result.

outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: The alumni page is presented as COMPLETE COHORTS by graduation year, headed simply 'OUR GRADUATES', not as selected highlights: 2022-23 (1 graduate - Diyan Raza), 2023-24 (6 - Jeremy Eckes, Rusdany Collado, Sadek Debwan, Michael Wilson, Patrick Mercho, Michael Alosilla), 2024-25 (4 - Sam Kara, Marisol Trejos, Jordon Prosapio, Solomon Nittala). What is complete is therefore the NAME LIST; the OUTCOMES are entirely absent - not one fellowship, employer, practice, city or board status is given for any of the 11. So graduate_fellowship_placements and career_outcomes are empty because nothing is published, not because a selection was made. Cohort sizes of 1, 6 and 4 against 4 positions per year are irregular and unexplained, and no 2025-26 cohort is listed as of September 2026 although the roster shows a full PGY-4, so the page appears one cycle behind.

movement_disorders.resident_elective: A required block rotation titled 'Movement Disorder' appears in the PGY-2 year of the program's own published rotation schedule. It is a required block, not an elective. Duration, site and supervising faculty are not published.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: This program inverts the usual pattern and the distinction must be stated precisely. RESIDENT EXPOSURE IS ESTABLISHED: the program's own curriculum page lists 'Movement Disorder' as one of seven PGY-2 rotations, so every resident passes through a movement-disorders block. That is documented, required exposure -- materially stronger than a department that merely treats Parkinson's disease. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY IS NOT ESTABLISHED: none of the eight published department members is a movement-disorders specialist or has any movement-disorders fellowship or certification; no movement-disorders or Parkinson's clinic is named by the program, by Larkin Health System's neurology service page, or by any participating site; there is no movement-disorders fellowship at either Larkin campus; no movement-disorders research, faculty-scholar project or publication is published; and no formal designation of any kind was found. The honest characterisation is therefore: guaranteed rotational exposure, undocumented depth and undocumented mentorship. For an applicant whose stated interest is Movement Disorders, the rotation is a real positive and the absence of an identifiable movement-disorders mentor is a real limitation, and the two should be presented together.
movement_disorders.summary: A required PGY-2 'Movement Disorder' rotation gives every resident documented movement-disorders exposure, but the program publishes no movement-disorders faculty, clinic, fellowship or research, and no formal designation.

ms_neuroimmunology.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: Neither resident exposure nor institutional capability is established, and unlike movement disorders there is no offsetting positive. The full four-year rotation schedule contains no MS, neuroimmunology or demyelinating-disease block. None of the eight published department members has MS or neuroimmunology training or certification. No MS clinic or infusion service is named by the program, by Larkin Health System, or by any of the nine participating sites. There is no MS fellowship at either Larkin campus. No MS research is published. No National MS Society designation of any kind was found. The only routes to MS exposure that could exist here are the unspecified PGY-3 and PGY-4 'Elective' blocks and general ambulatory neurology, neither of which is documented as carrying MS content.
ms_neuroimmunology.summary: No MS or neuroimmunology rotation, faculty member, clinic, fellowship, research activity or designation is published for this program. This is Alejandra's other stated interest and the program appears not to address it.

research_opportunities: The program publishes a complete four-year block schedule with named subspecialty rotations including Movement Disorder, Sleep Medicine, Neuro-Ophthalmology, Epilepsy, NCV/EMG, Pediatric Neurology and Neuro-Rehabilitation, plus PGY-3 and PGY-4 electives. There is a night float system, no moonlighting, and no research rotation or research track.

salary_benefits.summary: No salary figure is published for this program. Medical insurance for residents is cost-shared between institution and resident - an improvement on the registry's reading - but disability and mental health coverage are recorded as Not Available, dental and life insurance are unpaid by the institution, and moonlighting is not permitted.
salary_benefits.absence_message: Research complete - The program does not publish a resident salary. FREIDA carries an explicit null for salary, vacation and sick days, records 'Data not provided by program' for employment policies, and Larkin's GME site has no benefits page.

differentiators.title: A required PGY-2 Movement Disorder rotation, named in the published block schedule
differentiators.student_explanation: The program's own curriculum page lists 'Movement Disorder' as one of seven PGY-2 rotations, alongside Sleep Medicine and Neuro-Ophthalmology. It is a required block rather than an elective, so every resident rotates through it. For someone with existing Parkinson's and movement-disorder exposure this is guaranteed, timetabled contact with the subspecialty in the second year - though be aware the program does not publish who supervises it or where it takes place, and no movement-disorders specialist appears on its faculty list.

differentiators.title: Interviews are conducted virtually, which removes a 1,190-mile trip
differentiators.student_explanation: FREIDA's current record lists this program's applicant interview format as Virtual. Because Hialeah is roughly 1,190 road miles from Houston and Florida is a secondary market rather than a first preference, a virtual interview means this program can be explored at no travel cost and without competing against Texas interview dates. Note this is a change from older data, which listed in-person interviews.

differentiators.title: A genuinely multi-site rotation structure across nine named training locations
differentiators.student_explanation: Rather than training in one building, residents rotate across nine named sites recorded with ACGME: the Palm Springs Campus hospital in Hialeah, Palmetto General Hospital, Larkin Community Hospital in South Miami, North Shore Hospital, West Gables Rehabilitation Hospital, Design Neuroscience Center in Doral, Advanced Neuroscience Network in Hialeah, Florida Sleep and Neuro Diagnostic Services, and a neuro-ophthalmology practice in Aventura. Several map directly onto named rotations, so the variety is structural rather than aspirational. Expect meaningful local travel between sites.

differentiators.title: A dedicated PGY-3 NCV/EMG block and a PGY-4 Epilepsy block, taught by ABPN-subspecialty-certified faculty
differentiators.student_explanation: The schedule sets aside whole blocks for nerve conduction studies and EMG in PGY-3 and for Epilepsy in PGY-4. Two department members hold ABPN certification in Epilepsy (Dr. Carlos Oliu, and Dr. Ramzy Medaa who is also certified in Child Neurology), so the epilepsy block is matched to identifiable expertise. Procedural neurophysiology time like this is not guaranteed at every community program.

differentiators.title: Stroke and neuro-ICU exposure in each of the final three years, with a dual-fellowship-trained vascular neurologist on faculty
differentiators.student_explanation: Inpatient Neurology with ICU and Stroke appears in PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4, so cerebrovascular and neurocritical exposure recurs rather than being a single rotation. Dr. Ritesh Kaushal trained at the University of Chicago in Neurology and then completed two fellowships at St Louis University, in Vascular Neurology and in Endovascular Surgical Neuroradiology - an unusually specific credential for a community program's faculty list.

differentiators.title: A neuro-rehabilitation thread, including a PGY-4 inpatient rehabilitation block and two rehabilitation-fellowship-trained faculty
differentiators.student_explanation: The PGY-4 year includes an Inpatient Neurology Rehabilitation block, West Gables Rehabilitation Hospital is a formal training site, and two department members completed Neurologic Rehabilitation fellowships at University of Miami / Jackson Memorial - the Program Director, Dr. Kester Nedd, and Dr. Bruce Rubin. This is the program's most distinctive and best-supported clinical identity, and it is relevant to movement disorders in that gait, balance and functional recovery are shared ground.

differentiators.title: A department with a clear University of Miami / Jackson Memorial training lineage
differentiators.student_explanation: Three of the eight published department members trained at University of Miami / Jackson Memorial Hospital - the Program Director in both residency and fellowship, Dr. Rubin in fellowship, and Dr. Carlos Oliu in both residency and an epilepsy fellowship. A fourth trained in Neurology at Columbia's Neurological Institute and a fifth at the University of Chicago. That is a specific, checkable mentorship lineage rather than a general claim about faculty quality.

differentiators.title: An in-house multidisciplinary Sleep Medicine fellowship connected to an actual PGY-2 sleep rotation
differentiators.student_explanation: The Palm Springs Campus sponsors an ACGME Sleep Medicine (Multidisciplinary) fellowship, and this residency independently has a PGY-2 Sleep Medicine rotation, advertises a sleep subspecialty clinic and lists a sleep and neurodiagnostic centre as a training site. Multidisciplinary sleep fellowships accept neurology graduates, so this is a real internal progression route. The campus also sponsors Pain Medicine and Addiction Medicine fellowships on the same basis.

differentiators.title: A published five-year graduation window and no gap-experience requirement for current graduates
differentiators.student_explanation: Eligibility requires graduation from medical school within the past five years, which a June 2027 graduate applying in the 2026-2027 cycle satisfies easily. The program's clinical-experience condition applies only to applicants with a gap of a year or more between graduation and residency, so it does not apply to someone entering directly. A Houston away rotation therefore counts as a strengthening credential, not a compliance requirement.

differentiators.title: A named Puerto Rico training tie inside the published department
differentiators.student_explanation: Dr. Odalys Frontela, listed among the program's current department members, completed her internship and Internal Medicine residency at Mayaguez Medical Center in Mayaguez, Puerto Rico. For a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate this is a small but genuine point of shared background in a department of eight, and the only Puerto Rico connection identifiable anywhere in this program. Note she is certified in Internal Medicine rather than Neurology.

spanish_latino.summary: The program's own current FREIDA survey answers 'No' to instruction in medical Spanish or other non-English language. No named Spanish-language clinical service, bilingual track, interpreter policy or documented community partnership tied to this residency was found.
spanish_latino.explicitly_rejected_evidence: FIVE CATEGORIES OF EVIDENCE WERE AVAILABLE AND I REFUSED ALL FIVE. (1) HIALEAH'S DEMOGRAPHICS. Hialeah is among the most heavily Spanish-speaking cities in the United States. Governance law 5 forbids inferring Spanish-language training value from city demographics, and the contract names Florida as the place where this temptation is maximal. A city's language profile is a fact about the city, not a curriculum, not a rotation and not a training commitment. Rejected outright. It would have been the easiest and most persuasive-sounding claim in this dossier and it is worth nothing. (2) THE HOSPITAL'S 'LARGELY BILINGUAL' CHARACTERISATION. A secondary encyclopedia source states that the hospital became largely bilingual in Spanish and English, and in Haitian Creole, because of demographic influx. Rejected on three independent grounds: it is a secondary source, not official; it describes the HOSPITAL'S general operating environment rather than the residency's training environment; and its own stated basis is demographic influx, which law 5 excludes. (3) RESIDENT AND FACULTY SURNAMES. The 16-resident roster and the 8-member faculty list contain names that a careless reader would treat as evidence of Spanish-language capability. Governance law 4 forbids inferring anything from a name, and I inferred nothing. No name anywhere in this dossier is used as evidence of language, nationality, ethnicity or immigration status. (4) A PHYSICIAN-DIRECTORY LANGUAGE FIELD FROM THE WRONG PROGRAM. Larkin Health System's neurology service page documents that Dr. Mohan Deochand offers services in 'English, Spanish'. Rejected twice over: he appears on the SIBLING South Miami program's faculty roster and not on this program's, so using him would be cross-program contamination; and in any case an individual physician's directory language field is not a residency curriculum, a formal Medical Spanish program or a documented service. (5) A GENERIC 'DIVERSE PATIENT POPULATION' FRAMING. The program's own home page speaks of 'rich and diversified clinical experiences'. That is boilerplate about case mix, says nothing about language, and is on the contract's banned-phrase list. Rejected. WHAT WOULD HAVE COUNTED, AND DOES NOT EXIST HERE: a named Spanish-language clinical service or clinic; a formal Medical Spanish curriculum or elective; a bilingual training track; a published interpreter-services policy governing the residency; or a documented community partnership tied to this residency. None was found, and the program itself answers No to the closest published question.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: No resident or faculty member is identifiable as a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate, and no Puerto Rico medical school is represented on the roster. One department member, Dr. Odalys Frontela, completed her internship and Internal Medicine residency in Mayaguez, Puerto Rico. The program's eligibility wording says 'United States/Canada' without naming Puerto Rico - an ambiguity worth flagging.

program_name: Memorial Healthcare System (Hollywood Florida) Program

fellowships.not_in_house_note: No neurology subspecialty fellowship of any kind is sponsored by Memorial Healthcare System. The complete MHS GME program inventory was enumerated two independent ways — the public 'Residency and Fellowship Programs' index page and a full parse of the 4,164-URL mhs.net sitemap, which yields every GME program directory on the site: allergy and immunology fellowship, anesthesiology residency, cardiac critical care fellowship, cardiovascular disease fellowship, emergency medicine residency, general surgery residency, hematology and medical oncology fellowship, infectious disease fellowship, internal medicine residency, NEUROLOGY RESIDENCY, non-operative pediatric orthopedics, obstetrics and gynecology residency, pediatric cardiology fellowship, pediatrics residency, pharmacy residency (PGY-1 and eight PGY-2 tracks), physical medicine, podiatry residency, psychiatry residency and transitional year residency. There is no vascular neurology, epilepsy, clinical neurophysiology, neuromuscular, neurocritical care, movement disorders, MS/neuroimmunology, headache, sleep or neuro-oncology fellowship. FREIDA's 2026 survey corroborates with field_match_nrmp_adv_fellow = false. NO FELLOWSHIP WAS INFERRED FROM A FACULTY MEMBER'S SPECIALTY — the division contains fellowship-trained epileptologists, vascular neurologists, neuromuscular specialists and a movement disorders specialist, and none of that was allowed to imply a fellowship program exists. Consequence for residents: subspecialty fel

board_pass.note: No ABPN pass rate published. The program reports to FREIDA that it uses graduates' board certification pass rates as a program-evaluation method, superseding the registry's 'Board Certification Pass Rate Evaluation: No'. With 12 graduates total since 2023, any published rate would rest on very small numbers.

graduate_fellowship_placements.graduate: Sydney Oraham, MD (published on the alumni page as Sydney Shaffer, MD, Class of 2025 — probable name change, identity confidence MEDIUM-HIGH)
graduate_fellowship_placements.evidence: Institutional provider profile listing 'Residency: Memorial Regional Hospital, 2025, Neurology' and 'Fellowships: UF, Office Of The Registar, 2026, Vascular Neurology'

career_outcomes.outcome: Retained by the sponsoring institution as a Neuro-Hospitalist at Memorial Division of Neurology after completing her UF vascular neurology fellowship

outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: The alumni page is a COMPLETE roster of all 12 graduates across the classes of 2023, 2024 and 2025, but it publishes only name, degree and medical school for each — no fellowship, no job, no location. The one placement above was reconstructed independently from the institution's provider directory and is a single data point out of twelve. It is NOT a placement rate, a fellowship-match rate or a retention rate, and no such rate is computable from public sources. The other eleven graduates' outcomes are genuinely unpublished.

named_faculty.name: Casey Young, MD
named_faculty.role: Movement Disorder, Neurology — Memorial Division of Neurology, Hollywood
named_faculty.fellowship: Mount Sinai Downtown, Movement Disorders Fellowship, 2025
named_faculty.residency: Columbia University Irving Medical Center, Neurology, 2023
named_faculty.research: Genetic Parkinson's disease; motor and non-motor phenotyping of GBA Parkinson's disease

named_faculty.name: George Diaz, MD
named_faculty.role: Associate Program Director; listed on the institution's Movement Disorders Program team
named_faculty.note: Listed on the Movement Disorders Program page but his published subspecialty certifications are vascular neurology, neuromuscular medicine, brain injury medicine and clinical neurophysiology — NOT movement disorders

named_faculty.name: Vineet Nadkarni, MD
named_faculty.role: General neurologist whose published areas of focus include 'Movement disorders: Treats Parkinson's disease, tremors and other movement disorders through medications and rehabilitation'

named_faculty.name: Christopher DeMassi, MD
named_faculty.role: Neurosurgery — listed on the Movement Disorders Program team; performs DBS
named_faculty.fellowship: University of Miami Miller School of Medicine

movement_disorders.dedicated_clinic: Yes at the institutional level: the 'Movement Disorders Program' is one of the named Programs and Services of Memorial Neuroscience Institute, treating Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, dystonia, Huntington's disease and Tourette syndrome, with deep brain stimulation offered through neurosurgery and adjunct rehabilitation (a supervised Parkinson's Disease Exercise Program and a Parkinson's Disease Therapy physical/speech therapy program) at Memorial Regional Hospital South. No movement-disorders CLINIC is named anywhere in the residency's published rotation grid.
movement_disorders.resident_elective: Not named. The published four-year rotation grid contains no movement disorders block and no movement disorders clinic. PGY-4 carries 'Elective (3 blocks)' with no menu of electives published, and PGY-2/3/4 carry a combined 7 blocks of 'Ambulatory/Specialty clinics' whose constituent clinics are not itemised. A movement disorders experience could plausibly sit inside either, but nothing published establishes it.
movement_disorders.research: Casey Young, MD publishes on GBA-1 Parkinson's disease (presentations to the Silverstein Foundation Fellow Research Update Meeting, Montreal, June 2025; GBA1 Canada Meeting at the Montreal Neurological Institute-Hospital, June 2024) and on Parkinson's epidemiology in Hawaii. No resident co-authorship or resident research involvement in movement disorders is published, and FREIDA's 2026 survey sets field_research_rotation = 'Not available'.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: THE TWO ARE SHARPLY DIFFERENT HERE, AND THE GAP RUNS AGAINST THE RESIDENT. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY IS REAL AND RECENTLY STRENGTHENED: a named Movement Disorders Program, a fellowship-trained movement disorders neurologist (Casey Young, MD, Mount Sinai movement disorders fellowship completed 2025) hired into the division, an active DBS pathway with neurosurgery, dedicated Parkinson's exercise and therapy rehabilitation programs, and a stated scope covering Huntington's disease, dystonia and Tourette syndrome. DOCUMENTED RESIDENT EXPOSURE IS ESSENTIALLY ABSENT FROM THE PUBLIC RECORD: movement disorders is NOT among the six subspecialty strengths the program names for itself ('vascular neurology, epilepsy, neuroimmunology, neuromuscular disease, headache, and cognitive/behavioral neurology' — the program's own sentence, which omits movement disorders); there is no movement disorders rotation, clinic or elective in the published PGY-1 to PGY-4 grid; Casey Young does not appear on the residency faculty page at all; the Movement Disorders Program page names no residents, fellows or trainees; and the program sponsors no movement disorders fellowship. The honest reading is that a resident here would have institutional access to movement disorders patients and to a fellowship-trained specialist, but the program has published no structured movement disorders training experience. For an applicant whose stated interest is movement disorders this is the single most important gap in this dossier and it should be raised directly with the program.
movement_disorders.summary: Institutional movement-disorders capability is genuine — a named Movement Disorders Program, a DBS pathway, Parkinson's rehabilitation programs, and a movement-disorders-fellowship-trained neurologist hired in 2025. Documented resident exposure is not: there is no movement disorders rotation, clinic or elective in the published four-year grid, movement disorders is absent from the program's own list of its strengths, and the movement specialist is not on the residency faculty page. No Parkinson's Foundation, HDSA or CurePSP designation exists.

named_faculty.name: Buse Sengul, MD
named_faculty.role: PROGRAM DIRECTOR of this residency and the institution's MS/neuroimmunology specialist
named_faculty.fellowship: University of Florida College of Medicine, 2019 — MS-focused training
named_faculty.self_description: 'I am a neurologist and neuroimmunologist at Memorial Neuroscience Institute. I specialize in caring for patients with multiple sclerosis and neuroimmunologic disorders, such as neuromyelitis optica, stiff person syndrome, neurosarcoidosis, acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) and transverse myelitis.'
named_faculty.research: 'My research interests mirror my clinical specialties and include multiple sclerosis symptom control and treatment options.' Two Gordon Multiple Sclerosis Research Awards, Temple University Hospital, 2017 and 2018.

named_faculty.name: George Diaz, MD
named_faculty.role: Associate Program Director; listed on the Multiple Sclerosis Center team page

named_faculty.name: Vineet Nadkarni, MD
named_faculty.role: General neurologist whose published areas of focus include 'Neuroimmune diseases: Cares for multiple sclerosis and other diseases that affect how the brain and immune system interact'

named_faculty.name: Jada Santos, PsyD
named_faculty.role: Neuropsychology — published areas of focus include Multiple Sclerosis; documented Spanish

named_faculty.name: Fawad Yousuf, MD
named_faculty.role: Listed on the residency faculty page as 'Neurohospitalist, Neuroimmunology' (fellowship University of Miami / Jackson Memorial Hospital). CAVEAT: he does not appear in the institution's current Memorial Division of Neurology provider cross-links, so his current status is uncertain.

ms_neuroimmunology.dedicated_clinic: Yes — the 'Memorial Neuroscience Institute Multiple Sclerosis Center', a named center within the institute. Its page states it 'offers leading-edge treatments for MS and other neuroimmune disorders' and lists medication therapy management, neuropsychology, rehabilitation, disease-modifying medications, neurorehabilitation, integrative therapies and emotional support. On infusions, verbatim: 'Medication infusions are often part of MS care. Our team helps coordinate infusions through Memorial Healthcare System, other infusion centers or at home.'
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_elective: Not itemised as an MS block. The published grid gives PGY-2 'Ambulatory/Specialty clinics (2.5 blocks)', PGY-3 'Ambulatory/Specialty clinics (3 blocks)' and PGY-4 'Ambulatory/Specialty clinics (1.5 blocks)' — 7 blocks total — plus PGY-4 'Elective (3 blocks)'. Neither the specialty clinics nor the electives are broken out by subspecialty, so an MS clinic experience is highly plausible but not published.
ms_neuroimmunology.research: The Program Director's own research interests are in MS symptom control and treatment options. No MS clinical trial portfolio, no resident MS research output and no MS research infrastructure specific to the residency was found. FREIDA's 2026 survey sets field_research_rotation = 'Not available' with field_research_rotation_duration = 0, although the program page states 'Our Office of Human Research will assist residents with the development of research projects and submission to the IRB.'
ms_neuroimmunology.formal_designation: The institution states a National MS Society designation. VERBATIM from the Memorial Neuroscience Institute Multiple Sclerosis Center page, fetched and read directly: 'Memorial Neuroscience Institute has been recognized by the National MS Society as a Center for Comprehensive MS Care.' And on the same page: 'As a recognized Center for Comprehensive MS Care, we offer a wide range of treatments, including the latest disease-modifying medications.' AWARDING-BODY CHECK — PARTIAL ONLY, AND STATED AS SUCH: 'Center for Comprehensive MS Care' is the correct name of the National MS Society's top tier under its Partners in MS Care program — the identical phrase is used in designation announcements by UNC Department of Neurology, UC Davis Health, UAB and Hackensack Meridian, which corroborates the naming. HOWEVER, the National MS Society's own site is a JavaScript single-page application that returns only a 2.2 MB shell with no rendered content to non-browser clients, and its partner directory could not be reached; three candidate directory URLs returned 404 or an empty shell. Memorial's specific listing in an NMSS-hosted directory was therefore NOT independently confirmed. The designation is reported as an institutional claim whose wording matches the awarding body's official tier name, with the verification gap named openly rather than papered over.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: CAPABILITY AND RESIDENT EXPOSURE ARE UNUSUALLY WELL ALIGNED HERE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE MOVEMENT DISORDERS PICTURE AT THE SAME PROGRAM. Institutional capability: a named MS Center with an asserted National MS Society Center for Comprehensive MS Care recognition, disease-modifying therapy, infusion coordination, MS-focused neuropsychology (Jada Santos PsyD) and rehabilitation. The mechanism that connects it to residents is structural rather than inferred: the PROGRAM DIRECTOR HERSELF is the MS and neuroimmunology specialist, so residents are supervised and evaluated by the institution's MS lead, and 'neuroimmunology' is one of only six subspecialty strengths the program names for itself on its welcome page. What is still MISSING, and why this is MODERATE rather than STRONG: no MS or neuroimmunology block appears by name in the published four-year rotation grid; the MS Center page mentions no residents, fellows or trainees; there is no MS or neuroimmunology fellowship; and no resident MS scholarly output is published. So the alignment is real but unquantified — a resident's MS exposure here depends on the ambulatory/specialty clinic assignment and on the PD's own clinic, neither of which is published in detail.
ms_neuroimmunology.summary: MS and neuroimmunology is a genuine strength. The Program Director is herself a fellowship-trained MS neuroimmunologist, 'neuroimmunology' is one of six subspecialty strengths the program names for itself, and there is a named Multiple Sclerosis Center that states National MS Society recognition as a Center for Comprehensive MS Care. Rated MODERATE rather than STRONG because no MS block appears by name in the published rotation grid, there is no MS fellowship, and the NMSS listing could not be confirmed on the Society's own site.

research_opportunities: A 4-year categorical curriculum in 4-week blocks: a PGY-1 internship with 3 neurology blocks, then heavy inpatient consult service with a night-float system, 4 blocks of EEG/epilepsy monitoring unit across PGY-2 to PGY-4, 2 blocks of EMG/neuromuscular, 3 blocks of pediatric neurology at Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital, 1 block each of neuro-ICU, neuroradiology, neuro-rehabilitation and neuropathology, 7 blocks of ambulatory/specialty clinics and 3 PGY-4 elective blocks.

salary_benefits.summary: Resident salaries run from about $61,755 at PGY-1 to about $69,118 at PGY-4, with 25 days of paid leave that covers vacation, sick time AND holidays combined. An important change from the registry: in the program's 2026 FREIDA survey, health, dental, disability and mental-health coverage are now 'Institution & Resident Share Cost' rather than fully institution-paid; only group life remains fully paid.

differentiators.title: An NAEC-verified Level 4 adult epilepsy center, and four resident blocks inside it
differentiators.student_explanation: Memorial Comprehensive Epilepsy Program is listed in the National Association of Epilepsy Centers' own public directory as a 'Level 4 Adult Epilepsy Center' at 3501 Johnson Street, Hollywood — the address of Memorial Regional Hospital. That is the highest NAEC accreditation level, and it was confirmed in NAEC's own listing rather than taken from the hospital's word. The residency puts four 4-week blocks in the EEG / epilepsy monitoring unit across PGY-2 to PGY-4 and runs a dedicated EEG workshop in the didactic series, so this is the one subspecialty where institutional accreditation and resident rotation time line up exactly.

differentiators.title: The Program Director is a fellowship-trained MS neuroimmunologist
differentiators.student_explanation: Buse Sengul, MD completed MS-focused fellowship training at the University of Florida and describes herself as 'a neurologist and neuroimmunologist at Memorial Neuroscience Institute,' treating multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica, stiff person syndrome, neurosarcoidosis, ADEM and transverse myelitis. Her research interests are in MS symptom control and treatment. For someone who wants MS as a career, the person who runs the residency is the person who does the MS. 'Neuroimmunology' is also one of only six subspecialty strengths the program names for itself.

differentiators.title: A Universidad Central del Caribe graduate is on the adult neurology faculty
differentiators.student_explanation: Ana Coronado, MD earned her medical degree at Universidad Central del Caribe in 2017 and did her internal medicine internship at Universidad Central Del Caribe Escuela De Medicina in 2018, then completed neurology residency at Hahnemann and Temple and a headache fellowship at Ohio State. She now practises headache medicine at Memorial Division of Neurology's Weston clinic and is listed on the residency's own faculty page. She is the only UCC-trained faculty member identified at any Florida adult neurology program in this research wave, and she is a concrete person who took the same route out of the same school.

differentiators.title: A second Puerto Rico medical school is represented on the faculty
differentiators.student_explanation: Axel Baez-Lugo, MD earned his medical degree at Ponce Health Sciences University in 2020, completed neurology residency at the Medical College of Georgia in 2024 and a pain medicine fellowship at the University of South Florida in 2025, and practises at Memorial's Pembroke Pines neurology clinic. Two of the eighteen clinicians in this adult neurology division trained at LCME-accredited Puerto Rico medical schools.

differentiators.title: The Associate Program Director speaks Spanish and runs the satellite clinic network
differentiators.student_explanation: George Diaz, MD is Associate Program Director of this residency and simultaneously 'Director, Outpatient Satellite Neurology Clinics.' The institution's own provider directory documents his languages as Spanish and Portuguese. He is board certified in neurology, vascular neurology, neuromuscular medicine, brain injury medicine and clinical neurophysiology, and writes that he 'worked in tele-neurology to improve access to care to patients in areas underserved by neurologists.' He practises at the Miami, Aventura and Hialeah satellite clinics — the outpatient system that the residency's seven ambulatory blocks draw on.

differentiators.title: Seven of eighteen adult neurology clinicians have Spanish documented by the institution
differentiators.student_explanation: Memorial's provider directory publishes a languages field for each clinician. Within Memorial Division of Neurology, Spanish is documented for George Diaz MD, Axel Baez-Lugo MD, Maike Blaya MD, Sean Kenniff MD, Madiley Broz PsyD, Amina Rivero-Barba PsyD and Jada Santos PsyD — seven of eighteen, including the Associate Program Director and all three neuropsychologists. This is the institution's own published record of who speaks Spanish, not an assumption from anyone's name or medical school.

differentiators.title: A single Active categorical NRMP code with no eligibility trap
differentiators.student_explanation: The program's own admissions page states 'NRMP Number: 2085180C0' and 'We offer 4 categorical positions for years PGY1 to PGY4.' The NRMP Program Directory lists that one code as Active and categorical. There is no Advanced track requiring you to separately match a preliminary year, and no 'R' (reserved/physician) code — R positions are reserved for applicants with prior graduate medical education and are not available to senior medical students. FREIDA's 2026 survey confirms it: PGY-1 categorical true, prelim false, PGY-2 advanced false, PGY-2 reserved false, and previous GME not required. One code, one application, no barrier for a graduating senior.

differentiators.title: No minimum USMLE score, and no published Step 2 timing barrier
differentiators.student_explanation: The program states plainly 'We do not have a minimum USMLE score.' Its application-requirements list marks Step 1 as '(required)' but asks for Step 2 results only '(if available)' — and in its 2026 FREIDA survey the program answered No to requiring Step 2 before an interview. If your Step 2 CK result arrives in mid-October, nothing this program has published stands between you and application review or an interview invitation.

differentiators.title: Puerto Rico graduates enter through the U.S. eligibility pathway, with no ECFMG certificate needed
differentiators.student_explanation: The MHS GME 'Resident/Fellow Recruitment and Selection' policy, revised May 2026, sets out its first eligibility pathway as 'Be a graduate of an accredited medical, podiatric, or dental school in the United States or Canada.' Puerto Rico is part of the United States and Universidad Central del Caribe is LCME-accredited, so that pathway applies and the separate ECFMG requirement — which the program limits to 'a graduate of a foreign medical school' — does not. Worth knowing because the policy never names Puerto Rico explicitly, so it is a point to state clearly in your own application materials.

differentiators.title: Six training sites inside ten miles, including a Level 1 trauma center
differentiators.student_explanation: The program page lists Memorial Hospital West, Memorial Regional Hospital, Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital, Memorial Regional Hospital South, Memorial Miramar Hospital and Memorial Pembroke Hospital, 'all within 10 miles.' FREIDA's institution records show Memorial Regional Hospital at 1,013 beds with an average daily census of 653, 32,611 annual admissions and a Level 1 trauma center designation, and Memorial Hospital West at 486 beds. Multiple sites without long commutes, and case volume that a four-resident-per-year program does not have to share widely.

differentiators.title: Four residents a year and a faculty-to-resident ratio of 0.80:1
differentiators.student_explanation: The program writes that 'Our four resident per year program allows us to get to know each of our residents on a personal level.' FREIDA's 2026 survey puts the full-time faculty-to-resident ratio at 0.80:1 with 13 physician faculty and 2 non-physician faculty against 16 residents. This is a small-cohort program where a resident with a specific subspecialty interest can realistically ask one of thirteen attendings to supervise it.

differentiators.title: A public safety-net system where residents would train, not a rotation elsewhere
differentiators.student_explanation: Memorial Healthcare System is the South Broward Hospital District, a public special taxing district — FREIDA's own institution records name the sites 'Memorial Regional Hospital-South Broward Hospital District' and 'Memorial Hospital West-South Broward Hospital District.' Memorial Regional reported 7,560 Medicaid discharges against 32,611 admissions and 145,461 emergency visits. The admissions page states 'We require 100% of your training to occur at MHS,' so this is where all four years happen rather than a block rotated into.

spanish_latino.summary: There is real, documented Spanish-language clinical capacity inside this residency's own training environment: the institution's provider directory publishes a languages field, and Spanish is documented for 7 of the 18 clinicians in Memorial Division of Neurology — including the Associate Program Director of the residency and all three neuropsychologists. Set against that, there is NO formal Medical Spanish curriculum, NO named Spanish-language clinic or service line, and NO bilingual track. Rated MODERATE: a genuinely bilingual clinical workplace with bilingual residency leadership, but no structured Spanish-language training product.
spanish_latino.explicitly_rejected_evidence: Five categories of evidence were available and were refused. (1) BROWARD COUNTY AND HOLLYWOOD/HIALEAH DEMOGRAPHICS — refused outright under governance law 5 and contamination guard 7. No population percentage for Broward County, Hollywood, Hialeah, Miami-Dade or South Florida appears anywhere in this dossier as evidence of Spanish-language training value. The temptation was concrete: the Associate Program Director's satellite clinics include a Hialeah site, and it would have been easy to reach for Hialeah's Hispanic population share. That figure is not evidence about this residency and was not used. (2) THE 46% HISPANIC PATIENT-MIX FIGURE FOR SOUTH BROWARD COMMUNITY HEALTH SERVICES — a search result attributed to an MHS Community Health Needs Assessment reports that SBCHS serves a population that is 46% Hispanic with 84% uninsured. Refused for two independent reasons: the source is a 2016-2018 CHNA document and is plainly out of cycle, and more importantly there is NO evidence that neurology residents rotate at SBCHS or on the mobile health centers — the published four-year rotation grid contains no community clinic block, and the admissions page states all training occurs at MHS facilities. A patient-mix statistic for a clinical service the residents do not demonstrably staff is not evidence about their training. (3) SURNAMES — refused under governance law 4. Several division clinicians and residents have Spanish surnames. In particular Ana Coronado MD (a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate practising in Weston) publishes NO language field at all, and Seth Tarras MD and Casey Young MD likewise publish none; for all three, Spanish is recorded as unknown rather than true. It would have been trivially easy, and wrong, to credit Dr Coronado with Spanish on the strength of her name and her medical school. Similarly, no resident's language ability was inferred from a name — the program publishes no resident language data at all. (4) GENERIC DIVERSITY LANGUAGE — the program's own welcome page says 'Great patient diversity and an exciting range of pathology' and the interpreter services page says Memorial 'is located within a vibrant multicultural community in South Florida.' Neither is evidence of Spanish-language clinical training and neither was counted toward strength; the interpreter page was counted only for its concrete operational statements about 24-hour service and trained bilingual staff interpreters. (5) A LANGUAGE FILTER ON THE PUBLIC 'FIND A DOCTOR' SEARCH — the institution's provider search offers a languages filter, which could have been used to generate a system-wide count of Spanish-speaking physicians across all of Memorial Healthcare System. That number would describe a 4,000-plus-employee multi-hospital system, not a neurology residency, so the count was deliberately restricted to the 18 clinicians of Memorial Division of Neurology, each profile opened individually.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: No current resident or published alumnus of this program attended a Puerto Rico medical school. But the adult neurology faculty contains a genuine Universidad Central del Caribe tie — Ana Coronado, MD, UCC class of 2017 with her internship also at UCC — plus a Ponce Health Sciences University graduate, Axel Baez-Lugo, MD.

program_name: Palmetto General Hospital Program

in_house.sponsor_institution: Palmetto General Hospital (same ACGME Sponsoring Institution as the residency)
in_house.acgme_or_non_acgme: ACGME-accredited (ACGME ID 1881118001)
in_house.status: Active and accepting - FREIDA survey received 2026-07-21 with field_accepting_current_year = true; participates in the NRMP Main Match and ERAS

board_pass.note: No program-level ABPN pass rate is published, and ABPN does not release program-level rates publicly. FREIDA confirms the program uses graduates' board certification pass rates as one of its own evaluation metrics but reports no number. With a first appointment year of 2021 and quotas of 1 per year through 2024, the board-eligible graduate count is in the low single digits, so no meaningful rate could exist yet.
board_pass.student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - no board pass rate is published for this program, and the certifying board does not release program-level rates.

graduate_fellowship_placements.name: Mohammed Shan Uddin
graduate_fellowship_placements.medical_school: Florida International University Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine (US MD)
graduate_fellowship_placements.prior_training: Transitional Year internship, HCA Florida Orange Park Hospital, 2020
graduate_fellowship_placements.fellowship: Neuro-Ophthalmology, Weill Cornell Medicine, 2025 (also served as Instructor in Ophthalmology)
graduate_fellowship_placements.current_position: Neuro-Ophthalmology and Neurology, Hackensack Meridian Health

outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: Exactly one graduate could be documented, and he was found by targeted search of an outside employer's faculty page rather than drawn from any published cohort list - the program has no alumni page and never has, on the evidence of the full Wayback index for its former website. That single example (2024 chief resident, Weill Cornell neuro-ophthalmology fellowship 2025, now Hackensack Meridian faculty) is therefore subject to strong survivorship bias: graduates who did not obtain competitive fellowships or academic appointments are systematically harder to find. It establishes a ceiling, not a distribution. Total graduates to date are very few - NRMP quotas were 1 per year for appointment years 2021-2024 and 2 for 2025-2026 - so no placement rate is computed and none should be inferred.

movement_disorders.resident_elective: 'Movement Clinic' appears verbatim in the elective list of the program's own Neurology Residency Block Schedule PDF dated 2020-03-12 and in the archived program FAQ. Elective blocks sit in PGY-3 (2 blocks) and PGY-4 (3 blocks). No clinic name, location, attending, volume or objectives are published for it.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: Institutional capability in movement disorders could not be established at all: the hospital's own neurology service page describes only stroke, endovascular neurosurgery and the BrainPath subcortical approach, and the institution's complete eight-programme ACGME portfolio contains no movement-disorders fellowship. Resident exposure is limited to an optional senior elective named 'Movement Clinic' in a six-year-old programme document whose host site is now a parked domain. The program director is vascular- and neurocritical-care-trained; no movement-disorders capability was inferred from him or from anyone else. A resident wanting movement disorders here would be relying on one unverified elective line, not on a service.
movement_disorders.summary: A single elective line - 'Movement Clinic' - in the program's own 2020 block schedule is the entire movement-disorders evidence base. No dedicated clinic, no named faculty, no fellowship, no research and no formal designation.

ms_neuroimmunology.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: Neither institutional capability nor resident exposure could be established. The program's 17-item elective list contains no MS, neuroimmunology, neuroinflammation or infusion option; the PGY2-4 block rotations named in the FAQ contain no MS rotation; the hospital's neurology service page does not mention multiple sclerosis, demyelinating disease or an infusion centre; and the institution's complete ACGME portfolio (eight programmes, enumerated directly from FREIDA's JSON:API) contains no neuroimmunology or MS fellowship. I opened no page describing Palmetto General as a National MS Society Comprehensive Care Center or a Partners in MS Care site, and I therefore assert no such designation.
ms_neuroimmunology.summary: No MS or neuroimmunology training pathway exists at this program - no clinic, no elective, no faculty, no research, no fellowship and no NMSS designation. For one of Alejandra's two stated subspecialty interests, this is a genuine and material gap.

research_opportunities: This is a categorical four-year program with a heavily internal-medicine PGY-1 at Palmetto General, then three neurology years of monthly blocks covering inpatient neurology, consults, neuro ICU, outpatient neurology, EEG, EMG, neuroimaging, clinical psychiatry, neurosurgery and pediatric neurology, with a required 8-week research rotation and a substantial elective allowance in PGY-3 and PGY-4. The continuity clinic is one half-day a week at a private neurology office in Miami. All of the detailed curriculum evidence comes from the program's own documents, which are now reachable only through a web archive.

salary_benefits.summary: Salaries are $53,066 (PGY-1), $55,534 (PGY-2), $58,002 (PGY-3) and $60,470 (PGY-4), unchanged between the 2025 and 2026 survey cycles. Paid vacation is 16 days in PGY-1 and 20 days thereafter. Health, dental, life and disability coverage is cost-shared between institution and resident; dependent and domestic-partner medical coverage is available but not paid by the institution. Perks are free parking and an on-call meal allowance, and moonlighting is permitted.

differentiators.title: An in-house ACGME Vascular Neurology fellowship at the same sponsoring institution
differentiators.student_explanation: Palmetto General sponsors its own ACGME-accredited Vascular Neurology fellowship (ACGME 1881118001, one position, program director Roberto Sanchez, MD), which filed a current FREIDA survey on 2026-07-21 and is accepting applicants. A resident here trains inside an institution that also trains a stroke fellow, which is unusual for a community program of this size and gives you an internal pathway if stroke becomes your direction.

differentiators.title: Six consecutive fully-matched years in the NRMP Main Match
differentiators.student_explanation: NRMP's published program-level results show this program offered and filled every position it had in six straight appointment years: 1 of 1 in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024, then 2 of 2 in 2025 and 2 of 2 in 2026. For a small community program that came through two ownership changes and a parent-company bankruptcy in that same window, an unbroken fill record is a concrete stability signal.

differentiators.title: Categorical four-year appointment on a single application
differentiators.student_explanation: The NRMP code is 2121180C0 - a C, meaning categorical. You apply once and the appointment covers all four years including the PGY-1 internal medicine year at the same hospital. The program's own FAQ says it directly: 'You only need to submit one application for the Neurology program. This application serves for the four years of training.' There is no Advanced or Reserved code here, so you do not have to separately match a preliminary year and you are not caught by NRMP's rule that Reserved positions are not available to senior medical students.

differentiators.title: One-to-one teaching by design, in the program's own words
differentiators.student_explanation: In its 2026 FREIDA survey the program describes itself as providing 'an excellent one-to-one teaching experience while in service at the hospital or clinics.' That is structurally credible rather than just a slogan: with two residents per year and a single continuity clinic that schedules no more than one resident per day, you are rarely competing for procedures, consults or attending attention.

differentiators.title: High-acuity stroke volume at a certified Comprehensive Stroke Center, with code-stroke responsibility as a resident
differentiators.student_explanation: The hospital's neurology page states it 'is a Comprehensive Stroke Center' certified by The Joint Commission and the AHA/ASA, and lists endovascular neurosurgery and a 'BrainPath' subcortical approach among its services. The program's FAQ puts residents at the front of that work: on call you 'take all code strokes, new consults, and pages' from 7am to 7pm. Verify the certification's current status with the program, because the hospital's page also contains dated phrasing from an earlier ownership era.

differentiators.title: A required 8-week research rotation and a named research outlet
differentiators.student_explanation: FREIDA records the research rotation as 'Required' with a duration of 8 weeks, and the block grid shows dedicated research blocks in PGY-2 and PGY-4 marked 100% research. The program also names its own venue: residents are expected to present at 'the PGH research symposium' as well as at local, regional and national conferences. Protected research time is written into the schedule rather than left to be negotiated.

differentiators.title: Elective-heavy senior years, including a 'Movement Clinic' elective
differentiators.student_explanation: The program's block schedule gives PGY-3 two and PGY-4 three elective blocks, and says PGY-3 and PGY-4 residents 'will have more elective blocks so that they may fine tune their training for their specific interests and potential fellowship.' The published elective list includes a 'Movement Clinic' and a 'Vascular Clinic' alongside EEG, EMG, neuro-ophthalmology, neuromuscular, sleep and interventional neurology. For a movement-disorders interest this is the one available lever - but it is one elective line in a 2020 document, not a movement-disorders program, and you should ask whether the Movement Clinic elective still runs.

differentiators.title: A documented graduate placement into a Weill Cornell subspecialty fellowship
differentiators.student_explanation: A 2024 graduate of this residency, who served as its chief resident, completed a neuro-ophthalmology fellowship at Weill Cornell Medicine in 2025 and is now on faculty at Hackensack Meridian Health - documented on his employer's own provider profile. One graduate is not a placement rate, but it establishes that a resident from this program has cleared a competitive academic subspecialty bar.

differentiators.title: No required away rotation, no supplemental application, and an explicit no-score-cutoff stance
differentiators.student_explanation: FREIDA records no required away rotation and no supplemental ERAS application for the next cycle, and the program's own FAQ states 'We do not have a certain cutoff for scores in regards to Board exams' and that applicants who did not pass on the first attempt are 'not excluded', with each application 'evaluated on an individual basis'. That is a low-friction application and a stated whole-file review, which matters when a Step 2 CK result will land in mid-October.

differentiators.title: Interview odds that are unusually favourable for the specialty
differentiators.student_explanation: The program reports 15 interviews conducted for 2 first-year positions in the most recent cycle - roughly 7.5 interviews per position, where competitive neurology programs commonly run many times that. If you receive an interview here, the conditional odds are materially better than at a large academic department.

differentiators.title: Pediatric neurology and clinical psychiatry blocks at named external sites
differentiators.student_explanation: Rather than leaving breadth to chance, the block schedule assigns pediatric neurology to a named second site, Kidz Medical Services, in PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4, and schedules a clinical psychiatry block in PGY-3. Those are ACGME-required neurology competencies delivered through identified rotations rather than as ad hoc coverage.

spanish_latino.summary: No formal Medical Spanish curriculum, no bilingual track and no named Spanish-language clinical service - the program answers 'no' to FREIDA's Medical Spanish question in both survey cycles. What can be documented is indirect: a free hospital-wide interpreter service at the training site, a high-Medicaid safety-net patient population, and a residency continuity clinic based in the private office of a named neurologist whom physician directories describe as Spanish-fluent.
spanish_latino.explicitly_rejected_evidence: REFUSED, item by item. (1) HIALEAH'S DEMOGRAPHICS. Hialeah is among the most heavily Spanish-speaking cities in the United States, and it would have been effortless to convert that into a Spanish-training claim. It is not evidence about this residency and it is not counted - not the city, not Miami-Dade County, and not the phrase 'greater Miami'. (2) SURNAMES. Several individuals connected to this program have Spanish surnames. No language ability, ethnicity, nationality or immigration status was inferred from any name; the only language attributions recorded anywhere in this dossier come from pages that explicitly list languages spoken. (3) THE PROGRAM'S OWN 'DIVERSE POPULATION' TEXT. FREIDA field_special_features says 'An extensive population to learn from, with a very diverse range of neurological diseases', and the block schedule says continuity clinic exposes residents to 'a diverse patient panel'. 'Diverse' there refers to disease variety and is generic besides; it is not Spanish or Latino evidence and was not counted. (4) THE HOSPITAL'S CHARITY-CARE AND NO-SURPRISES-ACT POSTINGS and its 'Nondiscrimination Notice and Language Assistance Services' footer link - these are federally mandated compliance notices present at essentially every US hospital, and they were not counted as a language program. (5) THIRD-PARTY 'CULTURALLY COMPETENT' MARKETING. Multiple quarantined aggregator pages describe this as a program 'designed to train culturally competent and skilled neurologists'. That sentence appears on no program-authored source I could open, it recurs verbatim across commercial sites, and it was not counted. (6) LARKIN COMMUNITY HOSPITAL'S content. Larkin operates two Adult Neurology programs in this same metropolitan area, one of them in Hialeah itself, and its GME site publishes far more about its faculty and curriculum. Nothing from Larkin was imported into this domain or any other. (7) INSTITUTIONAL LANGUAGE PROGRAMS OUTSIDE THE TRAINING ENVIRONMENT - none were found, and none were manufactured.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: No connection to Universidad Central del Caribe or to any Puerto Rico medical school could be established - not among residents, not among the identifiable faculty, and not at the institutional level. The program publishes no eligibility language at all, so there is also no ambiguous wording that might inadvertently exclude a Puerto Rico LCME graduate.

outcomes.selected_examples_vs_complete_cohort: These read as COMPLETE COHORTS rather than curated highlights, for three reasons. First, each graduating year from 2020 through 2026 lists four or five named graduates, matching the program's four-per-year complement. Second, the 2026 class is published in full with every member marked 'Undecided' - a program showcasing selected successes would simply have omitted them. Third, the 2026 graduating class named on the Alumni page reconciles against the independently archived 2026-03-16 PRG-3 roster (Desai, Essa, Kinssies, Lefebvre), i.e. the published list is the actual cohort. One caveat: 'Ajay Sethi, M.D.' appears in BOTH the 2025 and 2026 class lists, and the archived roster supports the 2025 entry being correct, so the 2026 list of five is probably a cohort of four with one duplicate. 18 of roughly 25 graduates with known outcomes across 2020-2025 entered fellowship; 6 entered practice;

named_faculty: Jesse S Cohen, MD (movement disorders, University of Pennsylvania)
Joseph D Legacy, MD (movement disorders and deep-brain stimulation, UF Gainesville)
Kartik Mangipudi, MD (movement disorders and DBS, Mayo Clinic Arizona; Associate Program Director of this residency)
movement_disorders.dedicated_clinic: Movement Disorders and Parkinson's Program at the UF Health Neuroscience Institute at Jacksonville, including a deep brain stimulation program and botulinum toxin treatment for dystonia
movement_disorders.resident_elective: 'Behavioral neurology / Dementia' is a named PGY-4 elective; the Neurodegen/TBI block is a required rotation in all three years (2 weeks PGY-2, 4 weeks PGY-3, 4 weeks PGY-4) rather than an elective
movement_disorders.research: Jesse Cohen publishes neuroimaging work on Lewy body disorders (e.g. Movement Disorders 2025;40(9):1919-1929) and holds an MS in translational research from Penn on cognitive and sleep dysfunction in Parkinson disease. Joseph Legacy's published grant list includes a Phase 2 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled dose-range-finding trial of PRAX-944 in adults with essential tremor. Kartik Mangipudi researches gait and balance in Parkinsonian disorders.
movement_disorders.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: Both are present and they are not the same thing. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY: a named Movement Disorders and Parkinson's Program inside the UF Health Neuroscience Institute, with a DBS programme and neurosurgical options. ACTUAL RESIDENT EXPOSURE: roughly ten weeks of required, calendared outpatient neurodegenerative rotation across PGY-2 to PGY-4, in which the program states residents 'evaluate and treat patients with Parkinson's disease, Parkinsonian syndromes, dystonia and hyperkinetic disorders' with 'exposure to Deep Brain Stimulation and botulinum toxin treatment of dystonia'; movement clinics are also named in the PGY-2 outpatient subspecialty rotation and Movement Disorders is a named didactic block. The strongest downstream proof that the exposure is real rather than nominal is that five graduates across the last six classes matched into movement disorders fellowships. NO formal external designation exists - the Parkinson's Foundation Center of Excellence, the HDSA Huntington's Disease Center of Excellence and the CurePSP Center of Care all belong to the Norman Fixel Institute in Gainesville, a different campus and a different residency's institution, and none is claimed here.
movement_disorders.summary: Three fellowship-trained movement disorders faculty (one of them an Associate Program Director), a DBS and botulinum toxin programme, about ten weeks of required outpatient neurodegenerative rotation across the three years, and movement disorders fellowship placements in five of the last six graduating classes. No in-house fellowship and no formal designation.

named_faculty: Alexander Carvajal Gonzalez, M.D., M.Sc, Ph.D (autoimmune neurology, Harvard; neuroimmunology research fellowship, Johns Hopkins; PhD clinical neurology, Oxford)
William R Frazier, M.D., Ph.D. (neuroimmunology and neurovirology, NINDS/NIH)
Scott L Silliman, M.D. (stroke, cerebrovascular disease and multiple sclerosis; one of two providers NMSS lists at the designated centre)
ms_neuroimmunology.dedicated_clinic: UF Health Jacksonville Comprehensive Multiple Sclerosis Center / Comprehensive Multiple Sclerosis Program, UF Health Neuroscience Institute, 580 W 8th St, Tower I, 9th Floor, Jacksonville, FL 32209 - the same tower and floor as the residency's own department office
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_elective: 'Neuroimmunology' is a named PGY-4 elective. MS and demyelinating exposure is additionally built into the required Neurodegen/TBI rotation in all three years and into the PGY-2 outpatient subspecialty rotation, and 'Neuroimmunology / Multiple Sclerosis' is a named didactic block topic.
ms_neuroimmunology.research: Carvajal Gonzalez conducts translational studies of demyelinating, autoantibody-mediated and related neuroimmunological disorders, including mechanisms of neuroinflammation and biomarkers for diagnosis and treatment response. Frazier's research focuses on improving diagnosis, prognostication and treatment of autoimmune CNS disease and on preventing neuroimmune injury.
ms_neuroimmunology.formal_designation: National MS Society 'Partner in MS Care' AND 'Center for Comprehensive Care', verified on the National MS Society's own Find Doctors & Resources directory. Verbatim from that directory: 'UF Health Jacksonville Comprehensive Multiple Sclerosis Center / 580 W 8th St, Tower I, 9th Floor / Jacksonville, FL 32209 / (904) 633-0411' with badges 'Partner in MS Care' and 'Center for Comprehensive Care'. The designation is a single-site listing at a specific street address, not a multi-site or system-wide award. Corroborated by UF Health Jacksonville's own Awards and Recognition page: 'The Comprehensive Multiple Sclerosis Program at the UF Health Neuroscience Institute was recertified by the National MS Society for offering a multi-disciplinary model of care...'.
ms_neuroimmunology.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: Both are present and separately evidenced. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY is unusually strong for a community-based university-affiliated program: a National MS Society-designated Center for Comprehensive Care, verified against the Society's own directory, physically located in the residency's own building and on its own floor, with two fellowship-trained neuroimmunologists hired in 2025. ACTUAL RESIDENT EXPOSURE is real but narrower than the capability: MS is named among the PGY-2 outpatient subspecialty clinics, demyelinating and autoimmune CNS care is explicitly part of the required Neurodegen/TBI rotation 'under the supervision of our multiple sclerosis attendings', 'Neuroimmunology / Multiple Sclerosis' is a named didactic block, and 'Neuroimmunology' is available as a dedicated PGY-4 elective - but unlike movement disorders there is no separate MS-only block with its own week count, and only one graduate in the last six classes went to an MS fellowship (2025, USC Keck). A resident who wants depth in MS here would need to use elective time deliberately.
ms_neuroimmunology.summary: A National MS Society-designated Center for Comprehensive Care, verified on the Society's own directory at the residency's own address, staffed by two fellowship-trained neuroimmunologists plus Silliman. Residents get MS exposure in a required rotation and can take a dedicated neuroimmunology elective. No in-house MS fellowship.

research_opportunities: A block-scheduled three-year curriculum with heavy stroke and neurocritical care volume, a dedicated outpatient neurodegenerative rotation in all three years, 40 half-days of continuity clinic per year, 21 weeks of elective time, and chief-resident roles in PGY-4.

salary_benefits.summary: Stipends run $69,444 / $71,841 / $74,765 across the three program years, with 15 vacation and 10 sick days, fully institution-paid medical, mental-health, life and disability coverage, free covered parking, and free lodging on the Gainesville pediatric rotation. Dental is available but not employer-paid.

differentiators.title: Three fellowship-trained movement disorders faculty for a four-per-year program
differentiators.student_explanation: Jesse Cohen (movement disorders, University of Pennsylvania), Joseph Legacy (movement disorders and deep-brain stimulation, UF Gainesville) and Kartik Mangipudi (movement disorders and DBS, Mayo Clinic Arizona) all practise here. Mangipudi is also an Associate Program Director, so a movement specialist sits in program leadership and on your interview panel.

differentiators.title: A calendared outpatient movement and demyelinating rotation in all three years, not an elective you have to fight for
differentiators.student_explanation: The Neurodegen/TBI block appears in every year of the published block schedule - 2 weeks in PGY-2, 4 weeks in PGY-3 and 4 weeks in PGY-4. The program states you will 'evaluate and treat patients with Parkinson's disease, Parkinsonian syndromes, dystonia and hyperkinetic disorders' and get 'exposure to Deep Brain Stimulation and botulinum toxin treatment of dystonia', plus MS and autoimmune CNS care under the MS attendings in the same rotation.

differentiators.title: Movement disorders fellowship placements in five of the last six graduating classes
differentiators.student_explanation: The program's own alumni list shows graduates going to movement disorders fellowships at the University of Washington, Medical College of Georgia, The Queen's Medical Center in Honolulu, Emory and OHSU between 2021 and 2025. For a program graduating four people a year, that is an unusually dense track record into the exact fellowship you want.

differentiators.title: A National MS Society Center for Comprehensive Care in the same building and on the same floor as the residency office
differentiators.student_explanation: The National MS Society's own provider directory lists the UF Health Jacksonville Comprehensive Multiple Sclerosis Center at 580 W 8th St, Tower I, 9th Floor with both a 'Partner in MS Care' and a 'Center for Comprehensive Care' designation. That address is the residency's own department address, so the designated centre is not a separate campus you visit - it is where you work.

differentiators.title: Two neuroimmunologists trained at Harvard and the NIH, both hired in 2025
differentiators.student_explanation: Alexander Carvajal Gonzalez did autoimmune neurology subspecialty training at Harvard, a neuroimmunology research fellowship at Johns Hopkins and a PhD in clinical neurology at Oxford. William Frazier did neuroimmunology and neurovirology fellowship training at NINDS/NIH. Both joined in 2025, so the MS and neuroimmunology side of the department is actively being built out, and 'Neuroimmunology' is a named senior elective.

differentiators.title: A December 31 application deadline, which is unusually late
differentiators.student_explanation: The program states 'The deadline for submitting your completed application is Dec. 31.' Most programs close far earlier. If any part of your file - a Step 2 CK score, a letter - lands in October or November, this program is still open and still reviewing.

differentiators.title: A guaranteed preliminary PGY-1 year on the same campus, with no separate interview
differentiators.student_explanation: Because this is an advanced program you must also match a PGY-1 year. The program states 'We are an advanced program but do not require a separate interview for the preliminary PGY-1 internal medicine position' and 'Applicants who MATCH with our program are also guaranteed a PGY-1 position in internal medicine if they elect to conduct their preliminary year on our campus.' NRMP data confirm the paired Med-Prelim/Neurology track (code 1101140P1) matched 4 of 4 in 2026. That removes most of the usual risk and extra interviewing burden of an advanced program.

differentiators.title: A program director who trained in this program and has won five teaching awards
differentiators.student_explanation: Shannon LaBoy completed this very residency, returned as faculty, and has been program director since 2021 while also serving as neurology clerkship director. Her published awards include Exemplary Teacher in 2024 and 2021, a departmental Golden Apple Award in 2024, and Excellence in Student Education in 2018. Education is visibly her job, not a side duty.

differentiators.title: High-acuity stroke volume through a Level I trauma centre, a mobile stroke unit and a DNV Comprehensive Stroke Center
differentiators.student_explanation: UF Health Jacksonville is the only Level I trauma centre in Northeast Florida and Southeast Georgia, runs a Mobile Stroke Treatment Unit and telestroke service, and draws stroke patients by TraumaOne helicopter from a 12-county area. DNV Healthcare recertified the downtown programme as a Comprehensive Stroke Center in December 2025. You spend 12 weeks on the vascular service in PGY-2 alone and help manage thrombolysis and thrombectomy decisions in the ED.

differentiators.title: A required research rotation with sub-investigator roles on real trials, including a movement disorders trial
differentiators.student_explanation: The research rotation is required, and the program states residents 'participate, as sub-investigators, in departmental clinical trials' with on-campus biostatistics support. One movement faculty member's published grant list includes a Phase 2 randomised placebo-controlled trial of PRAX-944 in essential tremor, so there is an active movement-disorders trial you could plausibly join.

differentiators.title: The only in-house neurology fellowship takes its own graduates
differentiators.student_explanation: Vascular Neurology is the institution's single neurology fellowship, currently with three fellows. Two recent graduates of this residency went straight into it, and one of them, Yessenia Marquez, is now on the faculty. It is a genuine internal pathway rather than a nominal one.

differentiators.title: Documented graduate placements into Houston teaching hospitals
differentiators.student_explanation: Two 2020 graduates went to UTHealth Houston - one for vascular neurology and one for neurocritical care. This is a factual placement record, not a claim about convenience: Jacksonville is roughly 860 road miles from Houston and any visit is a flight.

spanish_latino.summary: The residency has no Medical Spanish curriculum and no faculty member documents Spanish-language ability. What does exist is institution-level: UF Health Jacksonville is the city's only safety-net hospital and staffs three certified Spanish interpreters plus remote interpreting, in the same buildings where residents train.
spanish_latino.explicitly_rejected_evidence: I refused to count, and name here so the refusals are auditable: (1) DUVAL COUNTY / JACKSONVILLE DEMOGRAPHICS. I did not look up and would not have counted the Hispanic or Latino share of Duval County's population, the Jacksonville metro, or Florida. City and county demographics are not program-level evidence and the contract forbids them outright. (2) ANY SURNAME. Several faculty and residents have surnames that a careless reader might treat as evidence of Spanish fluency or Latino identity - the program director's own name among them. No inference of language, ethnicity, nationality or immigration status was drawn from any name, in either direction. Alexander Carvajal Gonzalez's medical degree from Universidad Nacional de Colombia is reported as an institutional fact about the school he attended; it was NOT converted into a claim that he speaks Spanish or provides Spanish-language care, because no source says so. (3) THE PROGRAM'S OWN 'DIVERSE POPULATION' LANGUAGE. FREIDA's special features say 'we serve a diverse population' and the residency landing page advertises 'a diverse, competency-based curriculum'. Generic diversity language is explicitly not evidence of Spanish or Latino clinical relevance and was discarded. (4) A HISPANIC HERITAGE MONTH ARTICLE'S NAMED SPANISH SPEAKERS. The UF Health Jacksonville language-barriers article was published during Hispanic Heritage Month and names two bilingual staff - Gladys Bruno, a certified diabetes education specialist, and Kathy Hudson, a registered nurse in the pediatric emergency room. Neither is neurology faculty, neither is a resident, and neither belongs to this training program; I recorded the interpreter infrastructure from that article but did not attribute those individuals' Spanish fluency to the neurology residency. (5) SPANISH-LANGUAGE CAPACITY AT ANY OTHER UF HEALTH SITE. ufhealth.org spans both the Jacksonville and Gainesville campuses. Any Spanish or language-program content I encountered was checked for the Jacksonville campus marker before use, and nothing from the Gainesville campus was counted. (6) INTERPRETER SERVICES AS A SPANISH CURRICULUM. Interpreter availability is logged under its own permitted evidence type and was never upgraded into FORMAL_MEDICAL_SPANISH or SPANISH_CLINICAL_SERVICE.

ucc_puerto_rico.summary: No Universidad Central del Caribe or Puerto Rico connection was found anywhere in this program - no residents, no graduates, no fellows, no faculty and no leadership. Two faculty are offshore Caribbean graduates, which is a different category entirely.
